test_endpoint.articlesName: U.S. Supreme Court backs Facebook in case about unwanted texting
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: The U.S. Supreme Court on Thursday made it easier for businesses to pester consumers with phone calls or text messages by tossing out a lawsuit accusing Facebook Inc (FB.O) of violating a federal anti-robocall law.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"The U.S. Supreme Court on Thursday made it easier for businesses to pester consumers with phone calls or text messages by tossing out a lawsuit accusing Facebook Inc <a href=\"https:\/\/www.reuters.com\/companies\/FB.O\" target=\"_blank\">(FB.O) of violating a federal anti-robocall law."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The justices, in a 9-0 decision authored by Justice Sonia Sotomayor, sided with Facebook over its argument that text messages the social media company sent did not violate a 1991 federal law called the Telephone Consumer Protection Act (TCPA)."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The case highlighted the challenge for the justices in applying outdated laws to modern technologies. The ruling sparked calls for the U.S. Congress to update the law, enacted three decades ago to curb telemarketing abuse by banning most unauthorized robocalls."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"\"By narrowing the scope of the TCPA, the court is allowing companies the ability to assault the public with a non-stop wave of unwanted calls and texts, around the clock,\" Democratic Senator Edward Markey and Democratic Representative Anna Eshoo said in a joint statement."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The court ruled that Facebook's actions - sending text messages without consent - did not fit within the technical definition of the type of conduct barred by the law, which was enacted before the rise of modern cellphone technology."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The lawsuit was filed in 2015 in California federal court by Montana resident Noah Duguid, who said Facebook sent him many automatic text messages without his consent. The lawsuit accused Menlo Park, California-based Facebook of violating the Telephone Consumer Protection Act's restriction on using an automatic telephone dialing system."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Facebook said the security-related messages, triggered when users try to log in to their accounts from a new device or internet browser, were tied to users' cellphone numbers."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"\"As the court recognized, the law's provisions were never intended to prohibit companies from sending targeted security notifications and the court's decision will allow companies to continue working to keep the accounts of their users safe,\" Facebook said in a statement."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Sergei Lemberg, Duguid's lawyer, said anyone could steer clear of liability under the law as long as they use similar technology to Facebook's."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"\"This is a disappointing ruling for anyone who owns a cellphone or values their privacy,\" Lemberg added."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In this instance, the lawsuit asserted that Facebook's system that sent automated text messages was akin to a traditional automatic dialing system - known as an autodialer - used to send robocalls."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"\"Duguid's quarrel is with Congress, which did not define an autodialer as malleably as he would have liked,\" Sotomayor wrote in the ruling."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The law requires that the equipment used must use a \"random or sequential number generator\" but the court concluded that Facebook's system \"does not use such technology,\" Sotomayor added."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Duguid said that Facebook repeatedly sent him account login notifications by text message to his cellphone even though he was not a Facebook user and never had been. Despite numerous efforts, Duguid said he was unable to stop Facebook from \"robotexting\" him."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Facebook responded that Duguid had most likely been assigned a phone number that had been previously associated with a Facebook user who had opted in to receive the notifications."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"A federal judge threw out the lawsuit but in 2019 the San Francisco-based 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals revived it. The 9th Circuit took a broad view of the law, saying it not only bans devices that automatically dial randomly generated numbers but also stored numbers that are not randomly generated."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The National Association of Federally-Insured Credit Unions said the decision \"to narrowly interpret autodialers is a win for the credit union industry.\""},{"type":"paragraph","content":"\"We have long fought for this clarity to ensure credit unions can contact their members with important, time-sensitive financial information without fear of violating the TCPA and facing frivolous lawsuits,\" the association said in a statement."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Moody's lifts Portuguese banks' outlook on economic recovery prospects
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Rating agency Moody's upgraded the credit outlook for Portugal's banks to stable from negative on Thursday citing prospects of economic recovery after 2020's steep pandemic-induced slump, even as it expected their asset quality to deteriorate.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"LISBON, April 1 Rating agency Moody’s upgraded the credit outlook for Portugal’s banks to stable from negative on Thursday citing prospects of economic recovery after 2020’s steep pandemic-induced slump, even as it expected their asset quality to deteriorate."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Portugal’s tourism-dependent economy shrank 7.6% in 2020 in its worst contraction since the 1930s. Moody’s pointed to expectations of 3.7% and 4% growth in 2021 and 2022, respectively."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Moody’s said banks’ capital position was expected to hold steady, suffering “little change” over the outlook period and lenders would, for the most part, be able to avoid losses that could hurt capital."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"However, it expected “an increase in Portuguese banks’ problem loans this year as government support measures that protected their asset quality in 2020 start to wind down”, while provisions set aside last year were unlikely to offset an expected deterioration."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Portuguese banks have suspended over 45 billion euros worth of loan repayments under a scheme to help businesses and individuals through the pandemic, but also to avoid a jump in bad loans."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The freeze will end on Sept. 30. Some loans, namely mortgage loans, will start paying interest as of April. (Reporting by Catarina Demony; Editing by Andrei Khalip and David Evans)"}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: India central bank orders MobiKwik to probe alleged data leak -source
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: India's central bank has ordered digital payments firm MobiKwik to probe allegations that data of its 110 million users was breached, and warned that the company will face fines if lapses are found, a source with direct knowledge of the situation told Reuters on Thursday.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"India's central bank has ordered digital payments firm MobiKwik to probe allegations that data of its 110 million users was breached, and warned that the company will face fines if lapses are found, a source with direct knowledge of the situation told Reuters on Thursday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"MobiKwik, which is backed by Sequoia Capital and India's Bajaj Finance <a href=\"https:\/\/www.reuters.com\/companies\/BJFN.NS\" target=\"_blank\">(BJFN.NS), has faced growing criticism this week for denying a leak many customers and digital rights activists say is linked to the company's database."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) was \"not happy\" with the company's initial response and has asked it to act immediately, said the source, who declined to be named as the discussion between the RBI and the company was private."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The payments firm has also faced backlash for threatening legal action against a security researcher who first flagged the breach. "},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Several users said this week they had found information such as their credit card details on a leaked online database that allegedly belonged to MobiKwik, a claim the company has denied."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"\"The RBI has given MobiKwik an ultimatum and ordered them to retain an external auditor to conduct a forensic audit,\" said the person, adding the RBI could also impose fines if the breach is proven."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The RBI did not respond to a request for comment."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The central bank has the power to fine a payment systems provider a minimum of 500,000 rupees ($6,811) in such cases."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"MobiKwik did not respond to a request for comment and messages sent to its founders went unanswered."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"It has previously said users could have uploaded their data on several platforms and it was incorrect to say the leaked information was accessed from the payments company, adding it takes privacy and security very seriously."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"With 120 million users, MobiKwik competes in India with firms like Alibaba-backed Paytm and Google's payments service, which have witnessed a rapid surge in usage. But data breaches and leaks have also become common in the country."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"On Wednesday, New Delhi-based digital rights group the Internet Freedom Foundation (IFF) asked India's country's cyber security agency to probe the alleged data breach. The federal agency did not respond to Reuters queries."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Mastercard to invest $100 mln in Airtel Africa's mobile money unit
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Global payment processor Mastercard Inc (MA.N) will invest $100 million in Airtel Africa's (AAF.L) mobile money operations, valuing the business at $2.65 billion, the London-listed company said on Thursday.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"Global payment processor Mastercard Inc <a href=\"https:\/\/www.reuters.com\/companies\/MA.N\" target=\"_blank\">(MA.N) will invest $100 million in Airtel Africa's <a href=\"https:\/\/www.reuters.com\/companies\/AAF.L\" target=\"_blank\">(AAF.L) mobile money operations, valuing the business at $2.65 billion, the London-listed company said on Thursday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Airtel Africa is targeting a public listing of Airtel Mobile Commerce BV (AMC BV) within the next four years. Earlier this month, private equity firm TPG's The Rise Fund invested $200 million in AMC BV."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Mastercard will hold a minority stake in AMC BV, in line with Airtel Africa's plan to monetise the mobile money business by selling up to a 25% stake in the unit, the company said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The unit, operating under the Airtel Money brand in Africa, includes mobile wallets, merchant and commercial payments, virtual credit card and international money transfers available across 14 countries in the region."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Airtel Africa, which offers Airtel Money in Nigeria in partnership with a local bank, said it aims to have all mobile money operations to be owned and operated by AMC BV."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Swiss robots use UV light to zap viruses aboard passenger planes
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: A robot armed with virus-killing ultraviolet light is being tested on Swiss airplanes, yet another idea aiming to restore passenger confidence and spare the travel industry more pandemic pain.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"A robot armed with virus-killing ultraviolet light is being tested on Swiss airplanes, yet another idea aiming to restore passenger confidence and spare the travel industry more pandemic pain."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"UVeya, a Swiss start-up, is conducting the trials of the robots with Dubai-based airport services company Dnata inside Embraer <a href=\"https:\/\/www.reuters.com\/companies\/EMBR3.SA\" target=\"_blank\">(EMBR3.SA) jets from Helvetic Airways, a charter airline owned by Swiss billionaire Martin Ebner."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Aircraft makers still must certify the devices and are studying the impact their UV light may have on interior upholstery, which could fade after many disinfections, UVeya co-founder Jodoc Elmiger said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Still, he's hopeful robot cleaners could reduce people's fear of flying, even as COVID-19 circulates."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"\"This is a proven technology, it's been used for over 50 years in hospitals and laboratories, it's very efficient,\" Elmiger said on Wednesday. \"It doesn't leave any trace or residue.\""},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Elmiger's team has built three prototypes so far, one of which he demonstrated inside a Helvetic jet at the Zurich Airport, where traffic plunged 75% last year."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The robot's lights, mounted on a crucifix-shaped frame, cast everything in a soft-blue glow as it slowly moved up the Embraer's aisle. One robot can disinfect a single-aisled plane in 13 minutes, start to finish, though larger planes take longer."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Dnata executives hope airplane makers will sign off on the robots -- Elmiger estimates they'll sell for 15,000 Swiss francs  ($15,930) or so -- as governments require new measures to ensure air travellers don't get sick."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"\"We were looking for a sustainable, and also environmentally friendly solution, to cope with those requests,\" said Lukas Gyger, Dnata's chief operating officer in Switzerland."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"While privately owned Helvetic has not needed bailouts like much of the industry, its business has also been gutted, with its fleet sitting largely silently in hangars. UVeya's UV robots may help change that, said Mehdi Guenin, a Helvetic spokesman."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"\"If our passengers, if our crew know our aircraft are safe -- that there are no viruses or bacteria -- it could help them to fly again,\" Guenin said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"($1 = 0.9418 Swiss francs)"}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Deutsche Telekom eyes direct control over T-Mobile in medium term
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Deutsche Telekom (DTEGn.DE) expects to secure direct ownership of T-Mobile (TMUS.O) in the medium term, funded by a significant capital return to shareholders by its U.S. business, CEO Tim Hoettges told shareholders on Thursday.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"Deutsche Telekom <a href=\"https:\/\/www.reuters.com\/companies\/DTEGn.DE\" target=\"_blank\">(DTEGn.DE) expects to secure direct ownership of T-Mobile <a href=\"https:\/\/www.reuters.com\/companies\/TMUS.O\" target=\"_blank\">(TMUS.O) in the medium term, funded by a significant capital return to shareholders by its U.S. business, CEO Tim Hoettges told shareholders on Thursday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Addressing the telecoms group's annual general meeting, Hoettges said he expected T-Mobile to return up to $60 billion to shareholders between 2023 and 2025."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"With its share of the proceeds, Deutsche Telekom would be able to raise its holding in T-Mobile to more than 50% from 43% at a price below current market levels secured with options, he added. "},{"type":"paragraph","content":"\"It's harvest time,\" said Hoettges."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"He said that the first task will be to reduce group debt of about 120 billion euros ($141 billion), which had increased as a result of T-Mobile's takeover of smaller rival Sprint a year ago. test_endpoint.articlesName: Germany awards second round of permits to close hard coal plants
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: More than 1,500 megawatts (MW) of coal-fired generation will be shut from Dec. 8 this year, Germany's energy regulator said on Thursday, announcing the results of a second round of auctions designed to cushion the cost of closing polluting plants.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"More than 1,500 megawatts (MW) of coal-fired generation will be shut from Dec. 8 this year, Germany's energy regulator said on Thursday, announcing the results of a second round of auctions designed to cushion the cost of closing polluting plants."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Germany has promised to abandon coal by 2038 and achieve a mostly carbon-free energy system by 2050, but it is also trying to lessen the impact on utilities, regions, employment and the public budget. "},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Under a series of tenders between 2020 and 2027, operators are asked to declare at which price they would be prepared to shut their plants that use hard coal in return for funds to offset some of their losses."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The regulator sets a maximum price per MW of capacity to cap the public sector bill. The ultimate price takes into account bidders' offers and the CO2 emissions of the plants in question."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The 1,514 MW to go offline in December are Uniper's <a href=\"https:\/\/www.reuters.com\/companies\/UN01.DE\" target=\"_blank\">(UN01.DE) 757 MW Wilhelmshaven plant on Germany's North Sea coast and Czech operator EPH's Mehrum and Deuben power plants of 690 MW and 67 MW respectively."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"After 2027, compensation will no longer be available, so operators are ready to bid as low as possible to avoid losing out to competitors."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"\"The auction was again oversubscribed,\" Jochen Homann, the head of the Bundesnetzagentur regulator, said. \"The highest award lies significantly below the previously set maximum price.\""},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In all, the successful bidders will receive between zero and 59,000 euros per MW, the regulator said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"This was what they had offered to close their plants for, after the regulator set a maximum price of 155,000 euros\/MW."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Bidding for the third auction for the closure of 2,481 MW by the end of 2022 will close on April 30."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Following a first auction, the regulator closed 4,788 MW of coal-fired capacity on Jan 1, 2021. "},{"type":"paragraph","content":"More highly polluting brown coal is being shut down via a separate scheme with fixed compensation."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Coal India annual production drops for second straight year
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Coal India Ltd, the world's largest coal miner, said on Thursday its annual production fell for the second straight year, as lower electricity consumption due to coronavirus-induced lockdowns hurt fuel demand.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"CHENNAI, April 1 Coal India Ltd, the world’s largest coal miner, said on Thursday its annual production fell for the second straight year, as lower electricity consumption due to coronavirus-induced lockdowns hurt fuel demand."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The state-run miner produced 596.2 million tonnes of coal for the year ended March 31, compared with 602.1 million tonnes last year. Coal sales fell 1.3% to 573.8 million tonnes, the company said in a statement."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Primarily, what hurt Coal India’s supplies was reduced coal lifting by the power Sector,” the miner said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"A lack of supplies has led to an inventory of 99 million tonnes, rising by about 25% from the same period last year, it added."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“With the expected demand revival during summer months of Q1, the company has sufficient buffer to meet any surge and the stocks would be reduced substantially.” (Reporting by Sudarshan Varadhan; Editing by Rashmi Aich)"}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Swiss volumes help London catch up with Amsterdam in share trading
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: The City of London has almost closed the share trading gap with Amsterdam since dealings in Swiss shares resumed in the UK capital following Brexit, figures from Cboe exchange showed on Thursday.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"LONDON The City of London has almost closed the share trading gap with Amsterdam since dealings in Swiss shares resumed in the UK capital following Brexit, figures from Cboe exchange showed on Thursday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Amsterdam took the European top spot in share trading from London in January after roughly 8 billion euros ($9.39 billion) a day left for the Dutch capital."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"It was the first tangible sign of how Britain’s full departure from the European Union on Dec. 31 will impact the City as the follow-up EU-UK trade deal does not cover finance."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In January, the average daily value of shares traded in Amsterdam was 9.22 billion euros, with 8.62 billion euros in London and 6.06 billion euros in Paris, Cboe said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In March, Amsterdam traded 10.68 billion euros, just ahead of 10.62 billion euros in London, and 6.74 billion in Frankfurt, which has pushed Paris, at 6.44 billion, into fourth place, Cboe said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The European Commission had stopped EU investors from trading on Swiss exchanges in June 2019 after a treaty dispute. Switzerland then banned EU exchanges from trading Swiss shares."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Brexit meant that Britain no longer had to comply with such EU decisions and Swiss share trading resumed in London in early February. Before the ban, London handled around 1.2 billion euros daily in Swiss shares."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The shift in euro share trading was expected. Chunks of euro derivatives trading have also left for Amsterdam, and a billion euros in daily EU emission allowance contracts will follow on June 7."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Former EU financial services commissioner Jonathan Hill has said the move in share trading had “crystallised” minds that direct City access to the EU was unlikely. He said it was better to focus on making the UK globally competitive in finance. [L8N2LN73A]"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“The worst possible thing you can do is just sit there and hope the Europeans will come to our rescue,” Hill said last week."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"After agreeing a regulatory cooperation pact with London last week, Brussels has said it was in “no rush” to grant the City direct access to the 27-nation bloc."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"($1 = 0.8520 euros)"}]

test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Delivery app Glovo said on Thursday it had raised an additional 450 million euros ($528 million), calling it the largest financing round secured by a Spanish start-up.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"Delivery app Glovo said on Thursday it had raised an additional 450 million euros ($528 million), calling it the largest financing round secured by a Spanish start-up."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Glovo, based in Barcelona, has seen demand soar during the COVID-19 pandemic, as locked-down customers turned to its quick delivery service that provides everything from food to toiletries. It currently has some 10 million users."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Glovo said it would use the funds to expand further in the 20 markets where it operates. It will also focus on its Q-commerce division as part of a goal of growing ultra-fast deliveries across the 850 cities where the app operates."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"So-called quick commerce has boomed in the past year as the pandemic put a new premium on ultra-rapid deliveries of food and goods from relatively local stockrooms."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Investors have rushed to get in on the action of delivery apps, but the much-anticipated IPO of Deliveroo <a href=\"https:\/\/www.reuters.com\/companies\/ROO.L\" target=\"_blank\">(ROO.L) on the London Stock Exchange on Wednesday saw shares in the British delivery company plunge by as much as 30%, cutting more than 2 billion pounds off the company's valuation. <a href=\"\/business\/deliveroo-shares-plunge-30-london-debut-2021-03-31\/\"> read more "},{"type":"paragraph","content":"\"This investment will allow us to grow in our core markets, accelerate our leadership position in places where we are already very strong, continue to expand our Q-commerce division and bring more innovation to our multi-category offering,\" Glovo CEO Oscar Pierre said in a statement."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Glovo raised the latest investment in a new round of Series F financing led by New York-based Lugard Road Capital and Luxor Capital Group. Delivery Hero <a href=\"https:\/\/www.reuters.com\/companies\/DHER.DE\" target=\"_blank\">(DHER.DE), Drake Enterprises and GP Bullhound also participated in the round. All are previous investors in Glovo."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The company did not give a valuation for the business but Spanish financial newspaper Expansion cited a figure of 2 billion euros."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"($1 = 0.8525 euros)"}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: White House will seek law to require carbon-free power from U.S. utilities
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: The Biden administration said on Thursday it will seek to pass a law requiring utilities to source more power from renewable and other clean sources as part of an ambitious effort to address climate change through investing in infrastructure.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Biden administration said on Thursday it will seek to pass a law requiring utilities to source more power from renewable and other clean sources as part of an ambitious effort to address climate change through investing in infrastructure."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"A so-called clean energy standard (CES) would help put the United States on a path to delivering on President Joe Biden's campaign promise to decarbonize the nation's electricity sector by 2035, and the whole economy by 2050."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Nuclear energy and carbon capture and storage technologies would be included in the policy, Gina McCarthy, White House national climate adviser, said during a briefing with reporters."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"\"We're interested in pursuing this and talking to Congress about it,\" McCarthy said. \"The industry itself sees it as one of the most flexible and most effective tools.\""},{"type":"paragraph","content":"McCarthy's remarks came a day after Biden unveiled a $2 trillion plan to reshape the world's largest economy and counter China's rise. Much of the proposal was aimed at mitigating climate change through investing in clean energy technologies that could create union-represented jobs."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The administration did not give details on how it would seek to structure a national clean energy standard."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Democrats in Congress last month introduced a bill that would require 80% of retail power sales to come from sources that produce little or no carbon emissions by 2030, rising to 100% by 2035. Some Republicans have said the legislation would raise energy prices and destabilize the grid."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The federal government has lagged many states in developing policies requiring clean power sources. Most U.S. states have already set such goals, though fewer than 10 have set goals to move entirely away from fossil fuels and none would achieve net-zero emissions by 2035."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Many of the nation's biggest utilities, responding to investor pressure or state-mandated targets, have already pledged to eliminate all of their carbon emissions by 2050, with a few promising earlier timelines."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"But the industry has said that rapid advances in technologies like batteries, carbon capture and advanced nuclear will be critical to reaching those goals."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Pandemic slowdown led to record fall in EU carbon market emissions
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Emissions regulated by Europe's carbon market fell by 14.4% in 2020, their biggest percentage decline yet, as pandemic restrictions stifled economic activity and grounded flights, official data examined by carbon analysts at Refinitiv showed.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"Emissions regulated by Europe's carbon market fell by 14.4% in 2020, their biggest percentage decline yet, as pandemic restrictions stifled economic activity and grounded flights, official data examined by carbon analysts at Refinitiv showed."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Around 45% of the European Union's output of greenhouse gases is regulated by the Emissions Trading System (ETS), the bloc's flagship instrument to tackle global warming by charging for the right to emit carbon dioxide (CO2)."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Refinitiv analysts' interpretation of European Commission data found emissions covered by the ETS totalled 1.365 billion tonnes of CO2 equivalent (CO2e), down 14.4% on the previous year."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The fall was the largest in percentage terms since the market was launched in 2005."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The market does not cover emissions from agriculture or transport beyond the aviation sector."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"\"The substantial drop in emissions is the fallout from the pandemic with economic activity shrinking last year and renewables displacing fossil-fired power,\" Refinitiv analyst Ingvild Sorhus said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"With international travel restricted, aviation sector emissions dived 58.4% to 25.8 million tonnes CO2e."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"After aviation, the heat and power sector, whose emissions totalled 632.8 million tonnes of CO2e, down 17.1% on 2019, registered the next steepest fall."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Stationary emissions covered by the scheme, such as from power plants and factories, totalled 1.339 billion tonnes of CO2e, down 12.6% on the previous year, the data showed."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The figures were in line with analysts forecasts and the benchmark price of carbon permits in the ETS was little changed on Thursday at around 42.50 euros a tonne."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Carbon prices have been rising since the European Union agreed last year to toughen its climate targets, which will increase demand for permits to emit, and hit a record high of 43.77 euros\/tonne last month. <a href=\"\/business\/energy\/eu-price-pollution-hits-record-high-early-2021-2021-01-05\/\"> read more "}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: FiberCop goes live as Italy strives to close digital divide
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: FiberCop, created to manage Telecom Italia's (TIM) 'last mile' grid and open it up to other operators, became fully operational on Thursday, as the country's biggest phone group leads efforts to close a digital divide with the rest of Europe.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"MILAN, April 1 FiberCop, created to manage Telecom Italia’s (TIM) ‘last mile’ grid and open it up to other operators, became fully operational on Thursday, as the country’s biggest phone group leads efforts to close a digital divide with the rest of Europe."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In 2019, Italy ranked 24 out of 28 European Union member states in its take-up of ultrafast internet of at least 100 megabytes, the Digital Economy and Society Index (DESI) found."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"FiberCop, into which TIM transferred its copper last mile network connecting street cabinets to people’s homes and also the fiber assets from a joint venture with Fastweb, is meant to help facilitate a switch to fast fibre connectivity."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"It went live on Thursday after U.S. infrastructure fund KKR finalised its acquisition of 37.5% of FiberCop from TIM for 1.8 billion euros ($2.11 billion), TIM, Fastweb and KKR said in a joint statement."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In addition, Swisscom unit Fastweb underwrote FiberCop shares worth 4.5% by transferring the 20% it held in FlashFiber, a fibre network joint venture with TIM, into FiberCop."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"FiberCop will not require capital injections from shareholders, the companies said, adding it was expected to reach earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) of 0.9 billion euros on a full-year basis."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Massimo Sarmi, formerly a CEO at Poste Italiane, will be chairman at FiberCop and Carlo Filangieri, a long-term TIM manager, will be CEO."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Its aim is to ensure connection speeds of up to 1 gigabite for 76% of properties in the so-called grey and black areas of Italy by 2025, the companies said. Those mainly cover large cities and small towns and exclude non-economically viable areas."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The new company is a first step towards a government plan to create a single network by merging FiberCop into state-backed Open Fiber."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Open Fiber is a wholesale-only ultra-broadband jointly owned by Italy’s biggest utility Enel and state lender Cassa Depositi e Prestiti (CDP)."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"But the plans for a single operator have yet to be finalised, with questions around governance seen as one of the hurdles."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Sources told Reuters on Wednesday Italy was considering a new scheme to win control of Open Fiber."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Under Prime Minister Mario Draghi, who took office this year, Italy’s government has put digital infrastructure at the heart of the agenda, but some of his ministers have cast doubt on the project for a single network."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Boat carries 1,200 survivors from Mozambique militant attack to safety
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: A boat carrying 1,200 survivors of a deadly attack by Islamic State-linked insurgents in northern Mozambique reached safety in the port of Pemba on Thursday, some of them crying on arrival after spending days hiding in the bush.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"A boat carrying 1,200 survivors of a deadly attack by Islamic State-linked insurgents in northern Mozambique reached safety in the port of Pemba on Thursday, some of them crying on arrival after spending days hiding in the bush."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Aid workers were at the crowded port to give food to those disembarking from the green and white ferry, while police and soldiers kept control of crowds of people excited to see relatives rescued during the attack that began last week in Palma, a Reuters reporter at the port said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Many people were believed to have scattered into dense forest or to have attempted to escape by boat, aid workers said. <a href=\"\/world\/europe\/tens-thousands-feared-displaced-deadly-attack-mozambique-gas-town-2021-03-30\/\"> read more "},{"type":"paragraph","content":"An emotional Mariamo Tagir, who arrived on the ferry, told Reuters TV that she had spent seven days in the bush, crying every day."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"\"I don't know where my son is. It's very painful,\" said Tagir. \"The situation is really bad, many dead.\""},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Islamist insurgents have been increasingly active in the surrounding province of Cabo Delgado since 2017, although it is unclear whether they have a unified aim or what specifically they are fighting for."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The district where Palma is located is adjacent to natural gas projects worth $60 billion. It is home to around 110,000 people according to United Nations estimates, of whom more than 40,000 sought shelter there after fleeing attacks elsewhere."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"THOUSANDS DISPLACED"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Mozambique's government has confirmed dozens of deaths in Palma, including at least seven killed when militants ambushed vehicles trying to escape the Amarula Hotel. One South African is confirmed to have died as a result."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"British national Philip Mawer, who has been missing since the attack, was likely also killed in the incident, his employer RA International <a href=\"https:\/\/www.reuters.com\/companies\/RAI.L\" target=\"_blank\">(RAI.L) said in a statement on behalf of his family, adding a body matching his description had been recovered but not formally identified."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"\"The family is devastated by the loss,\" the statement said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Military operations were ongoing on Wednesday, according to footage shot by local news station TVM, which showed soldiers carrying rocket-propelled grenades and guns in the area, as well as reinforcements arriving by helicopter."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"\"I can't right now say we have the whole village under control,\" army spokesman Chongo Vidigal said in the footage, adding however security forces did have a presence in the port area."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Portugal, meanwhile, was reportedly ready to send 60 soldiers to help train armed forces in Cabo Delgado. <a href=\"\/world\/europe\/tens-thousands-feared-displaced-deadly-attack-mozambique-gas-town-2021-03-30\/\"> read more "},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Reuters has not been able to independently verify the accounts from the town. Most means of communication were cut off after the attack began on March 24. Phone calls to Mozambique's government and security officials went unanswered on Thursday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Aid groups believe the attack has displaced tens of thousands of people. Hundreds, including many foreign workers, have been evacuated by air. <a href=\"\/world\/europe\/thousands-find-refuge-after-insurgent-attack-mozambique-gas-town-2021-03-31\/\"> read more "},{"type":"paragraph","content":"As of Wednesday afternoon, a U.N. migration agency tracker showed more than 8,100 people had been displaced, almost half of them children. Roughly 20% had arrived in Pemba, with others turning up in the districts of Mueda, Montepuez and Nangade in Cabo Delgado."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"However, the full scale of the casualties and displacement remains unclear."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The ferry - organised by French energy major Total <a href=\"https:\/\/www.reuters.com\/companies\/TOTF.PA\" target=\"_blank\">(TOTF.PA) in coordination with the Mozambican government and the United Nations - docked at around 8 a.m. local time (0600 GMT) in Pemba, the provincial capital of Cabo Delgado."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Total, which has a gas project on the Afungi Peninsula near Palma, said in a statement that there were almost 1,200 passengers on board, mainly women and children."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"A humanitarian official said the government was screening those arriving at Pemba to prevent infiltration by armed groups."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Nord Stream 2 warns of security risks to pipeline from warships, planes
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: The consortium behind the construction of the Nord Stream 2 gas pipeline warned on Thursday about security risks to the project from warships and planes, as the link is nearing completion.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"The consortium behind the construction of the Nord Stream 2 gas pipeline warned on Thursday about security risks to the project from warships and planes, as the link is nearing completion."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The pipeline, aimed at bypassing Ukraine and doubling the capacity of the current Nord Stream undersea gas link from Russia to Germany, has been the focus of tensions between Moscow and Washington, which imposed sanctions against the project."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Andrey Minin, a senior official at the Nord Stream 2 AG consortium, told Interfax news agency that the project's fleet has been the target of \"regular provocations by the foreign civil and military vessels\"."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In an emailed comments to Reuters, Nord Stream 2 AG said it could confirm Minin's statement, which \"underlines the necessity to abide by the requirements of marine security\"."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"According to Interfax, Minin said an unidentified submarine had emerged near the pipe-laying vessel Fortuna on March 28 less than a mile away."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"He also cited several incidents with other vessels and said that the number of cases of low-flying \"foreign planes\" over the Nord Stream 2's vessels has increased in the second half of March."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"U.S. Secretary of State Antony Blinken said in an interview broadcast on Sunday that it was ultimately up to those building the Nord Stream 2 pipeline whether to complete it despite opposition from Washington. <a href=\"\/business\/energy\/blinken-says-up-nord-stream-2-builders-whether-finish-pipeline-2021-03-28\/\"> read more "},{"type":"paragraph","content":"According to Nord Stream 2 AG, the pipeline is 95% complete and around 121 kilometre (75 miles) is left to be built."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: German gas grids report progress with investment plans to 2030
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: German gas pipeline companies have completed 28 out of 201 measures planned between 2020 and 2030, keeping them on track to provide capacity expansions and conversions for increased imports this decade, industry group FNB said on Thursday.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"* Gas firms’ report shows 14% of plans for 2030 carried out"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"* Indigenous reserves fall, imports to rise"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"* Eugal pipeline fully constructed, feeder for Nord Stream 2"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"FRANKFURT, April 1 German gas pipeline companies have completed 28 out of 201 measures planned between 2020 and 2030, keeping them on track to provide capacity expansions and conversions for increased imports this decade, industry group FNB said on Thursday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Germany and its neighbours will need to get more gas via pipelines and seaborne shipments of liquefied natural gas (LNG), because supplies from the region’s reserves are dwindling."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Germany’s north-west and the Netherlands are already phasing out production of their local, low-calorific gas type, meaning transport, storage infrastructure and boilers must be changed to accommodate imported gas that is high-calorific."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In addition, Germany has embarked on a strategy to switch some existing gas infrastructure to yet-to-arrive hydrogen made from renewable energy via electrolysis under national decarbonisation plans."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"FNB, whose members include Gascade Gastransport, Ontras Gastransport and Open Grid Europe, must file implementation reports because the transport of energy commodities is paid for by consumers via regulated fees."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The 28 completions include compressor stations, metres and fittings such as one million low-cal boilers, under an 8.5 billion euro ($10 billion) investment plan approved last year, which included plans for 1,746 km of new pipelines."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The measures specifically included one or two LNG terminals and Eugal, a 480 km-pipeline for gas from the yet to be completed Nord Stream 2 (NS 2) subsea pipeline, to run onshore from north Germany to the Czech Republic."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Eugal project leader Gascade said in a separate statement on Thursday it had now built the pipeline’s second tranche, bringing capacity to the intended amount of 55 billion cubic metres (bcm)."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Germany currently receives pipeline gas from Russia via the Czech Republic, Poland and via NS 2-forerunner Nord Stream 1 and most of the rest from North Sea producers, with a small share produced at home."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Canada's cash-rich oil sands firms face pressure to spend on transition
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Canada's biggest oil sands producers are generating billions more in free cash flow in a faster-than-expected pandemic rebound, but taking a cautious approach to spending it that is disappointing environment-minded investors.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"Canada's biggest oil sands producers are generating billions more in free cash flow in a faster-than-expected pandemic rebound, but taking a cautious approach to spending it that is disappointing environment-minded investors."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Their strategy to repay debts and pay shareholders has won praise from investors in Canadian Natural Resources <a href=\"https:\/\/www.reuters.com\/companies\/CNQ.TO\" target=\"_blank\">(CNQ.TO), Suncor Energy <a href=\"https:\/\/www.reuters.com\/companies\/SU.TO\" target=\"_blank\">(SU.TO) and Cenovus Energy <a href=\"https:\/\/www.reuters.com\/companies\/CVE.TO\" target=\"_blank\">(CVE.TO)who are eager for higher returns. But greener shareholders warn they could divest or oppose management."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The sharp recovery has thrust the companies deep into a debate on returns versus cleaner fuels that will determine the makeup of their business for decades. The oil and gas sector accounted for 26% of Canada's carbon emissions in 2018, and Prime Minister Justin Trudeau has set a goal of net-zero emissions for the country by 2050."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Canadian Natural expects to generate up to C$5.4 billion  ($4.30 billion) in free cash flow in 2021, from C$692 million last year. Suncor projects additional cash flow of C$400 million this year and C$1 billion by 2023. Cenovus could generate C$3.5 billion this year, analysts at investment bank Morgan Stanley estimate, from a loss last year."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"CHANGE IS COMING"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Some investors and lenders warn they could walk away if more of that cash is not spent on projects that transition the companies for a low-carbon future."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"\"They have these ambitious transition targets and a relatively short window to make people believe that their transition plans are real,\" said Jamie Bonham, director of corporate engagement at NEI Investments, which owns shares in all three oil sands producers worth a combined C$71 million. NEI could divest or vote against directors if progress does not come soon, he said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"\"We will take into account whether they're moving in the right direction,\" said Steve Peacher, president of SLC Management, an investment subsidiary of Sun Life Financial <a href=\"https:\/\/www.reuters.com\/companies\/SLF.TO\" target=\"_blank\">(SLF.TO). \"We won't lend to energy firms that we don't think are doing that.\""},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Canada's biggest energy producers trade at a free cash flow yield of 15% for 2021 and 2022, compared with a median of 10% for U.S. peers, Morgan Stanley said in March."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"However, oil executives argue it is too soon to take a more aggressive approach, with the pandemic continuing."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"\"We're focused on our balance sheet,\" Canadian Natural President Tim McKay said, adding that repaying debt is a priority."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Suncor said in February it is spending additional cash on repaying debt and repurchasing shares, with 10% of its capital earmarked for a wind farm and cogeneration project."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"\"If you're structurally cutting shareholder returns to take their cash and invest it in the transition, that's going to be tough, because we need the support of the shareholders and the capital markets,\" Suncor Chief Executive Mark Little said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Cenovus has said it plans to reduce debt this year and did not comment further on spending plans."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"'CARROTS NOT STICKS'"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"While oil sands companies are being cautious with cash, Alberta has asked Ottawa to fund a C$30-billion, 10-year program to develop carbon capture."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The federal government will require the companies to share the costs of any carbon-capture initiatives, said a senior government source who was not authorized to speak publicly."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"One investor, Michael Sprung, said repaying debt and increasing dividends are the right corporate priorities. \"I think oil is going to be the primary part of their business,\" he said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"But lenders are growing cautious about the sector."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"\"We're trying to use carrots, not sticks,\" in pushing fossil fuels companies to produce more renewable energy, said Andrea Barrack, global head of sustainability at Canada's second-largest lender Toronto-Dominion Bank."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"If they fail to accelerate the shift to cleaner fuels, lenders will see them as risky over time and require higher interest rates, said Amy West, TD Securities' global head of sustainable finance."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Bank of Montreal also aims to reach net zero emissions in its lending portfolio by 2050, but without \"disruptive change\" to Canada's economy, Chief Executive Darryl White said. <a href=\"\/business\/environment\/bmo-targets-net-zero-emissions-lending-by-2050-cautions-against-abrupt-change-2021-03-10\/\"> read more "},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The oil sands companies finally have the cash to put toward greater emissions reductions, said Andrew Logan, senior director of oil and gas at Ceres, a shareholder advisory group."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"\"There's a big gap between rhetoric and investment,\" Logan said. \"They've been 20 years away for the last 20 years.\""},{"type":"paragraph","content":"($1 = 1.2563 Canadian dollars)"}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: KPN sues Sweden's Ericsson over telecom patents
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: KPN NV (KPN.AS), the largest Dutch telecommunications company, has filed a patent-infringement complaint against Ericsson (ERICb.ST) in a district court in Texas, the Swedish telecom equipment maker said on Thursday.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"KPN NV <a href=\"https:\/\/www.reuters.com\/companies\/KPN.AS\" target=\"_blank\">(KPN.AS), the largest Dutch telecommunications company, has filed a patent-infringement complaint against Ericsson <a href=\"https:\/\/www.reuters.com\/companies\/ERICb.ST\" target=\"_blank\">(ERICb.ST) in a district court in Texas, the Swedish telecom equipment maker said on Thursday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The issue revolves around Ericsson's alleged infringement of five KPN patents covering various wireless network functions."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In a court filing, KPN said it had offered to issue licences to Ericsson for the infringed patents but the Swedish company did not obtain a licence."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"\"We refrain from making any further comments since this is an ongoing legal matter,\" an Ericsson spokeswoman said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Lawsuits over royalty payments are not uncommon in the technology industry. Ericsson in December <a href=\"https:\/\/www.reuters.com\/article\/us-ericsson-patents-samsung-idUSKBN28L0MX\" target=\"_blank\">filed a lawsuit in the United States against Samsung <a href=\"https:\/\/www.reuters.com\/companies\/005930.KS\" target=\"_blank\">(005930.KS)in a patent dispute."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Ericsson had warned that delayed royalty payments and potential legal costs could reduce its operating income by 1-1.5 billion Swedish crowns ($118 million-$177 million) per quarter beginning in the first quarter of 2021."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"KPN has been a telecom equipment customer of Ericsson for more than a decade and last year <a href=\"https:\/\/www.reuters.com\/article\/kpn-5g-ericsson-idUSKBN2700Y1\" target=\"_blank\">awarded the company a contract to build core elements of its new 5G mobile network."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Dutch company said in the lawsuit that it is seeking monetary compensation for the infringed patents."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"A KPN spokesman declined to give more detail as the case had been filed with the court."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: India's digital IDs for land could exclude poor, indigenous communities
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Plans by the Indian government to assign digital identification numbers to plots of land could exclude rural and indigenous people who do not hold titles, and further marginalise those without internet access, experts said.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"April 1 (Thomson Reuters Foundation) - Plans by the Indian government to assign digital identification numbers to plots of land could exclude rural and indigenous people who do not hold titles, and further marginalise those without internet access, experts said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The 14-digit Unique Land Parcel Identification Number (ULPIN) was launched in 10 states earlier this year and will be rolled out across the country by March 2022, authorities at the Department of Land Resources told parliament this week."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The ULPIN will be based on the latitude and longitude of each parcel of land and will rely on surveys and cadastral maps, authorities said. Individual plot numbers will also be linked to bank records and the national ID Aadhaar numbers, they said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Officials have billed the programme as a way to tackle corruption and land disputes, but critics warned of many potential pitfalls - from outdated land registry records to flaws in the Aadhaar database."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Linking land records to Aadhaar requires “extreme caution”, said Kanchi Kohli, a senior researcher at the Centre for Policy and Research think-tank, citing frequent cases of mismatched IDs, or a lack of registration in the system."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“It may further complicate existing tensions in creating and maintaining land records, and gets particularly exclusionary when land is being used seasonally by pastoral communities or common use for forest produce or fishing,” she added."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The land ID scheme is part of a push to digitalise India’s land records that began in 2008 and was scheduled to be completed by the end of March this year. It will now be extended to 2024, authorities said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Land department officials told lawmakers digitalising land records was “a game changer in reducing corruption” as well as land disputes, saying it empowered ordinary people by allowing them to access information online."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"About 70% of land in developing nations is undocumented, leaving more than a quarter of the world’s population vulnerable to disputes, evictions and encroachment, according to the Washington-based land rights nonprofit Cadasta Foundation."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"While documenting land data can lead to greater efficiency in land administration and increased prosperity, authorities may not be consulting communities, failing to secure data, or using it to evict vulnerable people, human rights groups say."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Some Indian states have not surveyed their land in more than a century, and experts have questioned the logic of digitalising existing records, and raised concerns over data access and privacy as records are made accessible online."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Pranab Choudhury, convener at the Center for Land Governance think-tank, said the digital ID scheme was potentially beneficial but could become ineffective “and even highly contested” if it was based on outdated records."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Many plots have been subdivided since the last survey, yet remain as one plot in cadastral maps. Subdivisions are often not recorded to avoid transaction cost, so ULPIN should be implemented only after a complete resurvey,” he said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In addition, women, Dalits and indigenous people who are often prevented from owning land risk being shut out, he added."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"\"Implementing ULPIN hurriedly, without addressing legacy issues can seriously undermine citizen trust and may lead to more disputes. The poor and other disadvantaged groups may be further alienated and excluded,\" he added. (Reporting by Rina Chandran @rinachandran; Editing by Helen Popper. Please credit the Thomson Reuters Foundation, the charitable arm of Thomson Reuters, that covers the lives of people around the world who struggle to live freely or fairly. Visit \u003ca href=\"http://news.trust.org\"\u003enews.trust.org\u003c/a\u003e)"}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Value, small-cap funds outperform in first quarter as U.S. inflation worries rise
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: The Biden administration's $1.9 trillion stimulus plan and expectations of rising inflation helped bolster the performance of fund managers who made bets on economically-sensitive cyclical or small-cap companies in the first quarter of the year, Morningstar data showed.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"NEW YORK The Biden administration’s $1.9 trillion stimulus plan and expectations of rising inflation helped bolster the performance of fund managers who made bets on economically-sensitive cyclical or small-cap companies in the first quarter of the year, Morningstar data showed."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"At the same time, fund managers who remained heavily-invested in giant technology companies and high-growth stocks that had outperformed during the pandemic floundered."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The gap in performance was pronounced, with the average large-cap value fund gaining 11.4% for the quarter while the average large-cap growth fund rose 2.2% over the same time, according to Morningstar."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Kinetic Small-Cap Opportunities fund notched the best overall performance among actively managed U.S. equity funds with a 52.5% gain for the year through March 24, according to Morningstar. Among fixed income funds, the Virtus InfraCap US Preferred Stock logged the best overall performance with a 9.1% gain over the same time period."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Overall, active U.S. equity funds returned an average of 7% through March 24, with large cap funds returning an average of 5% while small-cap funds gained an average of 11.7%, according to Morningstar."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The benchmark S\u0026amp;P 500 is up 8.2% for the year to date."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“The more value-oriented, more economically-titled portfolios tended to do better in the first quarter,” said Todd Rosenbluth, director of mutual fund research at New York-based CFRA. “If interest rates remain range bound that bodes well for the future. But if we see rising interest rates that could slow the economy, which would benefit the larger cap strategies.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Expectations of an economic boom in the United States have pushed inflation expectations have risen to their highest levels since 2014. Rising inflation could weigh on the economy by increasing debt rates for companies and consumers."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Bond yields, meanwhile, rose to their pre-pandemic highs during the first quarter, with benchmark 10 year Treasuries rising to nearly 1.75%."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"That surge weighed on tech companies, many of which are valued more on their future earnings than current profits, and prompted investors to seek out companies such as financials that benefit from higher interest rates."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The ARKK Innovation ETF, run by star stock picker Cathie Wood, fell more than 10.7% during the quarter in a performance that left it in the worst 1 percentile of funds in its category, according to Morningstar. Among its top holdings are automaker Tesla Inc and streaming platform Roku Inc."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Despite that underperformance, the fund brought in nearly $5.5 billion in new funds so far this year, an inflow greater than any other actively-managed equity fund."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"ARK did not respond to a request to comment."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Climate activists spray black dye at Bank of England in 'Money Rebellion'
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Climate activists in London splashed black dye on the facade of the Bank of England's imposing neo-classical headquarters on Thursday as part of a protest against the finance sector's support of what they say is a climate catastrophe.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"LONDON (Reuters) -Climate activists in London splashed black dye on the facade of the Bank of England’s imposing neo-classical headquarters on Thursday as part of a protest against the finance sector’s support of what they say is a climate catastrophe."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Activists, some dressed as jesters, sprayed the dye at the building, known as “the Old Lady of Threadneedle Street”, leaving black stains on the main entrance to the building."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“This bank is killing us,” read a banner held up by one protester. “No more fossil fuels,” read another."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In Paris, activists draped a banner reading “magic money, toxic investments” on the Banque de France building on Rue Croix des Petits Champs. Protesters held smoke flares while others flung paint at the building and danced amid a rain of fake euro notes."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In London, police said they had arrested four people, one for trespassing and three for criminal damage."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Bank of England declined to comment when asked by Reuters for a response to the action."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“The action today is part of a wave of actions by XR’s Money Rebellion designed to expose the role of banks in the climate and ecological crisis,” the environmental movement Extinction Rebellion said. The action is being cast by the group as a “Money Rebellion.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Extinction Rebellion group wants to trigger a rebellion against the political, economic and social structure of the modern world to avert the worst devastation outlined by scientists studying climate change."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"It says the Bank of England has failed to be strict enough with commercial banks to stop them funding climate change and wants it to be much tougher with the financial sector."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"More fundamentally, the group says the Bank, which it cast as the “Bank of Extinction”, was a pillar of an economic model based on infinite growth that prioritised short-term profit over the health of the planet."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The group is targeting private banks too."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“It is not OK that the Bank of England can distribute money to companies that are destroying our planet whilst millions face the destruction of their future because of their actions,” said activist Amelia Halls, 22."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“The government is doing everything they can to greenwash themselves when at the same time we have a financial system in this country that is actively financing companies and institutions that are destroying the planet.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Bank of England was established in 1694. John Soane’s majestic Bank of England building was finished in the early 19th century but only the exterior of that remains. The rest was demolished and rebuilt in the early 20th century."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Pandemic slowdown led to record fall in EU carbon market emissions
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Emissions regulated by Europe's carbon market fell by 14.4% in 2020, their biggest percentage decline yet, as pandemic restrictions stifled economic activity and grounded flights, official data examined by carbon analysts at Refinitiv showed.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"LONDON Emissions regulated by Europe’s carbon market fell by 14.4% in 2020, their biggest percentage decline yet, as pandemic restrictions stifled economic activity and grounded flights, official data examined by carbon analysts at Refinitiv showed."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Around 45% of the European Union’s output of greenhouse gases is regulated by the Emissions Trading System (ETS), the bloc’s flagship instrument to tackle global warming by charging for the right to emit carbon dioxide (CO2)."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Refinitiv analysts’ interpretation of European Commission data found emissions covered by the ETS totalled 1.365 billion tonnes of CO2 equivalent (CO2e), down 14.4% on the previous year."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The fall was the largest in percentage terms since the market was launched in 2005."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The market does not cover emissions from agriculture or transport beyond the aviation sector."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“The substantial drop in emissions is the fallout from the pandemic with economic activity shrinking last year and renewables displacing fossil-fired power,” Refinitiv analyst Ingvild Sorhus said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"With international travel restricted, aviation sector emissions dived 58.4% to 25.8 million tonnes CO2e."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"After aviation, the heat and power sector, whose emissions totalled 632.8 million tonnes of CO2e, down 17.1% on 2019, registered the next steepest fall."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Stationary emissions covered by the scheme, such as from power plants and factories, totalled 1.339 billion tonnes of CO2e, down 12.6% on the previous year, the data showed."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The figures were in line with analysts forecasts and the benchmark price of carbon permits in the ETS was little changed on Thursday at around 42.50 euros a tonne."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Carbon prices have been rising since the European Union agreed last year to toughen its climate targets, which will increase demand for permits to emit, and hit a record high of 43.77 euros/tonne last month."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: U.S. envoy Kerry heads to India to try and lift "climate ambition"
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: U.S. climate envoy John Kerry will hold talks with Indian leaders during an Asian tour starting on Thursday in an effort to narrow differences on climate change goals to slow global warming.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"NEW DELHI U.S. climate envoy John Kerry will hold talks with Indian leaders during an Asian tour starting on Thursday in an effort to narrow differences on climate change goals to slow global warming."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government is facing calls from the United States and Britain to commit India, the world’s third biggest carbon emitter, to a net zero emissions target by 2050."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"India, whose per capita emissions are way lower than that of the United States, European countries and even China, is concerned that binding itself to such a target could constrain the energy needs of its people."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Kerry kicks off his trip on Thursday that will also take him to the United Arab Emirates and Bangladesh, which experts say is especially vulnerable to climate change as it has large numbers of people living in areas barely above sea level, and lacks infrastructure to protect them."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Special Presidential Envoy for Climate John Kerry will travel to Abu Dhabi, New Delhi, and Dhaka  April 1-9, 2021, for consultations on increasing climate ambition ...” the State Department said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Kerry will take part in a climate dialogue for the Middle East and North Africa hosted by Abu Dhabi on April 4, the UAE state news agency WAM said on Thursday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"It said the Regional Climate Dialogue would provide a platform for countries to “unite around progressive, practical solutions” to help reach global climate goals."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Kerry is leading efforts to get countries to commit themselves to reduce greenhouse gas emissions to zero by about the middle of the century."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"President Joe Biden has called a summit of 40 leaders including India and China on April 22-23."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Later this year world leaders will gather for the United Nations climate summit in Glasgow to build on a 2015 Paris accord to halt the increase in global temperatures at levels that would avoid the worst impacts of climate change."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Looking forward to meaningful discussions with friends in the Emirates, India, and Bangladesh on how to tackle the climate crisis,” Kerry tweeted."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"India says it will not only stick to the Paris accord to reduce its carbon footprint by 33-35% from its 2005 levels by 2030 but will likely exceed those goals as it ramps up use of renewable energy."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Thailand taps groundwater resources as hot season drought looms
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Facing severe drought as it enters its hottest season, Thailand has launched groundwater extraction operations in its most arid regions to tap sources deep beneath the soil, as it looks at ways to harness future supplies.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"YASOTHON, Thailand Facing severe drought as it enters its hottest season, Thailand has launched groundwater extraction operations in its most arid regions to tap sources deep beneath the soil, as it looks at ways to harness future supplies."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The groundwater department has sent geologists and more than 80 teams to areas not served by irrigation networks and regions typically hit by shortages as dam water levels are depleted."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In northeast Yasothon province, solar-powered water pumps and tanks have been deployed in one of 25 groundwater stations, among some 937 underground wells in the region."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“The water source on the surface, when it dries up, the only source left is what is underneath us,” Natural Resources and Environment Minister Varawut Silpa-Archa said during a visit."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“The amount of groundwater underneath Thailand has been tremendous,” he said, estimating 10% to 15% of Thailand’s more than 700 million litres (185 million gallons) of rainwater was beneath the ground."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Groundwater abstraction has been controversial in some countries, with concern about an over-reliance on underground sources instead of protecting and better managing water resources on the surface."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Some conservation groups say wildlife and flora are impacted by groundwater abstraction drying out lakes and wetlands while agriculture is consuming unsustainable amounts of water."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"It can also cause aquifers to deplete and water tables to fall, while abstraction can cause land to sink, as has happened in and around the capital Bangkok."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Varawut said “every precaution” was being taken to prevent damage and sinkholes."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Despite efforts to convince farmers to cultivate crops that are less water-intensive, water demand for agriculture keeps growing. To try to harness future supplies, authorities are studying whether to develop hundreds more groundwater resources."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Organic fruit farmer La Somabutr said there were few trees left to hold water and wells dried up in March and April, so the groundwater drilling had been a game-changer."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“It’s badly dry here,” he said. “Now we have this groundwater. I feel like I’m reborn.”"}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Taiwan opens first travel bubble, with tourism-dependent Palau
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Taiwan opened its first travel bubble during the COVID-19 pandemic on Thursday, with the small, tourism-dependent Pacific state of Palau, offering a lifeline to a country in a region where China and the United States are battling for influence.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"TAOYUAN, Taiwan Taiwan opened its first travel bubble during the COVID-19 pandemic on Thursday, with the small, tourism-dependent Pacific state of Palau, offering a lifeline to a country in a region where China and the United States are battling for influence."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Palau, less than four hours by plane from Taiwan, is one of only 15 countries to maintain formal diplomatic ties with the Chinese-claimed island, and the closing of its borders last year to keep the virus out has severely hurt its economy."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"With Palau recording no cases and the outbreak under control in Taiwan, Taipei agreed to the “sterile corridor” last month, though there are still controls, including tourists having to travel in a group and limited contact with local people."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Speaking at Taiwan’s main international airport at Taoyuan, outside of Taipei, Palau President Surangel Whipps Jr. said he was pleased the bubble was starting."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Many times we need to take bold steps, and I think this is a bold step. But it’s a very careful step and that’s why we say we’re opening Palau with care,” he said, before boarding a China Airlines 737 jet back home, accompanying the first group in the bubble."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Some other global travel bubbles have come and gone as the pandemic roared back, or offer quarantine-free travel only in one direction, like from the Cook Islands to New Zealand."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Pacific is the site of a diplomatic tug-of-war between Beijing and Washington, and in 2019 China snatched away two of Taiwan’s allies there, Kiribati and the Solomon Islands."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The United States has accused China of enticing developing Pacific nations with generous loans, charges Beijing denies."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Taiwan has provided development aid to Palau, including healthcare, and the bubble flight also has a small team of doctors and nurses aboard."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Still, for the travel-starved tourists on board it was an opportunity to finally go abroad again."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“I’m so excited. I’ve been looking forward to this for ages,” said Choyce Kuo, 44."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: U.S. trade chief voices concern to Vietnam over currency practices
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: U.S. Trade Representative Katherine Tai, in a call on Thursday with Vietnam's minister of industry and trade, highlighted U.S. concerns about Vietnam's currency practices, a USTR statement said.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"WASHINGTON (Reuters) -U.S. Trade Representative Katherine Tai, in a call on Thursday with Vietnam’s minister of industry and trade, highlighted U.S. concerns about Vietnam’s currency practices, a USTR statement said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Tai and the Vietnamese minister Tran Tuan Anh also “discussed U.S. concerns on illegal timber practices, digital trade and agriculture,” the statement said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Vietnam’s Ministry of Industry and Trade in a statement on Friday said Vietnam and the United States “will continue to actively cooperate to comprehensively address the concerns to maintain a stable trade relation.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The ministry said bilateral trade between the two countries is expected to reach $100 billion this year, up from $90.8 billion last year. The United States is Vietnam’s largest export market."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The U.S. Treasury Department in December labeled Vietnam a “currency manipulator” due to its growing trade surplus with the United States, its large global current account surplus and heavy foreign exchange market intervention to hold down the value of its dong currency."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In January, the USTR released the results of an investigation into Vietnam’s currency practices."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"It found Vietnam’s actions to push down the value of its currency were “unreasonable” and restricted U.S. commerce, but it did not take immediate action to impose punitive tariffs."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In February, Reuters exclusively reported that Vietnam’s central bank was intervening in foreign exchange markets, using what traders described as an unusual method."}]
