test_endpoint.articlesName: Italy reports 501 coronavirus deaths on Thursday, 23,649 new cases
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Italy reported 501 coronavirus-related deaths on Thursday against 467 the day before, the health ministry said, while the daily tally of new infections decreased to 23,649 from 23,904.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"MILAN Italy reported 501 coronavirus-related deaths on Thursday against 467 the day before, the health ministry said, while the daily tally of new infections decreased to 23,649 from 23,904."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Some 356,085 tests for COVID-19 were carried out in the past day, compared with a previous 351,221, the health ministry said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Italy has registered 109,847 deaths linked to COVID-19 since its outbreak emerged in February last year, the second-highest toll in Europe after Britain and the seventh-highest in the world. The country has reported 3.6 million cases to date."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Patients in hospital with COVID-19 - not including those in intensive care - stood at 28,949 on Thursday, down from 29,180 a day earlier."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"There were 244 new admissions to intensive care units, down from 283 on Wednesday. The total number of intensive care patients were down to 3,681 from a previous 3,710."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: South African health regulator approves J&J's COVID-19 vaccine
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: South Africa's health regulator has approved Johnson & Johnson's COVID-19 vaccine, paving the way for large-scale deliveries of the shot the government has put at the heart of its immunisation plans.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"JOHANNESBURG South Africa’s health regulator has approved Johnson \u0026amp; Johnson’s COVID-19 vaccine, paving the way for large-scale deliveries of the shot the government has put at the heart of its immunisation plans."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The conditional approval by the South African Health Products Regulatory Authority (SAHPRA) comes less than four months after it started a “rolling review” of the J\u0026amp;J vaccine, which has been administered to healthcare workers since mid-February in a research study."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"J\u0026amp;J aims to supply the country with 31 million doses of its single-dose vaccine, with 2.8 million doses being made available in the second quarter, it said in a statement announcing the approval."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"SAHPRA said in a separate statement the vaccine’s registration on March 31 was a significant step in the fight against COVID-19. It said its authorisation was subject to conditions including that the vaccine is administered in line with the government’s immunisation plan and that periodic safety updates would be submitted."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The J\u0026amp;J shots will come from local pharmaceutical company Aspen, which will be manufacturing up to 300 million doses under licence."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"South Africa’s vaccination campaign was dealt a blow in early February when it put on hold a plan to start inoculations with AstraZeneca’s vaccine, after a small trial showed it offered minimal protection against mild to moderate COVID-19 caused by the dominant local coronavirus variant."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The government then switched to using the J\u0026amp;J shot in an “implementation study” to start protecting frontline healthcare workers with limited doses. So far it has vaccinated roughly 260,000 people, out of 1.25 million health workers, health ministry data show."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The pace of vaccinations has been slow, with health experts, trade unions and businesses urging the government to ramp up vaccinations once more supplies become available."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The government is also expecting 20 million doses of COVID-19 vaccine from Pfizer, as well as supplies from the COVAX vaccine distribution scheme co-led by the World Health Organization and partners including the Gavi vaccines alliance."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"A large clinical trial of J\u0026amp;J’s vaccine, which was conducted in eight countries including South Africa, showed the vaccine was 66% effective in preventing moderate to severe COVID-19 infection and 85% effective in stopping severe disease and hospitalization."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Pfizer’s vaccine was 100% effective in preventing symptomatic cases among trial participants in South Africa, the company said on Thursday, adding, however, that the rate was derived from a group of 800 participants, a relatively small sample."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: COVAX COVID-19 vaccine facility faces shortfall in supply: WHO
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: The COVAX facility to distribute COVID-19 vaccines to poorer countries faces a "serious challenge" to meet demand, WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus told a news conference on Thursday.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"GENEVA The COVAX facility to distribute COVID-19 vaccines to poorer countries faces a “serious challenge” to meet demand, WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus told a news conference on Thursday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Last week, I made an urgent request to countries, with doses of COVID-19 vaccines that have WHO Emergency Use Listing, to share 10 million doses immediately with COVAX,” he said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“I requested manufacturers to help ensure that the countries that step up can rapidly donate those doses. This challenge has been heard but we’re yet to receive commitments for these doses. I’m still hopeful that some forward looking and enlightened leaders will step up,” he added."}]

test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: The United Kingdom reported 51 new COVID-19 deaths on Thursday, taking the seven-day total to 320, a drop of 38.5% compared with the previous seven-day period, official data showed.

test_endpoint.articlesName: Merkel appeals to Germans to stay home for Easter to stem pandemic third wave
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Chancellor Angela Merkel appealed to Germans on Thursday to stay at home over Easter and meet fewer people to help curb a third wave of the coronavirus pandemic, as the capital Berlin announced a nighttime ban on gatherings from Friday.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"BERLIN (Reuters) -Chancellor Angela Merkel appealed to Germans on Thursday to stay at home over Easter and meet fewer people to help curb a third wave of the coronavirus pandemic, as the capital Berlin announced a nighttime ban on gatherings from Friday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“It should be a quiet Easter, with those closest to you, with very reduced contact. I urge you to refrain from all non-essential travel,” Merkel said in a video message, adding this was the only way to help doctors and nurses fight the virus."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Merkel was accused of losing her grip on the COVID-19 crisis last week after she ditched plans for an extended Easter holiday agreed two days earlier with governors of Germany’s 16 states."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"She has since tried to shift the blame for the third wave of the pandemic onto state premiers, accusing them of failing to stick to earlier agreements to reimpose restrictions if infections rose."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"On Thursday, the city government of Berlin said it will impose a nighttime ban on gatherings from Friday and only allow children of essential workers to attend nursery from next week."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"As the weather has turned warm in recent days, Berliners have been flocking to public spaces. About a hundred youngsters threw bottles and stones at police in one park on Wednesday when they tried to break up the party, the Berliner Zeitung reported."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Merkel said it was no longer the elderly who were fighting for their lives in the pandemic, but the middle-aged and even younger patients who were ending up on ventilators in hospital."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"She held out hope, however, that the sluggish distribution of vaccinations would speed up after Easter, when family doctors will start giving shots."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Christian Karagiannidis, the scientific head of the DIVI association for intensive and emergency medicine, said Germany needs a two-week lockdown, faster vaccinations and compulsory tests at schools if hospitals are not to be overwhelmed."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“If this rate continues, we will reach the regular capacity limit in less than four weeks,” he told the Rheinische Post daily. “We are not over-exaggerating. Our warnings are driven by the figures.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Berlin city government said people would only be allowed to be outside on their own or with one other person from 9 p.m. until 5 a.m., though children under 14 are exempted."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"This will be the first limited curfew imposed in Berlin since the pandemic began a year ago. The city of Hamburg already announced on Wednesday it will restrict nighttime outings from Friday, with supermarkets and takeaways shut from 9 p.m."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Unlike Britain and France, Germany’s 16 states, which run their own healthcare and security affairs, have been reluctant to impose drastic limits on movement out of fear of further damaging the economy, as well as an aversion to far-reaching restrictions on freedoms in a country wary of its Nazi past."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The number of confirmed coronavirus cases in Germany, Europe’s most populous country and largest economy, rose 24,300 to 2.833 million on Thursday, the biggest daily increase since Jan. 14. The reported death toll rose by 201 to 76,543."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Hungary's private health sector sees opportunity as COVID snarls hospital ops
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: A year after COVID-19 arrived in Hungary, public hospitals have spent most of their resources fighting the virus and are currently battling its deadliest outbreak yet, unable to treat the growing numbers of people awaiting non-emergency procedures.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"BUDAPEST A year after COVID-19 arrived in Hungary, public hospitals have spent most of their resources fighting the virus and are currently battling its deadliest outbreak yet, unable to treat the growing numbers of people awaiting non-emergency procedures."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"So with public hospitals closed to elective surgery, a quiet revolution in private health care is unfolding, led by a wave of investment in private hospitals and growth in health insurance."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Traditionally public hospitals provide the overwhelming majority of in-patient care, looking after everything from tonsillectomies to heart bypass surgery, but the pandemic has created an opportunity for existing private healthcare providers to expand and new competitors to enter the market."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Private hospital executives interviewed by Reuters have pledged or invested 85 million euros ($100 million) in the sector: a new hospital due in the capital Budapest, taking the lion’s share of that spending, alongside a surgical ward planned in an existing facility and additional beds and upgraded equipment completed in another."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"There is no publicly available data on such investments, but in the past two years only two new private hospitals were opened. Total investment is dwarfed by annual public health spending worth 4% to 5% of economic output, based on OECD figures."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Private health insurance grew by 23% last year, with some of that large increase due to relatively low market penetration according to Hungarian insurance association figures."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The average waiting time for common procedures, such as orthopaedic surgeries, has rocketed to more than a year from just 22 days based on public data from the government’s National Health Insurance Fund."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"For example, the wait for a hip replacement has grown from 59 days to 406 days, for a hernia 25 days to 410 days, it said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Emergency surgery has continued throughout the pandemic."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"For Rozalia, a 41-year-old sales manager at a Hungarian company, the revolution cannot come soon enough. She had life-saving surgery to remove a tumour from her breast last summer and has since lived with a tissue expander, a temporary fix until an operation to change it to a permanent implant."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“All my doctor could say that once the halted operations restart, they will discuss when I may get mine it is not likely before the end of the summer,” she said, adding however that she cannot afford the procedure in the private sector."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Hungary’s health authorities have given no indication as to when waiting times could fall back to normal. Neither the public health fund nor the health ministry responded to requests for comment."},{"type":"heading","content":"HEALTH INSURANCE"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Antal Kovacs, chief executive at the Da Vinci private clinic in southern Hungary, is sceptical the backlog could be wrestled down in just a year once the coronavirus crisis abates."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Those who cannot or do not want to wait any longer, will look for private care, unless they require a procedure that cannot be performed in the private sector,” he said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Aron Kovaloczy, managing director at DLA Piper Business Advisory, said the quality, access, infrastructure of Hungary’s public health system “has been steadily declining for years”."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“In tandem with that, effective demand by people whose needs cannot be met by the public health system has been increasing,” he said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Of the $100 million investment under way and in the pipeline, the Buda Health Centre plans to start construction of a new hospital in Budapest this year at a cost of up to 30 billion forints ($97 million), adding 131 beds and eight operating rooms, Director Peter Pal Varga said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“As private health insurance expands and we also grow organically, our patient numbers will increase,” he said. “We need to meet the demand in the market.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Vienna Insurance Group’s Union unit said while the number of Hungarians who could afford private in-patient care was still low and currently available in-patient care limited, private sector offerings were set to expand in the coming years."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“As the role of the private sector increases, so does demand for private health insurance,” business unit leader Gabor Zsolnai said, adding that Union expected another 15-20% increase in private health insurance sales this year."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Anita Gurney, chief executive of the Duna Medical Centre private clinic that opened a new hospital in Budapest this year, said while in-patient private care could be pricey, it is no longer just the privilege of the elite."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“It all depends on when people’s pain or their patience reaches a limit pushing them towards private care,” she said."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: U.S. COVID-19 vaccine rollout analysis hampered by technology, state data reporting
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: When a dose of a COVID-19 vaccine leaves a U.S. manufacturing plant, its path can be traced all the way to the hospital or clinic representative signing for the shipment at its destination. What happens next is not always clear.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"When a dose of a COVID-19 vaccine leaves a U.S. manufacturing plant, its path can be traced all the way to the hospital or clinic representative signing for the shipment at its destination. What happens next is not always clear."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Federal agencies overseeing the rollout are relying on a tangled web of aging state vaccine registries complicated by state laws and practices."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Data collection has improved since the national vaccination campaign began in December, with county-level reporting in most states. But gaps and tech issues remain that could compromise equitable distribution of doses, analysis of vaccine protection, and identification of pockets of vaccine hesitancy, experts said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"It is a monumental task as the national vaccination campaign gathers steam with an average of 2.4 million shots going into arms each day and rising, and some 196 million doses distributed since December."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"As the vaccine rollout opens to all American adults, analysts will be watching whether the less advantaged lose out."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Are we achieving our equity goals?” said Dr. William Moss, executive director of the International Vaccine Access Center at Johns Hopkins University. “That would be very hard to tease out at a federal level, given the variation in how states are reporting.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The uncoordinated nature of data collection in Marin County, California, across the Golden Gate bridge from San Francisco, “makes it virtually impossible for me to have that global view that I need to be able to see who is getting vaccinated and who isn’t,” said Dr. Matt Willis, county public health officer."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The U.S. vaccine data system has two main parts: recently developed federal software from Palantir Technologies Inc that closely tracks distribution of doses, and a range of systems used by states that report into decade-old federal systems developed for limited tracking of child vaccinations."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“We know where every single dose was delivered; we know when it was delivered; we know who ordered it; we know who signed for it; we know who dropped it off at the location,” said one person involved in tracking vaccine distribution. “Where we lose sight of it is when (the providers) take it.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"‘IT’S NOT PERFECT’ Matthew Ritchey, an epidemiologist and data expert at the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), said vaccine data collection has improved significantly since the beginning of the rollout. The CDC, which is leading the nation’s vaccine data collection, now has a more detailed view of inoculations across the country."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Does that mean perfect? No, it’s not perfect. But the amount of information that we’re collecting now on a daily basis is pretty astounding,” he said, with most vaccinators reporting shots within the required 72 hours."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Last week, the CDC also publicly released county level data for the first time since the rollout began. A Kaiser Family Foundation (KFF) report using the data found counties with high Black and Hispanic populations had lower vaccination rates than others, confirming what many health experts had feared."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"However, KFF was only able to analyze about 72% of the counties due to low quality or incomplete county-level data from a dozen states, including Colorado, Georgia, and Virginia."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The CDC itself has a Texas-sized gap in its own data. The federal government is not receiving the same detailed information about vaccinations of the Lone Star state’s 29 million residents that it’s getting from other states, because Texas statutes prevent it from sending that data to the federal government. If anyone should be able to get this right, it’s California,” he said."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: WHO's Kluge says European COVID-19 vaccine campaign is 'unacceptably slow'
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Europe's rollout of vaccinations against COVID-19 is "unacceptably slow," the World Health Organization's European head said on Thursday, raising concern that delays in giving shots could prolong the pandemic as cases of variants spread.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"ZURICH Europe’s rollout of vaccinations against COVID-19 is “unacceptably slow,” the World Health Organization’s European head said on Thursday, raising concern that delays in giving shots could prolong the pandemic as cases of variants spread."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Only 10% of the region’s population have received one vaccine dose, and 4% have completed a full course, Hans Kluge said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“The rollout of these vaccines is unacceptably slow,” he said in a statement. “... We must speed up the process by ramping up manufacturing, reducing barriers to administering vaccines, and using every single vial we have in stock, now.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Europe was slower than Britain and the United States, not only to order vaccines last year from companies but also in approving them. Even once they were approved by the bloc, rates of vaccinations there have largely trailed behind British and U.S. efforts."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Kluge said new infections in Europe were rising in every age group except those aged over 80, a sign that the vaccinations that have gone to older groups are working but that the stuttering rollout was leaving younger people vulnerable."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“As variants of concern continue to spread and strain on hospitals grows, religious holidays are leading to increased mobility,” the WHO said in its statement."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Speeding up vaccination rollout is crucial.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In addition to tight supplies, squabbles over exports and delays by some vaccine manufacturers, and concerns over the safety of the AstraZeneca/Oxford vaccine after rare clotting events emerged have also curbed vaccination momentum."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Some countries are still not giving the British-Swedish company’s shots and others, including Germany, are restricting them to people over 60 years old."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Regulators and the WHO have declared that the shot’s benefits outweigh risks and continue to study the clotting incidents."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: CanSinoBIO says COVID-19 shot may be less effective over time, booster shot promising
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: China's CanSino Biologics Inc said the efficacy rate for its single-dose COVID-19 vaccine may fall over time although it should still have a rate of 50% or more five to six months after inoculation.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"BEIJING China’s CanSino Biologics Inc said the efficacy rate for its single-dose COVID-19 vaccine may fall over time although it should still have a rate of 50% or more five to six months after inoculation."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"A second shot given to trial participants six months after their first injection could offer substantial protection, Zhu Tao, CanSinoBIO’s chief scientific officer, said in an online presentation late on Wednesday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“A booster shot six months later led to a seven times to 10-times increase in neutralising antibody levels, so we expect in this case efficacy could reach over 90%,” Zhu said, though he cautioned more clinical trial data was needed for more precise estimates."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The company in February reported interim data that showed the shot was 68.83% effective at preventing symptomatic COVID-19 disease two weeks after vaccination but the rate fell to 65.28% after four weeks."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The February data reflected a shorter time span after the inoculation, Zhu said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The vaccine has been approved in China, Pakistan, Hungary and Mexico."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"CanSinoBIO is also planning a clinical trial in China for an inhaled version of the vaccine."}]

test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: The governor of Japan's Osaka prefecture has called for the cancellation of the Olympic torch relay in its largest city amid a sharp rise in COVID-19 cases, presenting an early test to organisers as they plan for the Games during the pandemic.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"TOKYO The governor of Japan’s Osaka prefecture has called for the cancellation of the Olympic torch relay in its largest city amid a sharp rise in COVID-19 cases, presenting an early test to organisers as they plan for the Games during the pandemic."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Osaka Governor Hirofumi Yoshimura said on Thursday the torch relay in the city should be cancelled and he wanted to have discussions with the Tokyo organising committee on the matter."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Prime Minister Yoshihide Suga told reporters he thought the decision had already been made."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“I understand Osaka has been cancelled as a result of talks between Tokyo Olympic organisers and the torch relay committee in Osaka,” Suga told reporters."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"But the Tokyo organising committee denied there had been such a decision."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“We will continue to hold close discussions with the Osaka prefectural authorities regarding the implementation of the Olympic Torch Relay, and strive to announce the outcome as soon as possible,” Tokyo organisers said in an emailed comment."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The relay began last week in Fukushima and is being seen as the first major test of the Games in holding a large-scale event while implementing stringent health protocols."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Around 10,000 runners will carry the torch through the country’s 47 prefectures over 121 days."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Tokyo Olympics organisers require roadside spectators to wear masks, practise social distancing and not cheer out loud to prevent the spread of the novel coronavirus, and there have been no reports so far of infections arising from the relay."},{"type":"heading","content":"EMERGENCY MEASURES"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Osaka, however, is battling a resurgence in infections."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Japan’s government on Thursday said it would impose emergency measures such as shorter business hours and asking people to work from home in the western Japan prefecture and two other areas to halt the rise in cases."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Those measures are scheduled to last for a month, until May 5, coinciding with the relay which is scheduled to go through Osaka on April 13-14."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“I think we need to have talks with the city of Osaka, but personally I think the torch relay in Osaka city should be cancelled,” Osaka Governor Yoshimura told reporters."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Officials in Nagano, also worried about a rise in infections, decided to bar spectators from parts of the torch relay as it passed through their prefecture on Thursday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Although Japan has been affected by the pandemic less severely than the United States and Europe, its vaccination campaign is off to a slow start while some prefectures are seeing an uptick in new infections."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Most Japanese oppose holding the Games this summer during the pandemic, surveys have shown."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Olympic organisers last month decided to bar international spectators from the Games, and this month are due to decide on the maximum capacity for spectators in venues."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Olympics, postponed by a year because of the pandemic, are scheduled to take place from July 23 to Aug. 8 and the Paralympics from Aug. 24 to Sept. 5."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Poland's Mabion aims to produce Novavax vaccine for Europe from third quarter
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Poland's Mabion aims to start production of U.S. firm Novavax's coronavirus vaccine for Europe from the third quarter, representatives of the biotechnology company said.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"WARSAW Poland’s Mabion aims to start production of U.S. firm Novavax’s coronavirus vaccine for Europe from the third quarter, representatives of the biotechnology company said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Mabion and Novavax last month signed a framework deal on the transfer of COVID-19 vaccine technology to Mabion’s plant in central Poland, which was designed to produce a rare diseases drug yet to be registered."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“The production of our core product is much more complicated (than vaccine),” Mabion board member Adam Pietruszkiewicz told Reuters."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Mabion is adding equipment necessary to start Novavax vaccine production, not without problems, as access to such machines has been limited. It is taking advantage of Novavax’s strong negotiation position with equipment suppliers."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“We still have to buy some equipment intended solely for the production of vaccines. However, our main machine park is ready. After completing this process, we should enter the commercial production phase at the beginning of the second half of the year,” Pietruszkiewicz said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Mabion would produce the active substance of the COVID-19 vaccine in the form of a recombinant virus protein. The active ingredient will be sent in 10 litre bags to a company in Germany, where the fill and finish will take place."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Typically, companies that specialise in the production of recombinant proteins very rarely have bottling lines with significant capacity. As a rule, these are specialised companies that have the infrastructure to fill vials in large quantities in a short time,” Mabion management board member Slawomir Jaros said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“The product will be distributed in Europe,” Mabion representatives added."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Mabion, which will be one of three Novavax’s vaccine producers in the European Union, has not revealed the size of the production, but said its 2,500 litre bioreactor is one of the largest in Europe."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Mabion and Novavax have not yet signed a final commercial agreement, but initial financial conditions have been agreed, the Polish company said."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Exclusive: EU seeks 10 million AstraZeneca vaccines from India to meet shortfall - Indian source
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: The European Union has asked India to allow it to buy 10 million doses of AstraZeneca's COVID-19 vaccine from Serum Institute of India, a government official told Reuters, the latest sign of growing pressure on Delhi to export more of its production to other countries.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"NEW DELHI The European Union has asked India to allow it to buy 10 million doses of AstraZeneca’s COVID-19 vaccine from Serum Institute of India, a government official told Reuters, the latest sign of growing pressure on Delhi to export more of its production to other countries."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The EU wants the doses from Serum, the world’s largest vaccine maker, to offset supply shortfalls from AstraZeneca’s European plants and speed up the bloc’s vaccine roll-out."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Any quick approval of the EU request is unlikely, however, with India scrambling to expand its own domestic vaccination drive, said the Indian government official, who asked not to be named as the discussions are private."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Britain is also pressuring India to export the second half of 10 million doses it had ordered from Serum, the source said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Serum was originally supposed to produce the AstraZeneca vaccine only for low and medium-income countries."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“The EU ambassador wrote a letter, saying, please give us (export) approvals,” said the source, adding the letter was sent around two weeks ago."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Serum, AstraZeneca and India’s foreign ministry did not respond to requests for comment. A spokeswoman for the EU Commission said the Commission had no immediate comment."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"India, however, has said that it is now focused on expanding its own immunisation drive as COVID-19 cases have surged since March."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Its decision to focus on its domestic needs, which came after the government was criticised at home for shipping tens of millions of doses overseas, will also affect the WHO-backed global network for vaccine distribution, known as COVAX. The network aims to secure COVID-19 vaccines primarily for dozens of poorer nations."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Production glitches have slowed vaccinations for the 450 million people in the 27-nation EU. The bloc's per capita immunisation lags that of countries such as Israel, the United Kingdom and the United States, according to the website Our World in Data \u003ca href=\"https://ourworldindata.org/covid-vaccinations\"\u003ehere\u003c/a\u003e."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"India has so far exported 64 million vaccine doses to 83 countries, and administered the same number of doses at home. Its inoculation drive expanded from Thursday to include everyone above the age of 45, which is expected to raise vaccine demand substantially."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"India has reported 12.22 million cases of the coronavirus, the third highest number globally after the United States and Brazil. It has recorded nearly 163,000 deaths from COVID-19."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Sudden extension of vaccine eligibility sows confusion in Poland
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Polish health care was plunged into confusion on Thursday after a surprise overnight decision to widen eligibility for COVID-19 vaccines triggered the crash of an online registration system, just as new infections soared to a new daily high.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"WARSAW (Reuters) -Polish health care was plunged into confusion on Thursday after a surprise overnight decision to widen eligibility for COVID-19 vaccines triggered the crash of an online registration system, just as new infections soared to a new daily high."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The incident left Polish doctors temporarily unable to prescribe drugs for non-coronavirus ailments, immunologist Pawel Grzesiowski told Reuters."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"It played out against the backdrop of a health service stretched to its limits by spiralling coronavirus case numbers that have left hospitals in some Polish regions on the brink of running out of ventilators."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Poland reported a fresh 24-hour record of 35,251 new COVID-19 cases on Thursday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The outage of the online registration system left doctors wondering if they had to postpone scheduled vaccinations, and wrongfooted people who had rushed to take advantage of an extension of eligibility to everyone over 40."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“These people already have appointments and now they hear in the media that these dates will be changed,” said Grzesiowski."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“There is colossal chaos, but also frustration, because people want to be vaccinated..., and now they hear that they will not get it.” People in Poland and many other European Union nations have been exasperated by a slow roll-out of vaccines."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Faced with a public outcry, the prime minister’s top aide, who is in charge of vaccinations, apologised for the system crash. “We should have communicated better about the system failure,” Michal Dworczyk told reporters."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Unfortunately...that didn’t happen, apologies are in order and in the space of a few hours the system will return to being fully functional.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Dworczyk also said that people in their 40s had mistakenly been given appointments in April. He said that they would be offered appointments in May instead."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"He had earlier said people aged 40-60 who had declared their readiness to be vaccinated had been sent referrals overnight due to slowing rates of registration among the over 60s."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Robert Biedron, a politician from the opposition Left grouping, was among many who expressed their dismay."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“That feeling when you think it’s April Fools, but it’s just another day of PiS in power,” he wrote on Twitter, referring to the ruling conservative nationalist Law and Justice party."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Having introduced further restrictions to limit the spread of the virus in March, Prime Minister Mateusz Morawiecki said on Thursday the state’s support scheme for the economy would be raised by around 30 billion zlotys ($7.63 billion)."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"More than 2 million of Poland’s 38 million people have received two doses of vaccine to date."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: UK data show good immune response in over 80s after 2-dose Pfizer COVID-19 shot
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Some 98% of 80 to 96 year-olds who had two doses of Pfizer's coronavirus vaccine had a strong antibody immune response, adding to evidence that it can help protect those most at risk of severe or fatal COVID-19, UK data showed on Thursday.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"LONDON Some 98% of 80 to 96 year-olds who had two doses of Pfizer’s coronavirus vaccine had a strong antibody immune response, adding to evidence that it can help protect those most at risk of severe or fatal COVID-19, UK data showed on Thursday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"A real-world study of 100 elderly people in Britain also found that participants who had previously been infected with the SARS-CoV-2 virus had a peak antibody response after just one dose of the Pfizer vaccine, and this response remained high after their second dose."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Paul Moss and Helen Parry, respectively a professor and a clinical lecturer at Birmingham University who co-led the study, said the high levels of antibodies detected were very reassuring, particularly since the antibody response was strong right up to the oldest participants at age 96."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“We were surprised, and very pleased,” Moss told reporters at a briefing about the findings. “But, of course, this does go with the excellent clinical protection that we’re seeing with the vaccine - so it does correlate.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Pfizer and its co-developer BioNTech said earlier on Thursday that updated clinical trial data showed their vaccine is around 91% effective at preventing COVID-19 cases."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Moss’s and Parry’s UK study involved 100 people aged 80-96 who were living independently and not in care homes, and who received two doses of the Pfizer COVID-19 vaccine three weeks apart. They were immunised before a UK policy change to extend the gap between COVID-19 vaccine doses to up to 12 weeks."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Immune measurements were taken two weeks after the second dose, the researchers said. The results have not been peer-reviewed by other scientists."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In laboratory tests, the researchers found the SARS-CoV-2 virus was strongly neutralised in serum from blood samples taken from participants."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"When tested against a mutated version of the virus called P.1 that was first discovered in Brazil, the levels of neutralisation reduced 14-fold, Parry said, but still showed the shot “retains broad efficacy” against this variant."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: German health minister confident "enough people" willing to take AZ shot
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: The AstraZeneca coronavirus vaccine's proven effectiveness means there will be no problem finding enough people willing to take it, German Health Minister Jens Spahn said.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"BERLIN The AstraZeneca coronavirus vaccine’s proven effectiveness means there will be no problem finding enough people willing to take it, German Health Minister Jens Spahn said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“I am certain we will find enough people willing to take the AstraZeneca vaccine because the protection it offers is good,” he told reporters on Thursday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Reports of extremely rare, but severe, side-effects after the vaccine was administered have prompted authorities in several countries including Germany to recommend that the shot not be used on younger people."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: India launches biggest vaccination drive yet against a surging coronavirus
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: India began vaccinating tens of thousands of people above the age of 45 on Thursday in its biggest push yet against a surging coronavirus that has hit the highest daily count since early October, officials said.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"NEW DELHI India began vaccinating tens of thousands of people above the age of 45 on Thursday in its biggest push yet against a surging coronavirus that has hit the highest daily count since early October, officials said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The world’s second most populous country aims to immunise 400 million people after expanding the programme, which had been restricted to the over-60s and people with serious health conditions, said a government official."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Our requirement is 400 million people to be vaccinated. That is our minimum requirement, our target,” the source, who did not wish to be identified, told Reuters."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Right now we are dealing with an emergency situation. Whatever we have, we will use it,” the source said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Anxious people lined up early at New Delhi’s Max hospital to get shots of the Oxford-AstraZeneca vaccine produced by the Serum Institute of India, the world’s biggest maker of vaccines."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“We have been saying from the beginning, everywhere and on social media, that please open up the vaccination programme, let everyone get it and be free from tension,” said Madhav Singh Rathore, 53, a salesman at a clothes store, who sat among a line of people waiting to get the injection."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"India kicked off its innoculation programme in January focused on health workers and then the elderly, saying it wanted to cover the most vulnerable first."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"‘FROM BAD TO WORSE’"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"It also shipped millions of doses of the vaccine to neighbouring countries and then across the world as part of a diplomatic initiative to win friends, but of late this has prompted criticism that people at home were being neglected."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Adding to the pressure on the government, the daily rise in cases has quadrupled in the space of a month as most of India has reopened for business and travel curbs have been lifted."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“The situation is going from bad to worse” V.K. Paul, the top COVID-19 adviser to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, said this week."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Data released by the health ministry on Thursday showed 72,330 new COVID-19 infections, the highest since Oct. 11. Deaths stand at 162,927."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"India’s overall caseload stood at 12.22 million, making it the third worst affected globally, behind the United States and Brazil."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Despite the second wave of infections, hundreds of Hindu devotes gathered on the banks of the river Ganges in the northern town of Haridwar to take a holy dip on the first day of a month-long ‘Kumbh Mela, or the pitcher festival."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Mother Ganga will protect us and destroy all the negative impact of COVID-19 in the world. However, we should be cautious and take precautions,” said Sunanda, a devotee."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Local authorities have said anyone coming from the 12 states where cases are rising will have to produce a negative COVID-19 test before being allowed to bathe in the river."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Biden turns to NASCAR, NAACP to convince people to take vaccines
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: President Joe Biden is enlisting the help of groups as varied as NASCAR and the NAACP as part of a multi-billion dollar effort to convince Americans to take COVID-19 vaccines.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"WASHINGTON President Joe Biden is enlisting the help of groups as varied as NASCAR and the NAACP as part of a multi-billion dollar effort to convince Americans to take COVID-19 vaccines."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Biden is trying to control a raging pandemic that has killed 550,000 Americans by obtaining enough vaccine for the country’s 330 million residents by May."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Yet, with a quarter of Americans reluctant to get vaccinated, filling the country’s vaccine shortage may not be enough."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Twenty-seven percent of Americans said they were not interested in getting vaccinated, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll this month, a figure that has not budged in months."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Vice President Kamala Harris and other administration officials will hold an online event on Wednesday bringing together churches, native tribal leaders, civil rights activists and sports leagues like Major League Baseball, Major League Soccer, the National Football League and NASCAR."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The organizations are founding members of the administration’s COVID-19 Community Corps, an effort to encourage people to take vaccines from trusted sources."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The administration is also pumping $10 billion to increase vaccine access in vulnerable communities, including public outreach. They are also launching a multi-million dollar advertising campaign in English and Spanish to urge people to seek information from the government about the vaccines and get the shot when they qualify."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Biden has set a goal of getting 200 million vaccine shots in people’s arms in his first 100 days in office."}]

test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"WASHINGTON President Joe Biden is enlisting the help of groups as varied as NASCAR and the NAACP as part of a multi-billion dollar effort to convince Americans to take COVID-19 vaccines."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Biden is trying to control a raging pandemic that has killed 550,000 Americans by obtaining enough vaccine for the country’s 330 million residents by May."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Yet, with a quarter of Americans reluctant to get vaccinated, filling the country’s vaccine shortage may not be enough."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Twenty-seven percent of Americans said they were not interested in getting vaccinated, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll this month, a figure that has not budged in months."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Vice President Kamala Harris and other administration officials will hold an online event on Wednesday bringing together churches, native tribal leaders, civil rights activists and sports leagues like Major League Baseball, Major League Soccer, the National Football League and NASCAR."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The organizations are founding members of the administration’s COVID-19 Community Corps, an effort to encourage people to take vaccines from trusted sources."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The administration is also pumping $10 billion to increase vaccine access in vulnerable communities, including public outreach. They are also launching a multi-million dollar advertising campaign in English and Spanish to urge people to seek information from the government about the vaccines and get the shot when they qualify."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Biden has set a goal of getting 200 million vaccine shots in people’s arms in his first 100 days in office."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Sweden to offer all adults first COVID shot by Aug 15, later than planned
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: A shortage of vaccines means Sweden expects to offer all adults a first dose of a vaccine against COVID-19 by August 15, later than its original plan of the end of June, officals said on Thursday.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"STOCKHOLM A shortage of vaccines means Sweden expects to offer all adults a first dose of a vaccine against COVID-19 by August 15, later than its original plan of the end of June, officals said on Thursday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“As the delivery forecast looks today, everyone over 18 should be able to have their first dose of the vaccine at the latest by August 15,” Marie Morell, health care chief of the Swedish Association of Local Authorities and Regions told reporters at a news conference."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Health Minister Lena Hallengren said the delay was due to a shortage of vaccines and changes in recommendations over how the vaccines are used."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Mini-break capital Prague faces tourist-free Easter - again
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Jakub Ricica's traditional Czech pub 'Deminka', located just behind the National Museum and a short stroll from dozens of hotels, is a magnet for the flocks of tourists who descend on Prague every year for the Easter break.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"PRAGUE Jakub Ricica’s traditional Czech pub ‘Deminka’, located just behind the National Museum and a short stroll from dozens of hotels, is a magnet for the flocks of tourists who descend on Prague every year for the Easter break."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"But for a second year running, the wooden chairs sit atop the tables, the beer mugs are stacked on the bar and the Pilsner taps remain dry ahead of what would normally be one of the biggest money-making weekends of the year."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Easter is usually the first weekend in Prague where things start to get really busy, and then it just keeps going,” said Ricica, who estimates that tourists generate about 60 percent of the revenue for his pub, which was founded in 1882."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“We don’t even look at this year anymore. We hope 2022 will be year zero.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Prague’s location in the heart of Europe, along with its fairy-tale centre of cobbled streets, Baroque architecture and castle perched on a hill overlooking the city, have made it a popular destination for long weekends such as Easter."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Czech capital welcomed more than 9 million tourists in 2019, making it the fourth most visited city in Europe after London, Paris and Rome, according to Euromonitor International."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"‘IT’S DESTROYING THEM’"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The city’s economy also depends on people spending money in its restaurants, pubs and hotels. Prague accounts for 60 percent of the Czech Republic’s tourism income, Mayor Zdenek Hrib said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“We see the big impact it has on Prague’s economy and on entrepreneurs providing services in this industry,” Hrib told Reuters, adding that 270,000 foreign tourists came to Prague during the Easter holiday in 2019 but close to zero this year. “It’s destroying them.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"With travel restrictions and closed borders across swathes of Europe, business owners say only vaccination campaigns will enable people to travel freely again."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"At the five-star President Hotel sitting on the Vltava river, director Veronika Fajcikova said that at this time of year the hotel, shuttered since October, would normally run close to full capacity, with guests coming from around the world for the busy holiday weekend."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"While the staff has used the down time to make upgrades including a rooftop bar, Fajcikova said there were no plans to re-open until the foreign tourists return."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“All hotels in Prague are usually sold out and the rates are high for Easter,” she said in the eerily quiet and empty hotel."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“After the low season you welcome the spring to come and business to increase. Now we just want to survive.”"}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: China's TopRidge Pharma to produce Sputnik V vaccine, Russia's RDIF says
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: China's TopRidge Pharma has agreed to produce more than 100 million doses of Russia's two-shot Sputnik V vaccine against COVID-19, Russia's RDIF sovereign wealth fund said on Thursday.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"MOSCOW China’s TopRidge Pharma has agreed to produce more than 100 million doses of Russia’s two-shot Sputnik V vaccine against COVID-19, Russia’s RDIF sovereign wealth fund said on Thursday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The fund, which markets Sputnik V globally, said the two sides planned to cooperate on clinical trials in China and to promote its use there."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"TopRidge Pharma will be able to distribute the vaccine in mainland China, Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan, RDIF said in a statement."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Germany needs to secure booster shots for next year: health minister
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Germany needs to secure more output capacity with leading COVID-19 vaccine makers because repeat shots will likely be needed from next year, and Germany would go it alone if other European Union members fail to see the urgency, its health minister said.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"FRANKFURT Germany needs to secure more output capacity with leading COVID-19 vaccine makers because repeat shots will likely be needed from next year, and Germany would go it alone if other European Union members fail to see the urgency, its health minister said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“For now we don’t know how long protection will last,” Jens Spahn said in an online press briefing."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Nobody can rule out the need for repeat shots for immune reinforcement. Therefore we should secure capacity within the European Union framework, if not done urgently, then nationally,” he added."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The emergence of new variants has added urgency and talks with some manufacturers for 2022 supply contracts had already begun, he added."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Hong Kong to resume use of BioNTech COVID-19 vaccines on April 5
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Hong Kong authorities said on Thursday they would resume the use of BioNTech's COVID-19 vaccine next Monday after abruptly halting inoculations nine days ago due to defective packaging.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"HONG KONG (Reuters) -Hong Kong authorities said on Thursday they would resume the use of BioNTech’s COVID-19 vaccine next Monday after abruptly halting inoculations nine days ago due to defective packaging."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"A 300,000 dose batch is due to arrive in Hong Kong on Friday that was produced and packaged at a different plant to the two batches whose use was halted by authorities."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The announcement comes as the city’s government seeks to convince residents to get vaccinated after a sluggish take-up due to dwindling confidence in a rival vaccine from China’s Sinovac and fears of adverse reactions."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“We want to enhance public confidence in the vaccine program,” Patrick Nip, secretary for the Civil Service, told a briefing on Thursday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"With low levels of infection in the city, many people feel less urgency to get a vaccination quickly and some residents have criticised the lack of data available for the Sinovac vaccine compared to the BioNTech offering."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Prior to its suspension, the number of Hong Kong residents booking the BioNTech shot was more than double the number for the Sinovac shot, according to government figures."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Hong Kong government said BioNTech was still conducting investigations into the previous two batches and it would wait for a final conclusion before using them. It added that the safety and efficacy of the vaccine has not been affected."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Around 7% of Hong Kong’s 7.5 million population has been vaccinated, one third of which have taken the BioNTech vaccine."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The BioNTech vaccine is distributed in Hong Kong and Macau via a partnership with China’s Fosun Pharma, while BioNTech partners with Pfizer in markets outside greater China."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The former British colony has recorded around 11,400 coronavirus infections and 205 deaths."}]

test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"HONG KONG (Reuters) -Hong Kong authorities said on Thursday they would resume the use of BioNTech’s COVID-19 vaccine next Monday after abruptly halting inoculations nine days ago due to defective packaging."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"A 300,000 dose batch is due to arrive in Hong Kong on Friday that was produced and packaged at a different plant to the two batches whose use was halted by authorities."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The announcement comes as the city’s government seeks to convince residents to get vaccinated after a sluggish take-up due to dwindling confidence in a rival vaccine from China’s Sinovac and fears of adverse reactions."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“We want to enhance public confidence in the vaccine program,” Patrick Nip, secretary for the Civil Service, told a briefing on Thursday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"With low levels of infection in the city, many people feel less urgency to get a vaccination quickly and some residents have criticised the lack of data available for the Sinovac vaccine compared to the BioNTech offering."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Prior to its suspension, the number of Hong Kong residents booking the BioNTech shot was more than double the number for the Sinovac shot, according to government figures."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Hong Kong government said BioNTech was still conducting investigations into the previous two batches and it would wait for a final conclusion before using them. It added that the safety and efficacy of the vaccine has not been affected."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Around 7% of Hong Kong’s 7.5 million population has been vaccinated, one third of which have taken the BioNTech vaccine."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The BioNTech vaccine is distributed in Hong Kong and Macau via a partnership with China’s Fosun Pharma, while BioNTech partners with Pfizer in markets outside greater China."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The former British colony has recorded around 11,400 coronavirus infections and 205 deaths."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Russia reports 9,169 new COVID-19 cases, 383 deaths
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Russia reported 9,169 new COVID-19 cases on Thursday, including 2,151 in Moscow, pushing the infection tally in the country to 4,554,264 since the pandemic began.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"MOSCOW Russia reported 9,169 new COVID-19 cases on Thursday, including 2,151 in Moscow, pushing the infection tally in the country to 4,554,264 since the pandemic began."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The government coronavirus taskforce said that 383 people had died in the last 24 hours, taking Russia’s death toll to 99,233."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Russia’s statistics service, which is keeping a separate tally, has reported a much higher toll and said that more than 200,000 Russians died of COVID-19 through January."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Only 1 in 5 with COVID symptoms in UK seek test: study
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Only one person in five in Britain with COVID-19 symptoms has sought or would seek a test, according to a study which found a link between people on low pay and poor adherence to the government's rules.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"LONDON Only one person in five in Britain with COVID-19 symptoms has sought or would seek a test, according to a study which found a link between people on low pay and poor adherence to the government’s rules."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Eighteen percent of participants in the study published in the British Medical Journal said they got or would get a test after showing symptoms and 42.5% would fully adhere to isolation rules, according to the study."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“This is such an important part of any government’s pandemic control measures,” one of the reports authors - Susan Michie, a University College London health psychology professor - told BBC Radio."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“I think given that new cases a day are stuck at around 4,000 this is a ... real area where we could begin to make progress.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Michie said people told researchers they did not isolate because they needed to leave home for provisions or caring responsibilities or to go to work, often in low-paid jobs."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"She said developing countries such as Vietnam were doing a good job at providing financial support to help people follow isolation rules."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Britain has earmarked 37 billion pounds ($50.87 billion) for spending on its test and trace system over two years. Lawmakers said last month that it had failed in its key goals."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The survey was based on responses from 53,880 people - some of whom had contracted COVID-19 - between March 2 last year and January 27 2021."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"($1 = 0.7273 pounds)"}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Peak of French COVID-19 wave could be within ten days: Veran
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: France could hit the peak of the third wave of the COVID-19 pandemic in seven to 10 days with the new restrictive measures announced on Wednesday by French President Emmanuel Macron, Health Minister Olivier Veran told France Inter radio.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"PARIS France could hit the peak of the third wave of the COVID-19 pandemic in seven to 10 days with the new restrictive measures announced on Wednesday by French President Emmanuel Macron, Health Minister Olivier Veran told France Inter radio."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Macron ordered France into its third national lockdown and said schools would close for three weeks as he sought to push back the third wave of COVID-19 infections that threatens to overwhelm hospitals."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“We could reach a peak of the epidemic in seven to 10 days if all goes according to plan”, Veran said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Then we need two extra weeks to reach a peak in intensive care units (ICUs) that could occur at the end of April.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Daily new COVID-19 infections in France have doubled since February to average nearly 40,000. The number of COVID-19 patients in intensive care breached 5,000 this week, exceeding the peak hit during the six-week second lockdown enforced late last year."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Japan announces emergency measures in Osaka area to curb COVID-19 cases
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Japan's government said on Thursday it will impose emergency measures, such as shorter business hours and asking people to work from home and refrain from activities like karaoke, in the western region of Osaka to halt a rebound in COVID-19 cases.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"TOKYO (Reuters) -Japan’s government said on Thursday it will impose emergency measures, such as shorter business hours and asking people to work from home and refrain from activities like karaoke, in the western region of Osaka to halt a rebound in COVID-19 cases."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Osaka governor Hirofumi Yoshimura said Olympic torch events in the prefecture’s main city should be cancelled, a day after he raised alarm about an emerging fourth wave of infections."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The infection control measures will cover the prefectures of Osaka, Hyogo, and Miyagi and will last from April 5 until May 5, said Economy Minister Yasutoshi Nishimura, who also heads the nation’s COVID-19 response."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"A final decision on enacting the measures will be made at a task force meeting headed by Prime Minister Yoshihide Suga this afternoon."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"New infections in Osaka have exceeded those of the much larger metropolis of Tokyo in recent days."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Osaka prefecture reported 599 new cases on Wednesday, close to the record of 654 in early January when the nation was gripped in its third and most deadly wave of the pandemic. Tokyo reported 475 new infections today (April 1), the most since Feb. 10."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The new measures are based on a revised infection control law and can be applied to a narrower area than a state of emergency, which Suga declared for most of the country in early January."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The controls allow regional governments to order businesses to shorten hours and to impose fines of 200,000 yen ($1,806.52) or publish the names of those that do not comply. Additionally, residents are being asked to telework and to refrain from activities like karaoke."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Osaka emerged early from the state of emergency, but then experienced a sharp rebound in cases toward the end of March."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“In Osaka in particular, the number of infected individuals in their 20 and 30 is increasing as people continue to go out at night,” Chief Cabinet Secretary Katsunobu Kato said on Thursday. “Reports of mutant strains are also increasing, and the contagion is expected to continue.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"($1 = 110.7100 yen)"}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Vietnam receives first batch of vaccines under COVAX scheme
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Vietnam received 811,000 doses of AstraZeneca's COVID-19 vaccines on Thursday, its first batch of vaccines under the global COVAX scheme, following a week-long delay caused by limited supply.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"HANOI Vietnam received 811,000 doses of AstraZeneca’s COVID-19 vaccines on Thursday, its first batch of vaccines under the global COVAX scheme, following a week-long delay caused by limited supply."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Southeast Asian country, which began its coronavirus vaccination programme last month, is aiming to secure 30 million doses in total via the COVAX vaccine-sharing facility."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Thursday’s delivery took Vietnam’s number of AstraZeneca doses to nearly 930,000 so far, but the country is looking to diversify its procurement from more sources, including Pfizer, Johnson \u0026amp; Johnson, Moderna, China’s Sinovac and Russia’s vaccine, Sputnik V."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In a meeting with health minister Nguyen Thanh Long, Russia’s embassy in Hanoi on Wednesday offered to help Vietnam manufacture Sputnik V locally, the health ministry said in a statement."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Long also said Vietnam would approve the Chinese vaccine within weeks, after Sinovac submits the required documents. Vietnam is among only a few countries in Asia yet to use the Chinese vaccine."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Vietnam has been praised for its record in containing the virus through mass testing and tracing and strict quarantining, which has kept its cases to just 2,603, with 35 deaths. Nearly 50,000 people have been vaccinated."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Thursday’s shipment, originally of 1.37 million doses, was expected to be delivered by March 25 but was delayed due to supply shortages, according to the United Nations’ children’s fund, UNICEF, which is handling the COVAX rollout in Vietnam."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Vietnam’s first domestically developed COVID-19 vaccine, called Nanocovax, is expected to be put into use in 2022."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Four Vietnamese companies are engaged in vaccine research and production and two are at the human trial stage."}]

files.filesDescription: A health worker holds a vial of the vaccine as Vietnam starts its official rollout of AstraZeneca's coronavirus disease (COVID-19) vaccine for health workers, at Hai Duong Hospital for Tropical Diseases, Hai Duong province, Vietnam, March 8, 2021. Thanh Hue

test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"HANOI Vietnam received 811,000 doses of AstraZeneca’s COVID-19 vaccines on Thursday, its first batch of vaccines under the global COVAX scheme, following a week-long delay caused by limited supply."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Southeast Asian country, which began its coronavirus vaccination programme last month, is aiming to secure 30 million doses in total via the COVAX vaccine-sharing facility."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Thursday’s delivery took Vietnam’s number of AstraZeneca doses to nearly 930,000 so far, but the country is looking to diversify its procurement from more sources, including Pfizer, Johnson \u0026amp; Johnson, Moderna, China’s Sinovac and Russia’s vaccine, Sputnik V."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In a meeting with health minister Nguyen Thanh Long, Russia’s embassy in Hanoi on Wednesday offered to help Vietnam manufacture Sputnik V locally, the health ministry said in a statement."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Long also said Vietnam would approve the Chinese vaccine within weeks, after Sinovac submits the required documents. Vietnam is among only a few countries in Asia yet to use the Chinese vaccine."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Vietnam has been praised for its record in containing the virus through mass testing and tracing and strict quarantining, which has kept its cases to just 2,603, with 35 deaths. Nearly 50,000 people have been vaccinated."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Thursday’s shipment, originally of 1.37 million doses, was expected to be delivered by March 25 but was delayed due to supply shortages, according to the United Nations’ children’s fund, UNICEF, which is handling the COVAX rollout in Vietnam."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Vietnam’s first domestically developed COVID-19 vaccine, called Nanocovax, is expected to be put into use in 2022."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Four Vietnamese companies are engaged in vaccine research and production and two are at the human trial stage."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Ukraine reports record daily COVID-19 deaths for second day in a row
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Ukraine registered a record daily high of 421 coronavirus-related deaths over 24 hours for the second day in a row, health minister Maksym Stepanov said on Thursday.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"KYIV (Reuters) -Ukraine registered a record daily high of 421 coronavirus-related deaths over 24 hours for the second day in a row, health minister Maksym Stepanov said on Thursday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"On Wednesday, Ukraine reported 407 deaths and Stepanov told the government infections were likely to rise further over the next one to two weeks."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Stepanov said 17,569 new infections were reported over the past day and a record high 5,160 people were hospitalised. On Wednesday, Ukraine reported 11,226 new cases, far below the record 18,132 cases last week."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Ukrainian capital Kyiv, which is still leading in the number of new infections, will impose a strict lockdown from April 5, restricting public transport, closing all schools and kindergartens."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The city has already banned public events, closed cafes and restaurants in an attempt to stop a new wave of disease."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Many Ukrainian regions have also imposed strict lockdown."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Ukraine has reported a total of 1,691,737 coronavirus cases and 33,246 deaths."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Cuba vaunts 'technical sovereignty' in COVID battle
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Cuba's homegrown vaccine candidates have made headlines worldwide. Less well-known is its production of medical gear such as ventilators and CT scanners for the treatment of COVID-19 patients in a bid to achieve "technological sovereignty" during the pandemic.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"HAVANA Cuba’s homegrown vaccine candidates have made headlines worldwide. Less well-known is its production of medical gear such as ventilators and CT scanners for the treatment of COVID-19 patients in a bid to achieve “technological sovereignty” during the pandemic."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"During a tour of production facilities in Havana on Wednesday, officials touted the medical gear that had enabled them to save money and keep the mortality rate from COVID-19 low even as other countries had struggled to import such equipment."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Our country is saving money and could save many millions of dollars thanks to all the results of sovereignty we have achieved,” said Eduardo Martínez, head of state-run biopharmaceutical corporation BioCubaFarma."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Communist-run island nation has sought to develop such manufacturing in part in response to the decades-old U.S. trade embargo, tightened by former President Donald Trump, which hampers the import of medical equipment."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Daily coronavirus cases hit a new record of 1,051 on the island of 11 million inhabitants on Wednesday, bringing the total to more than 75,000. Deaths remain low at 424, one of the lowest rates per capita worldwide."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Cuba said late last year it had spent $100 million on confronting the pandemic so far, a strain on the economy that had already been suffering shortages of even basic goods such as medicine and food."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The country is on the brink of a possible major biopharmaceutical achievement, namely the development of a homegrown vaccine. Its most advanced candidate, currently in phase three trials, is called Sovereignty 2."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“The results we have had until now predict very satisfactory results and therefore we maintain that before year-end, our population will be immunized with the vaccines we are developing,” said Martinez."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Chinese city on border with Myanmar reports more COVID cases
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Health authorities in China's southwestern Yunnan province on Thursday reported six new COVID-19 cases in Ruili amid efforts to contain a fresh outbreak in the city bordering Myanmar.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"SHANGHAI Health authorities in China’s southwestern Yunnan province on Thursday reported six new COVID-19 cases in Ruili amid efforts to contain a fresh outbreak in the city bordering Myanmar."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Home quarantine, restrictions on exiting the city, and mass testing started on Wednesday after authorities reported an outbreak of six COVID cases and three asymptomatic patients - those infected but do not show symptoms."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Two of the latest six COVID patients and 10 of the 23 new asymptomatic patients in Ruili are Myanmar citizens, the Health Commission of Yunnan Province said in a statement."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Health authorities in Yunnan have yet to identify how the latest cluster started."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Ruili is a key transit point for Yunnan province, which has struggled to monitor its rugged 4,000 km (2,485-mile) border with Laos, Myanmar and Vietnam for illegal immigration amid a wave of unauthorised crossings last year by those seeking a haven from the COVID-19 pandemic."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Ruili rolled out similar COVID-19 curbs last year after imported infections from Myanmar were detected."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"For all of mainland China, a total of 16 COVID cases and 42 asymptomatic cases were reported on March 31, the National Health Commission (NHC) said in a separate statement on Thursday. The Ruili cases accounted for all of the new locally transmitted infections reported by the NHC."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"COVID-19 first emerged in the central Chinese city of Wuhan in late 2019 and brought the country to a virtual standstill in early 2020 before it took spread globally. The country has since recovered and new infections now stand at a fraction of what it saw at the height of the outbreak in February 2020."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The total number of confirmed COVID-19 cases in mainland China now stands at 90,217, while the death toll remained unchanged at 4,636."}]
