test_endpoint.articlesName: Canada's Ontario to go back into 28-day lockdown - reports
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: The Canadian province of Ontario, the country's most populous, will enter another lockdown on the weekend for 28 days, local media reported, as it grapples with rising COVID-19 cases and intensive care hospitalization rates.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"TORONTO, March 31 The Canadian province of Ontario, the country’s most populous, will enter another lockdown on the weekend for 28 days, local media reported, as it grapples with rising COVID-19 cases and intensive care hospitalization rates."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Canadian Broadcasting Corporation (CBC), citing unnamed sources, said the province’s premier would announce the new lockdown measures on Thursday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The new steps would still allow both essential and non-essential retailers to remain open, albeit with occupancy limits and schools would not be closed ahead of a spring break slated for April 12, the CBC said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Ontario, which also enacted a month-long lockdown in late December, has seen more than 2,000 cases a day for seven straight days to Wednesday and a record number of patients in intensive care."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Canadian health authorities are wrestling with a rise in cases driven by the spread of virus variants. The country has had a total of 982,116 COVID-19 cases and 22,959 deaths. (Writing by Amran Abocar Editing by Shri Navaratnam)"}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Pakistan court allows commercial sale of COVID-19 vaccine
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: A Pakistani court on Thursday ordered that a batch of the Russian Sputnik V COVID-19 vaccine imported by a private company be immediately made available to the public for sale, according to a court document and officials.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"KARACHI, Pakistan, April 1 A Pakistani court on Thursday ordered that a batch of the Russian Sputnik V COVID-19 vaccine imported by a private company be immediately made available to the public for sale, according to a court document and officials."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The government had argued that pricing issues should be settled first."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Any restriction relating to sale of the COVID-19 vaccine at this stage would be against the public interest because of its undisputed urgent need due to the crisis faced by the country,” a Sindh High Court judge said in an order on Thursday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Pakistan, largely reliant on the COVAX vaccine-sharing initiative, last month allowed private firms to import vaccines and agreed to exempt them from price caps, but later rescinded the exemption and said it would set maximum prices."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The decision threw the government and pharmaceutical companies into dispute, and stalled the commercial sale of the vaccine."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Thursday’s court order was passed in a case brought last week by M/S AGP Ltd, which imported 50,000 doses of Sputnik V on March 17."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"A senior official of AGP told Reuters that the company had asked the court to allow it to sell the vaccine at a price of 12,268 Pakistani rupees ($80.54) for a pack of two doses of Sputnik V."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"It was not immediately clear if this would be the price it would be marketed at, which is much higher than the initial government proposed price of 8,449 Pakistani rupees ($55.47)."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"AG Pharma had told the court it has cost the company $45 for a pack of two doses."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The court said it would hold further hearings to determine pricing, but said the sale of the vaccines should start immediately and, once a fair price was determined, any monetary difference could be recovered from the company at a later stage."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Pakistan is one of the first countries in the world to allow the commercial sale of COVID-19 vaccines. ($1 = 152.3200 Pakistani rupees) (Reporting by Syed Raza Hassan; Editing by Alex Richardson)"}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: RPT-China unlikely to wield U.S. bond weapon as tensions stay high
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: China is unlikely to pare its purchases of U.S. Treasuries significantly anytime soon as its foreign exchange reserves grow, even as trade and geopolitical tensions between Washington and Beijing remain high, analysts and investors said.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"NEW YORK (Reuters) -China is unlikely to pare its purchases of U.S. Treasuries significantly anytime soon as its foreign exchange reserves grow, even as trade and geopolitical tensions between Washington and Beijing remain high, analysts and investors said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The risk that China could slow its bond buying or sell from its more than $1 trillion portfolio is a subject of concern to investors as the two largest economies battle over trade tariffs, geopolitical tensions and human rights issues."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"U.S. President Joe Biden last week compared Chinese President Xi Jinping to Russian President Vladimir Putin, calling them both supporters of autocracy. But he said Washington was not looking for confrontation with China over differences on trade, Beijing’s rollback of democracy in Hong Kong, treatment of minority Uighurs and military buildup."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Concerns about relations come as Treasury yields jumped to one-year highs in March and new debt supply to finance government spending and a widening deficit surges to record highs, showing no signs of slowing."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"But analysts say it would be complicated for China to unload its bonds without hurting their value and creating losses for itself."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Despite everything we’ve seen in terms of the increase in tensions, we still haven’t seen China rapidly divest. It’s not a weapon they can use without hurting themselves,” said Matt Gertken, geopolitical strategist at BCA Research."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"If an issue like Hong Kong or Taiwan blows up, then China “may use Treasury securities as a signal,” Gertken said. In that case, however, other countries may buy Treasuries on concerns about global stability, which could boost demand for bonds as a safe haven, limiting the impact, he added."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"China’s foreign exchange reserves have grown in the last few months as the yuan has appreciated, and that has increased its investments in U.S. Treasuries, Morgan Stanley analyst Min Dai said in a recent report."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"China has seen a strong rebound in exports in recent months as it recovered from COVID-19 business shutdowns and imports of Chinese products in the European Union and the United States grew, thanks to fiscal stimulus measures."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The most recent government data showed China increased its holdings of U.S. Treasuries to $1.095 trillion in January, up from $1.054 trillion in October, though they remain below a peak of $1.32 trillion reached in 2013."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Japan is the largest foreign holder of U.S. debt, with $1.28 trillion in Treasuries in January. The Federal Reserve holds $4.92 trillion in Treasuries as of last week."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"China’s holdings are also shrinking on a percentage basis as the U.S. government debt supply expands and the Federal Reserve increasingly asserts itself as the main player in the market."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“It’s definitely something I think we have to be aware of but I’m not sure it’s as material as it used to be just given how large the debt stock is of the U.S.,” said Brian Kloss, a fixed income portfolio manager at Brandywine Global."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Outstanding U.S. debt has surged to $21.65 trillion as of year-end, from $17.19 trillion a year earlier and $8.29 trillion in 2010."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Another issue that would make it difficult for China to reduce its U.S. bond purchases is that few other markets are as liquid or low-risk as U.S. Treasuries."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"If it does sell bonds, any rise in yields could prove attractive to other investors as the bonds become relatively more attractive."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“As rates have backed up, it starts to become attractive to other foreign investors especially on a hedged basis, so they may step in to fill some of that void if China does back away,” said Kloss."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Fed is also expected to step in if bond yields rise to a point where they could harm U.S. economic growth."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Either way, “it’s just not a weapon China can use easily,” said Gertken. “China only owns about 5% of Treasuries, so they can move the needle but not much more than that.”"}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Dollar slides, consolidates recent gains, ahead of U.S. payrolls data
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: The dollar fell on Thursday, consolidating recent gains that pushed it to nearly three-year highs during the first quarter, but the outlook remained upbeat in the wake of improving economic prospects backed by the Biden government's more than $2 trillion stimulus plan.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"NEW YORK The dollar fell on Thursday, consolidating recent gains that pushed it to nearly three-year highs during the first quarter, but the outlook remained upbeat in the wake of improving economic prospects backed by the Biden government’s more than $2 trillion stimulus plan."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Investors are now looking to Friday’s non-farm payrolls report to confirm their positive view on the dollar and the economy."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The dollar gained 3.6% against a basket of six currencies in the first three months of the year, its best quarterly performance since June 2018, with investors betting on a swift and robust economic recovery."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“We’re seeing the U.S. growth outlook just crushing Europe’s,” said Edward Moya, senior market analyst, at online FX trading platform, OANDA."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“The Biden administration is not even three months on the job and it’s about to deliver its second multi-trillion-dollar stimulus package. We’ll probably see the U.S. run hot and that’s probably driving the rise in Treasury yields including the dollar.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"U.S. President Joe Biden announced on Wednesday his long- awaited $2 trillion-plus job plan, including $621 billion to rebuild infrastructure."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Meanwhile, U.S. data showed strong growth prospects."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"A report on the U.S. manufacturing sector showed a stronger-than-expected reading of 64.7 in March, the highest in more than 37 years. That was offset, though, by slowing construction spending, which fell 0.8% in February, and an increase in U.S. jobless claims in the latest week."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In afternoon trading, the dollar index slipped 0.3% to 92.933."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The dollar though slipped a bit after the jobless claims report, with claims of 719,000 in the week ended March 27."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The dollar index’s gains in the first quarter came as the euro, the biggest component in the index, struggled on concerns the euro zone’s recovery is being hampered by a third wave of COVID-19 infections."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"France’s President Emmanuel Macron ordered the country into its third national lockdown and said schools would close for three weeks. The euro zone also lags the United States in vaccination programs."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Sentiment toward Europe, though, received a boost when data showed euro zone monthly factory activity growth galloped at its fastest pace in the nearly 24-year history of a leading business survey."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The euro was last up 0.3% at $1.1768."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The dollar was down 0.1% against the yen at 110.61 yen, after ending March with its biggest monthly gain since November 2016. It rose as high as 110.97 on Wednesday, the highest in a year."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The U.S. non-farm payrolls report is the major data release this week, with economists expecting an increase of about 650,000 jobs in March."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Considering the recent price action, the risk of a selloff in the U.S. dollar is elevated if the jobs report fails to meet expectations,” said Matt Weller, global head of market research at FOREX.com and City Index."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“In that scenario, the beaten-down euro/dollar could have room to recover back toward its 200-day (exponential moving average) and the previous support level near $1.1830 through early next week.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In observance of Good Friday, Reuters will not be putting out market reports during the European hours."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Rising U.S. yields a villain in EM FX growth story, sell-off likely by end-June - Reuters poll
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Battered emerging market currencies will only pare some of their recent steep losses over the coming year, according to analysts polled by Reuters who said a sell-off was likely in the next three months with rising U.S. yields posing a big risk.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"BENGALURU/JOHANNESBURG Battered emerging market currencies will only pare some of their recent steep losses over the coming year, according to analysts polled by Reuters who said a sell-off was likely in the next three months with rising U.S. yields posing a big risk."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Having strengthened over 3% in 2020, an index of emerging market currencies erased nearly half of those gains in the last three months as reflation bets spurred by massive U.S. fiscal stimulus drove the dollar index to a four-month high."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"A majority of FX strategists in the March 26-31 Reuters poll said the dollar’s recent strength would be short-lived and stuck to their previous view that the greenback would weaken against emerging market currencies."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Still, most won’t recoup heavy losses made so far this year."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Amid the reflationary expectations pulsing through markets the outlook has become even more complicated. The single biggest risk is a destabilising rise in U.S. Treasury yields that impairs equity/credit markets, leading to incremental capital flight from EM markets and pressure on currencies,” said Jason Daw, head of emerging markets strategy at Societe Generale."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“There will be tactical long EM FX opportunities during periods of oversold conditions, but over a medium-term horizon, a neutral-to-bearish stance is warranted. At best, currencies will tread water and at worst resume their long-term depreciation trend.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"When asked about the likelihood of a sell-off in emerging market currencies in the next three months, nearly 60% of 53 FX strategists who answered an additional question said likely, including six who said very likely."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"That lines up with the findings of a separate Reuters poll of fixed income strategists who said another global bond market sell-off was likely in the next three months."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"For a graphic on Reuters Poll: Emerging market currencies outlook:"},{"type":"paragraph","content":""},{"type":"infographics","media_type":"static","content":"https://fingfx.thomsonreuters.com/gfx/polling/qzjpqlzbbvx/EMRG%20FX%20april.PNG"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Emerging market central banks have come under increasing pressure from global rising yields, weakening currencies and raising inflation strains. Policymakers in Russia delivered a surprise rate increase last month while in Brazil and Turkey they hiked by more than expected."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"But that was not expected to give any significant boost to currencies in less developed countries."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“The surprise rate hikes from Brazil, Russia and Turkey don’t change the picture that most EM central banks will stay dovish, providing less support for EMFX,” said James Lord, global head of EMFX at Morgan Stanley."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Turkey’s lira has been one of the worst performing emerging market currencies this year, behind only the Argentine peso and Brazilian real, as concerns about Turkey’s falling forex reserves and high inflation levels erased gains from a series of interest-rate hikes since November."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The lira, which plunged to a near all-time low last week after President Tayyip Erdogan replaced a hawkish central bank chief with a critic of high interest rates, was set to fall about 1% to 8.41/$ in the next 12 months, the poll showed."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Not much was expected from high-yielders such as the South African rand, which has lost its appeal in the past few weeks as U.S. bond yields scaled one-year highs. The currency was expected to trade within a narrow range in the next 12 months."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Oil currencies such as Russia’s rouble, which suffered as a reopening of the Suez Canal led to a decline in oil prices, was expected to gain this year but still be far from levels seen in early 2020."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Not all was well with Asia too, where the economic recovery has been strong."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Investors were bearish on all Asian currencies for the first time in a year with bets on the yuan, which had been relatively more bullish as China was the only major economy to see growth in 2020, turned short for the first time since June, a separate Reuters poll on currency positioning showed. [ASIA/FXP]"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Chinese yuan, the most actively-traded emerging market currency, was predicted to gain 2.7% to 6.40 per dollar in 12 months."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"India’s rupee, one of the best-performing EM currency so far in 2021, was expected to turn worst-performing among its peers."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"(For other stories from the April Reuters foreign exchange poll:)"}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: U.S. dollar to remain strong for at least another month - Reuters poll
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: The U.S. dollar will remain strong for at least another month, according to a Reuters poll of foreign exchange strategists, who still forecast that the currency will weaken in the longer term.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"BENGALURU The U.S. dollar will remain strong for at least another month, according to a Reuters poll of foreign exchange strategists, who still forecast that the currency will weaken in the longer term."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Following a spike in benchmark Treasury yields, which touched a 14-month high on Tuesday, the greenback is up about 3.5% this year, a solid revival given it started the year on the defensive."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Trillions of dollars in expected government infrastructure spending and a robust U.S. economic recovery will likely keep bond yields rising and the dollar well-supported in the near-term, forcing reassessments of bets against the currency."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Indeed, the latest trader positioning data showed currency speculators trimming their net short positions to the lowest level since June 2020."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“We started the year dollar negative both in the short-term and in the long-term but the shift in the environment is so dramatic that staying dollar negative in the short-term was very risky,” said Steve Englander, head of G10 FX research at Standard Chartered."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Over 85% of analysts, or 48 of 56, who answered an additional question said the current dollar strength would last at least another month. Of the 48, 11 said it would last three to six months and 16 said it would last more than six months."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The other eight said the dollar’s revival was already over or would end in less than a month."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"But beyond short-term outperformance, the March 26-31 poll of over 65 FX strategists in total predicted the dollar would weaken over the 12-month horizon."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Those forecasts line up with a separate Reuters survey of fixed-income strategists published last week who were not expecting sovereign yields to be a lot higher than current levels over the coming year."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"For a graphic on Reuters poll graphic on the EUR/USD and U.S. 10-year Treasury yield outlook:"},{"type":"paragraph","content":""},{"type":"infographics","media_type":"static","content":"https://fingfx.thomsonreuters.com/gfx/polling/oakpelwwnvr/MicrosoftTeams-image%20(1).png"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“I don’t think we’re going to have a massive run-up on the dollar in the way we did a couple of years ago. I’m beginning to think I’m going to have to bring that lower over the next couple of weeks or so,” added Rabobank’s Foley."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Despite the dollar gaining across the board this year, much like in previous cycles, it was emerging market currencies which suffered the most."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"While they were expected to pare some of their recent steep losses over the coming year, there was plenty of selling pressure expected for developing economies’ currencies over the next 12 months."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"For a graphic on Reuters poll graphic on currency market outlook:"},{"type":"paragraph","content":""},{"type":"infographics","media_type":"static","content":"https://fingfx.thomsonreuters.com/gfx/polling/dgkpleyymvb/FX%20April%20EQ.PNG"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Nearly 60% of analysts, or 28 of 48, who answered an extra question said emerging market currencies would underperform over the next three months. test_endpoint.articlesName: Impact of Fed policy changes on China's markets is limited -PBOC official
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Stimulus measures implemented by the Federal Reserve over the past year and future policy changes that the U.S. central bank has signalled will have limited impact on China's financial markets, a Chinese central bank official said on Thursday.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"BEIJING (Reuters) -Stimulus measures implemented by the Federal Reserve over the past year and future policy changes that the U.S. central bank has signalled will have limited impact on China’s financial markets, a Chinese central bank official said on Thursday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“The positive effect of China’s normal monetary policy stance is emerging,” Sun Guofeng, head of the People’s Bank of China’s (PBOC) monetary policy department, told a briefing. He said that policy was returned to normal after the COVID-19 epidemic in China was brought under control in May."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“The next step is to manage our own affairs well, and we must keep our monetary policy steady.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"China will keep the yuan’s exchange rate basically stable at a reasonable level, and step up prudent management of cross-border capital flows and guide market expectations."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"There is also a need to keep China’s benchmark lending rate for corporate and household loans, Loan Prime Rate (LPR), at a reasonable level, Sun said, to anchor the money supply. PBOC has kept LPR steady for the 11th straight month in March."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Wang Xin, director of the central bank’s research bureau, said at the same briefing that the PBOC has launched a multi-lateral digital currency research pilot programme with monetary authorities in Hong Kong, Thailand and United Arab Emirates."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The pilot is to study the so-called payment versus payment (PvP) settlement in cross-border transactions of currency pairs using distributed ledger technology, according to Wang."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Wang said PBOC is also testing cross-border use of digital yuan with Hong Kong monetary authority."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"PBOC vice governor Liu Guiping, who was also present at the briefing, said China will also gradually incorporate climate-related risks into the PBOC’s macroprudential regulatory framework."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“We will also push forward the green investment principles for Belt and Road projects, and strictly control the overseas investments in new coal-fire power plants,” said Liu, adding that Beijing will work with U.S. to push forward sustainable finance agenda for G20 countries."}]

test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"LONDON (Reuters Breakingviews) - MONEY ON THE MOVE. Africa’s mobile money revolution is attracting a big hitter. Global payments giant Mastercard on Thursday announced it’s investing $100 million into Airtel Africa’s cash-transfer unit, which lets users zap each other money via basic mobile phone handsets. The deal values the division, which operates in 14 countries, at $2.65 billion, over a third of its parent’s total enterprise value."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The valuation of 12 times the unit’s expected EBITDA this year, compared with the 4 times multiple at which its parent trades, may prompt other African telecommunications operators to go digging for value in their mobile money coffers. With the continent’s mobile phone markets increasingly saturated, operators see sense in jumping on the payments revolution rumbling round the globe. (By Ed Cropley)"}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Russia's Yandex seeks more time to respond to allegation it broke competition law
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Russian internet giant Yandex asked on Thursday for an extra month to respond to accusations that it violated competition law on its search engine at the expense of other companies, Russia's Federal Antimonopoly Service (FAS) said.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"MOSCOW, April 1 Russian internet giant Yandex asked on Thursday for an extra month to respond to accusations that it violated competition law on its search engine at the expense of other companies, Russia’s Federal Antimonopoly Service (FAS) said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The state agency told Yandex in February that it had created unequal market conditions for general online search services, that it was preferentially promoting its own products and asked it to stop."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Around 20 Russian internet companies signed an open letter, supporting the move by the FAS. In it, they accused Yandex of abusing its dominant market position and urged it to establish a level playing field for fair competition in online searches."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“We are in dialogue with the FAS and are working on the next steps,” Yandex said on Thursday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In its warning in February, the FAS said it could be forced to initiate antitrust proceedings against Yandex, should the internet company fail to comply. Yandex could face a possible fine if found to have broken competition law."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In February, a Yandex spokesman said: “We are confident in our position and are ready to defend it.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The FAS said it would decide on what further action to take, including granting the extension, within 10 days. (Reporting by Alexander Marrow Editing by Alexandra Hudson)"}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Russia's Sberbank and Mail.Ru on verge of dividing assets as JV nears split- sources
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Russia's largest lender Sberbank and internet firm Mail.Ru are on the verge of dividing assets in their ride-hailing and food delivery joint venture due to a wide range of disagreements, three sources close to both sides said.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"MOSCOW, April 1 Russia’s largest lender Sberbank and internet firm Mail.Ru are on the verge of dividing assets in their ride-hailing and food delivery joint venture due to a wide range of disagreements, three sources close to both sides said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The partners are discussing how to split the business, a person close to Sberbank’s supervisory board said, in a blow to the lender’s plans to remodel itself as a tech company and diversify into non-banking businesses."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The joint venture, set up in December 2019, encompasses the food delivery app Delivery Club, ride-hailing service Citymobil and other assets, with each partner holding a 45% stake."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"According to Sberbank’s accounts, the venture reported a loss of 27.8 billion roubles ($366.37 million) in 2020."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"It finally became clear in the winter that “the JV will not last”, one of the sources told Reuters, with a Sberbank representative at a Mail.Ru Group board meeting trying to block an annual bonus payment to top executives."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Two people confirmed that Lev Khasis, first deputy chairman of Sberbank’s executive board, had voted against the bonus."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Sberbank denied that the venture was close to breaking up, calling the reports “unsubstantiated rumours”."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Already today the value of our joint business is much higher than the investments made in it, which offers great value for our shareholders,” Sberbank said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Mail.Ru declined to comment. On Tuesday, the group said it has no plans to exit the joint venture."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Last spring, when the partners disagreed over control issues and payment services, the two parties fought to maintain the venture, one person close to the matter said, but no such efforts are being made now. The two firms pumped an additional 12 billion roubles into the venture in August."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"A break-up would bring an end to Sberbank’s fourth attempt to make a non-banking partnership after failing to agree terms with Alibaba Group in 2017 and terminating ties with internet giant Yandex last summer after two years of cooperation."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The bank was also in talks to buy a large minority stake in Ozon, sources told Reuters in June, before the online retailer decided to go down the IPO route with a successful Nasdaq debut late last year."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Financial Times first reported this week that Sberbank and Mail.ru were planning to break up their $1.6 billion tech joint venture."}]

test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: George Floyd's girlfriend took the witness stand on Thursday and described their relationship, from a first kiss to date nights at restaurants, but also spoke about how an addiction to painkillers took hold of their life together.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"MINNEAPOLIS (Reuters) -George Floyd’s girlfriend took the witness stand on Thursday and described their relationship, from a first kiss to date nights at restaurants, but also spoke about how an addiction to painkillers took hold of their life together."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Courteney Ross, 45, was the first witness who personally knew Floyd to testify at the trial of Derek Chauvin, the former Minneapolis policeman charged with murdering the man she loved by kneeling on his neck during an arrest last May."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In her testimony, Ross described how her romance with Floyd began in 2017 when he offered to pray with her. She also spoke about addiction: As with millions of other Americans, Floyd and Ross struggled to quit opioids."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“It’s a classic story of how many people get addicted to opioids,” Ross said. “We both suffered from chronic pain: mine was in my neck, his was in his back.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The death of Floyd, a 46-year-old Black man, set off protests across the United States and around the world over racial injustice and police brutality against Black people."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Prosecutors wanted the jury to hear Ross’s frank account of opioid use to undermine a central plank of Chauvin’s defense in a trial seen as a litmus test of accountability in U.S. policing."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Chauvin’s lawyers argue that Floyd’s death, which the county medical examiner ruled a homicide at the hands of police, was really an overdose from the fentanyl found in his blood at an autopsy."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Prosecutors have said Eric Nelson, Chauvin’s lead attorney, has sought to raise the drug use in an effort to muddy Floyd’s character and that the theory would be contradicted by medical evidence."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Nelson seemed to acknowledge the sensitivity when he stood up to cross-examine Ross: “I’m sorry to hear about your struggles with opioid addiction,” he began. “Thank you for sharing that with the jury.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Before that, Ross, who had pinned a heart-shaped brooch to her black jacket for the occasion, smiled fondly at the memory when asked by prosecutors in the fourth day of witness testimony how she first met Floyd."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“It’s one of my favorite stories to tell,” she said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"‘SIS’? YOU OK?’"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Ross, 45, said she first met Floyd in August 2017 at a Salvation Army homeless shelter, where he worked as a security guard. She was waiting in the lobby to visit the father of her son after closing up the coffee shop where she worked. Floyd approached her."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Floyd has this great, deep, southern voice, raspy,” she said, “and he was, like, ‘Sis’? You OK, sis’?’”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"He sensed she felt sad and alone and offered to pray with her."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“It was so sweet,” Ross said, dabbing a tissue to her eyes. “At the time I had lost a lot of faith in God.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"They had their first kiss in the lobby that night and except an occasional break were together until his death, she said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In his cellphone, Floyd listed Ross, a mother of two, as ‘Mama.’"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"They took walks in the parks and around the lakes of Ross’s native Minneapolis, which was still new to the Texas-raised Floyd, and dined out often: “He was a big man,” she said, describing his daily weightlifting, “and it look a lot of energy to keep him going.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"She said he adored his two young daughters and was a “mama’s boy.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"After his mother’s death in 2018 he seemed “kind of like a shell of himself, like he was broken.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"At times the couple took prescribed painkillers. At other times they bought OxyContin and other pills on the black market. Sometimes they beat the habit; sometimes they relapsed."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Addiction, in my opinion, is a lifelong struggle,” she said. “It’s not something that comes and goes, it’s something I’ll deal with forever.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Nelson, Chauvin’s lawyer, asked Ross about an episode during which she took Floyd to a hospital emergency room, where he was treated for five days for an overdose."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“You did not know that he had taken heroin at that time?” Nelson asked her. She said no."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Lawyers for Floyd’s family, Ben Crump and Antonio Romanucci, criticized Chauvin’s defense in a joint statement: “Tens of thousands of Americans struggle with self-medication and opioid abuse and are treated with dignity, respect and support, not brutality,” their statement said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Ross said her last conversation with Floyd was on May 24, when they spoke on the telephone."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"A day later, Floyd was pinned under Chauvin’s knee, under arrest on suspicion of buying cigarettes at a food store with a counterfeit $20 bill."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The jury has heard three days’ of testimony by onlookers who said they screamed at Chauvin and other officers, imploring them to check Floyd’s pulse."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"On Thursday, paramedics who arrived at the scene testified that they had to move police off Floyd, who by then had stopped breathing, had no pulse and whose pupils were dilated."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“In lay terms,” Derek Smith, one of the paramedics, told the jury, “I thought he was dead.”"}]

test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: (Refiles to make clear in paragraph 7 that medical examiner noted there was fentanyl in Floyd's blood at autopsy)
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"(Refiles to make clear in paragraph 7 that medical examiner noted there was fentanyl in Floyd’s blood at autopsy)"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The jury in the murder trial of former Minneapolis police officer Derek Chauvin heard testimony on Monday from the doctor who pronounced George Floyd dead and the city’s police chief who said Chauvin broke department rules and its ethics code."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Chauvin, who is white, had been pressing his knee into the neck of Floyd, a 46-year-old Black man in handcuffs, for about nine minutes on May 25, 2020, a scene that ignited global protests against police brutality."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Here is some testimony from court on Monday:"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"DR. BRADFORD LANGENFELD, EMERGENCY DOCTOR WHO PRONOUNCED FLOYD DEAD"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Langenfeld, an emergency physician, testified he took over Floyd’s care after two paramedics brought him to the Hennepin County Medical Center."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Asked by prosecutor Jerry Blackwell if the paramedics indicated that they suspected a drug overdose or heart attack, Langenfeld said they did not, indicating only that Floyd’s heart had stopped beating and that there may have been a delay in starting resuscitation efforts."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“It’s well known that any amount of time that a patient spends in cardiac arrest without immediate CPR markedly decreases the chance of a good outcome,” he told the jury. Medical tests led Langenfeld to think it was unlikely that Floyd suffered a heart attack, he told the jury. The most likely explanation, the doctor said, was asphyxia."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Eric Nelson, Chauvin’s lawyer, asked Langenfeld whether fentanyl could also lead to the low oxygen and high carbon dioxide levels in Floyd’s blood. Langenfeld agreed it could. Floyd’s girlfriend testified last week that Floyd was addicted to opioids. A medical examiner who ruled Floyd’s death a homicide at the hands of police noted there was fentanyl in Floyd’s blood at autopsy."},{"type":"heading","content":"MEDARIA ARRADONDO, CHIEF OF MINNEAPOLIS POLICE DEPARTMENT"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Arradondo testified that Chauvin broke Minneapolis Police Department rules and its ethics code during the incident."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“It’s not part of our training, and it is certainly not part of our ethics and our values,” Arradondo told the jury as prosecutors sought to undermine a central plank of Chauvin’s defense."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Arradondo said it was unusual for police to take someone into custody where the alleged crime was as minor as in the case of Floyd, who was suspected of using a counterfeit $20 bill to buy cigarettes at the Cup Foods grocery store."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"A prosecutor asked him to explain to the jury how police officers receive extensive training on how to use force and to reduce tensions."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“We are oftentimes the first face of government our community will see, and we will often meet them at their worst moments,” he said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Officers carry tourniquets and are trained how to use them to treat gunshot wounds, are taught how to do chest compressions and are given naloxone inhalers to be used to rapidly reverse an opioid overdose, Arradondo said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"He was asked to read aloud parts of the department’s code of ethics."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“It’s really about treating people with dignity and respect above all else,” he told the jury."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Chauvin used too much pressure on Floyd’s neck, Arradondo said, pointing to police training that he said emphasized the “sanctity of life.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Arradondo said Chauvin also did not “de-escalate” the situation and did not provide mandated first aid."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In cross-examination, Nelson got Arradondo to say it had been “many years” since he himself had made an arrest."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"He also had Arradondo agree with him that a police officer’s use of force is often “not attractive.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"KATIE BLACKWELL, FORMER COMMANDER OF DEPARTMENT’s TRAINING DIVISION"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Blackwell, who is now inspector of the department’s 5th Precinct, was the commander of the department’s training division at the time of the incident."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"She told the jury that Chauvin went through extensive training on defensive tactics and was a field training officer himself. She also testified she has known him about 20 years."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Prosecutor Steve Schleicher showed Blackwell a photograph of Chauvin kneeling on Floyd and asked her if that was a technique learned in Minneapolis Police Department training."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“It is not,” Blackwell said. “I don’t know what kind of improvised position that is, so that’s not what we train.”"}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Mother wounded trying to shield 9-year-old son slain in California mass shooting
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: One of four people shot dead in a suburban Los Angeles real estate office was a 9-year-old boy struck by gunfire in the arms of his wounded mother as she tried in vain to shield him from the attack, officials said on Thursday.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"LOS ANGELES (Reuters) -One of four people shot dead in a suburban Los Angeles real estate office was a 9-year-old boy struck by gunfire in the arms of his wounded mother as she tried in vain to shield him from the attack, officials said on Thursday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Authorities also disclosed that the suspected gunman in Wednesday’s violence, who was himself wounded before he was taken into custody, knew all of his victims and had a family relationship with at least one of them."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The bloodshed inside a two-story office complex in the city of Orange, about 30 miles (48 km) southeast of downtown Los Angeles, marked the third deadly mass shooting in the United States in a month."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Ten people were killed at a supermarket in Boulder, Colorado, on March 22, and eight others died in a series of attacks on three Atlanta-area spas on March 16. The accused gunman in each of those rampages was likewise arrested."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"But the suspect’s connection with the dead in the California attack appeared to set it apart from the shootings in Georgia and Colorado, where the victims were believed to have been killed at random."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“The preliminary motive is believed to be related to a business and personal relationship which existed between the suspect and all of the victims,” Orange Police Department Lieutenant Jennifer Amat told a news conference."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The identities of the victims were being withheld pending notification of relatives, police said. The surviving victim, a woman badly wounded while cradling her son in her arms as he was fatally shot, worked at the business, authorities said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"She remained hospitalized in critical but stable condition on Thursday. Three other adults - two women and a man - were killed."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The suspect, identified as Aminadab Gaxiola Gonzalez, 44, a resident of the nearby city of Fullerton, also was listed in critical condition. He may be arraigned on murder charges from his hospital bed on Friday, said Kimberly Edds, a spokeswoman for the Orange County District Attorney’s office."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"He is accused of opening fire in the office of a mobile home realty company after first using bicycle-style locks to seal off two sets of gates to the courtyard in the center of the office building, blocking entrance to the complex from the outside."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Police officers, encountering gunfire as they arrived on the scene, were forced to use bolt cutters to open the gates and directly confront the suspect. Two officers initially exchanged gunfire with the gunman from outside the gates."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“In the meantime, a horrific rampage was going on in offices and people were dying or were being shot,” District Attorney Todd Spitzer said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The suspect was arrested once police entered and found him injured, Amat said. Edds said investigators, who recovered a semi-automatic handgun from the scene, did not yet know whether the gunshot he suffered was self-inflicted or from a bullet fired by police."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Authorities said they also recovered a backpack containing pepper spray, handcuffs and ammunition that they believe belonged to the suspect, who had been living in a motel room in Anaheim before Wednesday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Police said they obtained surveillance video camera footage of the suspect at the crime scene. A still image from that video was released showing the gunman wearing a ball cap, dark glasses and a black bandanna, striding through an office while brandishing a pistol in one hand. He also appeared to be have a backpack slung over one shoulder."}]

test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"LOS ANGELES (Reuters) -One of four people shot dead in a suburban Los Angeles real estate office was a 9-year-old boy struck by gunfire in the arms of his wounded mother as she tried in vain to shield him from the attack, officials said on Thursday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Authorities also disclosed that the suspected gunman in Wednesday’s violence, who was himself wounded before he was taken into custody, knew all of his victims and had a family relationship with at least one of them."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The bloodshed inside a two-story office complex in the city of Orange, about 30 miles (48 km) southeast of downtown Los Angeles, marked the third deadly mass shooting in the United States in a month."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Ten people were killed at a supermarket in Boulder, Colorado, on March 22, and eight others died in a series of attacks on three Atlanta-area spas on March 16. The accused gunman in each of those rampages was likewise arrested."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"But the suspect’s connection with the dead in the California attack appeared to set it apart from the shootings in Georgia and Colorado, where the victims were believed to have been killed at random."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“The preliminary motive is believed to be related to a business and personal relationship which existed between the suspect and all of the victims,” Orange Police Department Lieutenant Jennifer Amat told a news conference."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The identities of the victims were being withheld pending notification of relatives, police said. The surviving victim, a woman badly wounded while cradling her son in her arms as he was fatally shot, worked at the business, authorities said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"She remained hospitalized in critical but stable condition on Thursday. Three other adults - two women and a man - were killed."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The suspect, identified as Aminadab Gaxiola Gonzalez, 44, a resident of the nearby city of Fullerton, also was listed in critical condition. He may be arraigned on murder charges from his hospital bed on Friday, said Kimberly Edds, a spokeswoman for the Orange County District Attorney’s office."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"He is accused of opening fire in the office of a mobile home realty company after first using bicycle-style locks to seal off two sets of gates to the courtyard in the center of the office building, blocking entrance to the complex from the outside."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Police officers, encountering gunfire as they arrived on the scene, were forced to use bolt cutters to open the gates and directly confront the suspect. Two officers initially exchanged gunfire with the gunman from outside the gates."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“In the meantime, a horrific rampage was going on in offices and people were dying or were being shot,” District Attorney Todd Spitzer said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The suspect was arrested once police entered and found him injured, Amat said. Edds said investigators, who recovered a semi-automatic handgun from the scene, did not yet know whether the gunshot he suffered was self-inflicted or from a bullet fired by police."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Authorities said they also recovered a backpack containing pepper spray, handcuffs and ammunition that they believe belonged to the suspect, who had been living in a motel room in Anaheim before Wednesday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Police said they obtained surveillance video camera footage of the suspect at the crime scene. A still image from that video was released showing the gunman wearing a ball cap, dark glasses and a black bandanna, striding through an office while brandishing a pistol in one hand. He also appeared to be have a backpack slung over one shoulder."}]

videos.description: [NFA] The shooting in Orange, California, that killed four people including a 9-year-old boy on Wednesday was carried out by a 44-year-old man who knew the victims, police said on Thursday, as they ruled out the shooting as a random act.

test_endpoint.articlesName: Bolsonaro confirms Ribeiro as Banco do Brasil CEO; chairman resigns
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro swore in Fausto Ribeiro as chief executive of Banco do Brasil SA on Thursday, according to a securities filing, just hours after the bank's chairman and a second board member announced their resignations after criticizing Ribeiro's appointment...
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"SAO PAULO (Reuters) -Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro swore in Fausto Ribeiro as chief executive of Banco do Brasil SA on Thursday, according to a securities filing, just hours after the bank’s chairman and a second board member announced their resignations after criticizing Ribeiro’s appointment."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The swearing in of Ribeiro marked Bolsonaro’s latest political intervention in a state-controlled company. Ribeiro, 53, has been the head of a small business unit at Banco do Brasil since September but has been at the bank for more than three decades. As CEO, Ribeiro will manage executives who are now his bosses."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Chairman Helio Magalhaes and fellow board member Jose Guimaraes Monforte, whose board resignations were announced in a securities filing, were among the four members of Banco do Brasil SA’s eight-member board who said that Ribeiro was not ready for the job."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The four directors said in a publicly issued statement that the board should have the power to appoint its leader."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In his letter of resignation, Magalhaes said he decided to quit because the government has neglected Banco do Brasil, the country’s second largest bank by assets, and other state-controlled companies."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Currently, the far-right Bolsonaro is entitled to nominate Banco do Brasil’s chief executive, leaving the bank’s board of directors little say, in a deviation from corporate governance best practices."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Ribeiro, whose appointment also makes him a board member, replaces Andre Brandao."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In their statement, board members Magalhaes, Monforte, Luiz Spinola and Paulo Roberto Evangelista de Lima said that while Ribeiro met the legal requirements to become Banco do Brasil’s CEO, he lacks management experience to run the bank."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Brandao did not participate in the meeting. He submitted his resignation as CEO in March, two months after Bolsonaro disagreed with cost-cutting measures he had undertaken."},{"type":"heading","content":"LETTER OF RESIGNATION"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Magalhaes, who previously headed the Brazilian units of Citigroup Inc and American Express Co, wrote that the interference in the efficiency program illustrates the government’s disrespect for Banco do Brasil’s corporate governance, saying it is no longer among the government priorities for the bank."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"One board member said he learned about Ribeiro’s appointment from a government statement, which he said signaled that it was a political nomination."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Amid a snowballing coronavirus pandemic, Bolsonaro has been facing political pressure as he prepares to run for reelection next year."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Brandao had antagonized Bolsonaro by planning to close more than 100 branches and cut 5,000 jobs through a buyout program. Leaving a small city without a brick-and-mortar Banco do Brasil branch can hurt local politicians’ popularity, given that many Brazilians still lack internet connections."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"When Bolsonaro took power in 2019, he pledged to sell off many state companies and appoint executives with private-sector experience to run or oversee them."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"However, earlier this week, the Brazilian government named three new board members at Banco do Brasil, replacing private-sector veterans previously named by Economy Minister Paulo Guedes. Two of them, Aramis de Andrade and Walter Ribeiro, are former Banco do Brasil executives. Ieda Cagni is a civil servant at the Office of the General Counsel to the National Treasury."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"It is not the first time that Banco do Brasil has been the target of political interference. Former leftist President Dilma Rousseff forced the bank to reduce interest rates on loans and fees, hitting profitability."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Ribeiro’s appointment was very odd given that the bank had several executives in its ranks better suited to the CEO position,” said Carlos Daltozo, head of equities at research broker Eleven."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The changes at Banco do Brasil come less than two months after Bolsonaro replaced the CEO of Petrobras over fuel price hikes. The CEO of state power company Centrais Eletricas Brasileiras SA, known as Eletrobras, quit in January over what he called a lack of political support in Congress for privatizing the company."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Nationals' home opener postponed due to COVID-19 issues
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: The Washington Nationals' home opener against the New York Mets, scheduled for Thursday, has been postponed due to COVID-19 issues, Major League Baseball said.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Washington Nationals’ home opener against the New York Mets, scheduled for Thursday, has been postponed due to COVID-19 issues, Major League Baseball said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The decision was made a day after the Nationals said one of their players tested positive for COVID-19, while four others and a staff member were in quarantine following contact tracing."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“We’re unable to disclose any additional information about who tested positive,” Nationals General Manager Mike Rizzo said in a report on the team’s website."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“But we are following MLB protocols and CDC protocols and working closely with the league to determine our next steps. There’ll be a lot of balls in the air until then.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"MLB said that out of an abundance of caution, the game will be not be made up on Friday. The two teams currently are still scheduled to play on Saturday and Sunday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"A subsequent report on the Nationals’ website indicated at least two more positive cases were discovered within the organization after additional testing."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Washington was one of 15 teams scheduled to play their home opener on Thursday, with each club filling different portions of their stadiums’ capacity. The Nationals plan to allow 5,000 fans, or about 12% capacity, into their ballpark."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Because of the COVID-19 pandemic, no fans were allowed to attend MLB games last season until late in the play-offs."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Last year’s truncated MLB season was roiled early by several postponements related to COVID-19 and the Miami Marlins were shut down for a week in a bid to contain an outbreak among their players."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Suspected Italian spy gave Russia highly confidential material: source
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Italian police have found a stash of classified and highly classified military documents they believe an Italian navy captain gave to a Russian official in return for cash, a judicial source said on Friday.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"ROME Italian police have found a stash of classified and highly classified military documents they believe an Italian navy captain gave to a Russian official in return for cash, a judicial source said on Friday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Walter Biot, 54, was arrested on Tuesday in a Rome carpark. A police source said he had been seen handing information to a Russian military attache in exchange for 5,000 euros ($5,900)."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The judicial source with access to the case files said police had recovered a memory card containing 181 photos classified as confidential, nine classified as highly confidential and 47 classified as secret documents from NATO."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Biot’s lawyer Roberto De Vita told an Italian newspaper that his client had told him that he had handed over information to Russia for money, but denied having leaked classified documents."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Biot appeared in court for the first time on Thursday but declined to speak. “He asked for time to collect his thoughts,” De Vita told reporters."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Interviewed later by Corriere della Sera newspaper, De Vita said that Biot had told him he was not ideologically driven and had never handed over “documents which could put Italy or other countries at risk”."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Italy, which has traditionally enjoyed better relations with Moscow than many other Western states, has expelled two Russian diplomats in retaliation and denounced the alleged espionage as a “hostile act”."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Russian foreign ministry was quoted as saying on Wednesday that it regretted the expulsions, but that they did not threaten bilateral relations."},{"type":"heading","content":"FINANCIAL TROUBLES"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Biot’s lawyer said his client had four children, one of whom was seriously ill and needed special care."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“‘I have made a mistake, but I did it for my family. I had a moment of great weakness and fragility. I was involved in a mechanism that was bigger than me. I had a debt that I could not repay’,” De Vita quoted him as saying."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"De Vita did not immediately respond to a request by Reuters for further comment."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Biot is being held in a Rome jail and has been denied house arrest. He faces a minimum 15 years in prison if found guilty of military espionage."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Biot’s wife, Claudia Carbonara, told Corriere della Sera that the family was struggling to get by on his salary of 3,000 euros a month, with expenses including 1,200 euros a month on their mortgage."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“He is not stupid or irresponsible. He was just desperate,” she was quoted as saying. Contacted by Reuters, Carbonara declined to comment."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Biot has the rank of a frigate captain and had a desk job since 2010. He was currently working at the defense ministry department tasked with developing national security policy."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Russian official who was seized on Tuesday left Rome on Thursday along with an embassy colleague, a diplomatic source said. Both men worked in the military attache’s office at the Rome embassy."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Italian media named them as Dmitry Ostroukhov and Alexei Nemudrov. Russian authorities have not released their names."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"($1 = 0.8524 euros)"}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Biden allows Trump ban on temporary foreign workers to expire
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: President Joe Biden allowed a proclamation from his Republican predecessor that had blocked many temporary foreign workers from coming into the United States to expire on Wednesday, according to a related court filing on Thursday.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"WASHINGTON President Joe Biden allowed a proclamation from his Republican predecessor that had blocked many temporary foreign workers from coming into the United States to expire on Wednesday, according to a related court filing on Thursday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Democratic president has rolled back some of former President Donald Trump’s immigration policies since taking office on Jan. 20 including last month revoking a proclamation that had blocked many immigrant visa applicants from entering the United States."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Trump first issued his directive on temporary foreign workers in June 2020 and renewed it through March 31 before leaving office, portraying it as necessary to protect American workers amid high unemployment during the coronavirus pandemic."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Reuters and other outlets reported the planned move earlier in the week."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Elections officials fear Georgia law could politicize voting operations
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Election officials in conservative and liberal parts of Georgia say a new law allowing a Republican-controlled state agency to take over local voting operations could make the process too partisan.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"WASHINGTON Election officials in conservative and liberal parts of Georgia say a new law allowing a Republican-controlled state agency to take over local voting operations could make the process too partisan."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Voting rights advocates have also warned that the provision, part of sweeping voting restrictions signed into law last week by Governor Brian Kemp, targets Democratic bastions such as Atlanta’s Fulton County that helped deliver the party control of the White House and Congress in recent elections."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The new law has mostly gained attention for its measures to strengthen absentee ballot identification requirements, curtail ballot drop box use and penalize members of the public who offer food and water to voters in line."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Months after former Republican President Donald Trump falsely claimed voter fraud in the 2020 elections, Republican backers say Georgia’s law is needed to restore confidence in election integrity. Civil rights groups have filed three lawsuits asserting the law illegally restricts voting rights, particularly for minority voters."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The legislation authorizes the Republican-majority legislature to appoint the state election board’s majority while demoting the elected secretary of state, Georgia’s top election official, to a non-voting position."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"It also allows the state board to remove local supervisors it deems derelict and replace them with individuals of its choosing."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"That power has alarmed Democrats and civil rights organizations in light of Trump’s unprecedented pressure campaign to overturn the results in key Democratic counties."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"But even some election officials from Republican-leaning counties said they opposed allowing the state board to take over local elections, a Reuters survey of the state’s 159 counties found."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"‘DANGEROUS PATH’"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Of the 55 that responded, officials in 11 counties of varying sizes and political leanings - Bartow, Macon-Bibb, Cobb, DeKalb, Floyd, Heard, Jones, Murray, Paulding, Quitman and Tattnall - said the law gave the state too much control over election administration. Traditionally, locally appointed nonpartisan or bipartisan boards and judges oversee issues such as voter eligibility, polling place locations and vote certification."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“If we don’t rely on and hire smart people with institutional knowledge, and the process becomes politicized, then we go down a very dangerous path,” said Baoky Vu, a Republican on the DeKalb County elections board."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Election officials in 12 other counties did not express concerns with the law, while 32 officials declined to comment."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Georgia is among several battleground states, including Florida and Arizona, where Republican lawmakers have pushed new voting restrictions they say will curb voting fraud, despite research showing such instances are rare in the United States."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Voting rights advocates say some efforts are intended to punish election officials who, like Georgia Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger, a Republican, rebuffed Trump’s demand to change the election outcome."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Asked for comment, Kemp’s spokeswoman pointed to a Fox News column the Republican governor published on Wednesday, arguing that the law “makes it easy to vote by expanding access to the polls and harder to cheat.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The bill’s main Republican sponsors in the legislature did not respond to requests for comment."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The law underscores how deeply Trump’s fraud assertions have penetrated his party. A Reuters/Ipsos poll in February found 62% of Republicans were “very concerned” that elections were tainted by ineligible voters."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"‘FRANKLY SCARY’"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Some election officials said that far from improving trust in elections, the law could diminish local oversight."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Joseph Kirk, the elections supervisor in Bartow County, which Trump won by 50 percentage points in 2020, said he found it “frankly scary” the state would replace a bipartisan local board with a political appointee."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“You’re basically allowing the general assembly to appoint people who may not know anything about running elections,” said Deidre Holden, the elections supervisor in heavily Republican Paulding County."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"But in rural Lowndes County, elections supervisor Deb Cox told Reuters the new measure would improve upon the current oversight procedures for election mismanagement."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Aklima Khondoker, Georgia state director of All Voting is Local, a voting rights group, said she has heard from election officials that some are afraid to criticize a measure that effectively allows state lawmakers to remove them from their jobs."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The law, she said, is “holding our counties hostage.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Amy Steigerwalt, a political science professor at Georgia State University, said unproven voter fraud allegations could theoretically serve as the basis for suspending a local official. The law cites long lines as a reason for possible intervention, though its other provisions will likely worsen waits in populous counties, she added."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“The question is, how are these decisions going to be made?” Steigerwalt said. “What type of ‘malfeasance’ or ‘nonfeasance’ might someone be accused of?”"}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: 'Xinjiang cotton is my love': Patriots on show at China Fashion Week
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Designer Zhou Li took to the stage amid applause following her runway show at China Fashion Week with a prop that has political overtones: a bouquet of cotton plants.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"BEIJING Designer Zhou Li took to the stage amid applause following her runway show at China Fashion Week with a prop that has political overtones: a bouquet of cotton plants."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“As far as I’m concerned, I think Xinjiang cotton is my sweetheart, my love, which is to say I’m very grateful it has brought me such happiness,” Zhou, 56, told Reuters after her show on Tuesday in Beijing."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Zhou, chief designer and founder of Chinese fashion brand Sun-Bird, is a patriotic supporter of a boycott targeting several major western apparel brands in China that have expressed concern over alleged rights abuses in Xinjiang province."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"She said her garments on show on Tuesday, which featured slick minimalist designs with ruffles and ancient Chinese characters, used Xinjiang cotton exclusively."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“For our Chinese designs, I’m certainly right to support the Xinjiang people,” she said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"H\u0026amp;M, Burberry, Adidas and Nike are among those hit by consumer boycotts in China after their comments on alleged human rights abuses in Xinjiang resurfaced on Chinese social media last week."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The backlash has put the brands in an awkward position given the importance of the market in China, where news and social media are tightly controlled by the Communist Party-controlled government and patriotic campaigns targeting foreign brands are common."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“First of all, as everyone knows, these are false statements (from the brands)”, 19-year old fashion model Zhao Yinuo said outside the event. “But of course I can’t comment too much on this because it involves political issues.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“I have a sense of national pride,” she said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The European Union, the United States, Britain and Canada last week imposed sanctions on Chinese officials, accusing them of human rights abuses in Xinjiang. China retaliated with sanctions of its own on lawmakers and academics."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Xinjiang produces around 20% of the world’s cotton."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Some researchers and lawmakers say Xinjiang authorities use coercive labour programmes to meet seasonal cotton picking needs. China strongly denies the claims, and says all labour in Xinjiang is consensual and contract-based."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“I can’t believe our Chinese Communist Party would ever do such a thing,” said a 19-year old student surnamed Li at the fashion event. “Our nation is very united.”"}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Allies of jailed Kremlin critic Navalny say he's lost 8kg due to sleep deprivation
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Allies of Kremlin critic Alexei Navalny said on Thursday he had lost 8kg in prison before even beginning a hunger strike, something they blamed on guards depriving him of sleep even as the prison service defended his treatment in custody.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"MOSCOW (Reuters) -Allies of Kremlin critic Alexei Navalny said on Thursday he had lost 8kg in prison before even beginning a hunger strike, something they blamed on guards depriving him of sleep even as the prison service defended his treatment in custody."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Navalny, one of President Vladimir Putin’s most prominent critics, went on hunger strike on Wednesday to try to force the prison holding him to give him proper medical care for what he said was acute pain in his back and legs."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The opposition politician whose release the West has demanded said last week that guards were waking him up every hour at night and that his appeals for medical care were being ignored."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"On Thursday, his allies said he had been taken to be weighed after declaring the hunger strike and that his weight had fallen to 85kg (187 lbs) from the 93kg (205 lbs) he weighed when he arrived at the IK-2 prison facility last month."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“He himself links this weight loss primarily to the fact that he is not allowed to sleep and is woken up eight times a night,” his allies said in a post on his Twitter account."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Navalny’s lawyers visit him in jail regularly and help him publish messages on social media."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The prison service in Vladimir region, where IK-2 is located, deny he is being deprived of sleep and said in a statement late on Wednesday that conditions for him at the prison were entirely legal and the same as for other inmates."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Correction facility officers strictly respect the right of all inmates to eight hours of uninterrupted sleep,” it said, adding that guards check on inmates visually at night, something it said did not stop them resting."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"It also said Navalny was being provided with all necessary medical care."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Navalny has said that daily requests for a doctor of his choice to examine him and for proper medicine have been ignored in prison."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Navalny’s allies said their chosen doctor had not been able to visit him on Thursday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Instead, they said, Maria Butina, a Russian state TV talk show host who earlier spent time in jail in the United States as a foreign agent, turned up with a camera crew."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“She shouted that this was the best and most comfortable prison. Navalny told her off in front of a line of prisoners for 15 minutes, calling her a parasite and servant of the thieves in power,” they said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Alexei Barinov, a doctor, told Reuters early on Thursday that Navalny’s lawyers had asked him to treat Navalny and that they had asked the prison service either to allow him into the prison or to let Navalny out to a clinic."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“We’re waiting for a decision from the FSIN (prison service),” he said."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: UK sanctions Myanmar conglomerate, says junta sinking to new lows with killings
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Britain sanctioned a Myanmar conglomerate on Thursday for its close links to the military leadership which Foreign Secretary Dominic Raab said was wantonly killing innocent people including children.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"LONDON Britain sanctioned a Myanmar conglomerate on Thursday for its close links to the military leadership which Foreign Secretary Dominic Raab said was wantonly killing innocent people including children."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Britain imposed sanctions on the Myanmar Economic Corporation (MEC) for involvement in serious human rights violations by making funds available to the Myanmar military, as well as its association with senior military figures."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“The Myanmar military has sunk to a new low with the wanton killing of innocent people, including children,” Raab said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“The UK’s latest actions target one of the military’s key funding streams and impose a further cost on them for their violations of human rights.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Myanmar has been rocked by protests since the army overthrew the elected government of Nobel laureate Aung San Suu Kyi on Feb. 1 citing unsubstantiated claims of fraud in a November election."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"At least 538 civilians have been killed in the protests, 141 of them on Saturday, the bloodiest day of the unrest, according to the Assistance Association for Political Prisoners (AAPP)."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"U.S. Secretary of State Antony Blinken, who has called for international companies to consider cutting ties to enterprises that support Myanmar’s military, welcomed Britain’s action."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“The coup leaders must cease all violence against the people of Burma and restore democracy,” he said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Britain’s Next on Thursday joined a growing list of European clothing retailers suspending new production orders with factories in Myanmar in the wake of the coup."}]
