test_endpoint.articlesName: Erin who? Main rival to Canada's Trudeau struggling to win voters' attention as election looms
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau's chief rival in an election expected within months has struggled to make himself known to voters amid the COVID-19 pandemic - and for Erin O'Toole, time may be running out.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"OTTAWA Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau’s chief rival in an election expected within months has struggled to make himself known to voters amid the COVID-19 pandemic - and for Erin O’Toole, time may be running out."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"O’Toole, a 48-year-old ex-soldier and one-time Cabinet minister, won the leadership of the right-leaning Conservatives last August and stresses the need for a fiscally prudent recovery plan. Trudeau’s Liberals have poured hundreds of billions of dollars into aid programs, racking up record-high budget deficits and national debt levels."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"If O’Toole loses the next election, he could well be forced out, leaving the party looking for its fifth leader in six years and handing the free-spending Liberals and their environmentally minded “build back better” agenda a long-term advantage."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"It would be tough for anyone to take on the Trudeau brand, especially during a pandemic. Trudeau’s late father, Pierre, ranks as the third-longest-serving prime minister in Canadian history."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Trudeau, 49, dominates the airwaves, holding news conferences at least twice a week, often to announce millions of dollars in new pandemic support or details on vaccines."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"By contrast, O’Toole’s late-night leadership acceptance speech in August was almost ignored."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“If people see Erin O’Toole in a headline, they’re like ‘Who?’ If we did our own research into public opinion, I’ll bet you an unnamed ‘Trudeau rival’ would poll higher than Erin O’Toole,” said one well-placed Conservative who backs the party’s leader."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“He’s at a huge disadvantage, at least as far as being able to brand himself,” said the Conservative, who requested anonymity given the sensitivity of the situation."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In fact, O’Toole launched a Twitter campaign last month saying: “Let me reintroduce myself.” O’Toole has just 124,000 Twitter followers compared with 5.5 million for Trudeau."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Conservative leader is pressed for time. Liberal insiders say Trudeau, who barely hung onto office with a minority in the October 2019 election, is preparing for a snap vote in the second half of 2021, about two years early, to seek another majority."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"With a minority, Trudeau must depend on support from opposition legislators to govern."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"‘NO PODIUM’"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The scale of the pandemic, said Conservative strategist Chad Rogers, means opposition leaders “have no podium until the day of an election.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"O’Toole also faces the challenge of leading a party that has lost two elections since holding power from 2006-2015 and contains social conservatives and right-leaning moderates."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Billing himself as a regular family man best-placed to grow the party’s base, O’Toole won the leadership after predecessor Andrew Scheer quit over his failure to win in 2019 despite a series of scandals surrounding Trudeau."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"O’Toole took a hard line during the leadership campaign to woo the right, but then edged toward the center, talking up the importance of labor unions and social equality in a bid to gain support, especially in voter-rich cities. The change in tack upset some members, say insiders, and may not be working."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“He’s not finding the traction he needs towards the center, which is where I think he’s figured out the party needs to go. ... It’s just not working yet,” said Shachi Kurl, executive director of polling firm Angus Reid."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Kurl says the Conservatives could win if they capture enough support from voters concerned about deficits. Angus Reid’s most recent poll had the Liberals leading Conservatives by 35% to 31%, not enough to secure a Trudeau majority."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Conservatives publicly say they back O’Toole. In private, four insiders complained about mixed messaging and his trouble remotely managing 120 legislators - the biggest opposition grouping in Canadian history."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Large caucuses are not meant to live in opposition for a long time and they like to test new leaders,” Rogers said in an interview."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The internal tensions emerged at a policy convention last month when - against O’Toole’s wishes - most delegates voted against recognizing climate change as a real threat."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Conservative leader, aware of polls showing most Canadians worry about climate change, is promising a green plan of his own. He brushed off the vote and declared the debate on global warming over, but the rift was clear."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Conservative Party spokesman Cory Hann said it was always difficult for opposition leaders to become known and that was particularly true during a pandemic."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“We have had to rethink how we get out there ... but it’s a challenge we’re tackling head-on,” he said by phone."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Four dead, 2 wounded, including suspect, in shooting near Los Angeles
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Four people were killed, one of them a child, in a shooting on Wednesday at an office building in suburban Los Angeles before the suspect, wounded in an exchange of gunfire with police, was taken into custody, police reported.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"ORANGE, Calif. (Reuters) -Four people were killed, one of them a child, in a shooting on Wednesday at an office building in suburban Los Angeles before the suspect, wounded in an exchange of gunfire with police, was taken into custody, police reported."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The bloodshed in the city of Orange, about 30 miles southeast of downtown Los Angeles, marked the third deadly mass shooting in the United States in less than a month. Authorities offered no explanation as to a possible motive."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Orange Police Department Lieutenant Jennifer Amat told reporters that police officers arrived on the scene at about 5:30 p.m. local time as shots were being fired and “engaged with the suspect.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"She said three adults and one child were found shot dead, and two other people struck by gunfire, including the shooter, were transported to area hospitals."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Audio of Amat’s on-scene briefing with reporters was played for Reuters afterward by the video news service OnScene.TV. The police department said in a message posted to its Facebook page that the situation had since been “stabilized” with no further threat to the public."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The shooting erupted in a two-story office building that opens onto an inner courtyard ringed by several businesses. The larger neighborhood consists of homes, apartments and other commercial properties."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Officials had no further details of the incident immediately available."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The shooting came a little more than two weeks after eight people were shot to death by a gunman who went on a rampage at three Atlanta-area day spas on March 16. Ten people were killed on March 22 when a man opened fire at a supermarket in Boulder, Colorado. The lone suspects in both those shootings were arrested."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Reacting on Twitter to Wednesday’s events in Orange, California Governor Gavin Newsom called the latest bloodshed “horrifying and heartbreaking.”"}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Scotland's Salmond: independence more important than personalities
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Scotland's former political leader Alex Salmond said on Thursday his new pro-independence party, which could cost the ruling Scottish National Party votes in a May election, had nothing to do with his bitter row with the country's current leader.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"LONDON Scotland’s former political leader Alex Salmond said on Thursday his new pro-independence party, which could cost the ruling Scottish National Party votes in a May election, had nothing to do with his bitter row with the country’s current leader."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Salmond said people had been “quite upset” after he launched the Alba Party last week, stunning Scotland’s First Minister Nicola Sturgeon, his former protégé but with whom he fell out during a bitter legal dispute."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Frankly, the cause of independence is much, much bigger than personalities,” Salmond told BBC radio."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“It’s a noble cause, a huge cause for Scotland, and everybody through history, but now, has to put aside personal differences and work for that national interest.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Sturgeon’s SNP has promised to hold another independence referendum should the party win a majority in elections on May 6. Salmond was Sturgeon’s mentor during his seven years as first minister and he led the secessionist campaign in the 2014 independence referendum when Scots voted 55%-45% to remain in the United Kingdom."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Asked about his comments that Sturgeon’s leadership had failed over her government’s handling of sexual harassment claims against him, Salmond said: “Everybody in politics has to take criticism from time to time, but I’m talking about the cause of advancing Scotland’s case for independence.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Salmond was cleared of committing multiple sex offences against women last year."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"He said his aim was to maximise the number of pro-independence lawmakers and a secessionist “supermajority” in the Scottish parliament after the May elections would make it hard for British Prime Minister Boris Johnson to deny another vote."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“A supermajority in the parliament, that is composed of not just one party the SNP, but other independence parties like Alba, will change that power balance considerably, because no Tory (Conservative) prime minister wants to be trying to face down an entire parliament or an entire people,” he said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Opinion polls have shown support and opposition to independence now roughly equal among voters."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: UK opposition leader says 'British instinct' likely to oppose COVID passports
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Britain's opposition Labour leader Keir Starmer has expressed scepticism about the use of so-called vaccine passports to allow people to access hospitality and entertainment venues, saying the "British instinct" could be against such documents.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"LONDON Britain’s opposition Labour leader Keir Starmer has expressed scepticism about the use of so-called vaccine passports to allow people to access hospitality and entertainment venues, saying the “British instinct” could be against such documents."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The government is reviewing the idea of asking people to show proof of a COVID-19 vaccination to access crowded spaces such as pubs or sports events to help with the reopening of some sectors of the economy."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Starmer said he would not make any formal decision on whether to support the initiative before studying government proposals but indicated there could be opposition to the idea from the public if death rates are near zero and hospital admissions are very low."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“I think this is really difficult and I’m not going to pretend there’s a clear black and white, yes-no easy answer on this,” Starmer told the Daily Telegraph."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"He said if “we get the virus properly under control, the death rates are near zero, hospital admissions very, very low, that the British instinct in those circumstances will be against vaccine passports.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"British Prime Minister Boris Johnson suggested last month that some pubs might require customers to produce vaccine certificates but said it may be up to individual venues to decide. He acknowledged there are “moral complexities” around introducing such rules."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The leader of the Liberal Democrats Ed Davey this week branded the use of COVID-19 passports within the United Kingdom as “illiberal” and “unworkable” and the plans are opposed by some lawmakers in Johnson’s party."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Britain has recorded 4.3 million cases of COVID-19 and a total death toll of more than 126,00 people, one of the highest rates in the world."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Biden supports moving MLB All-Star Game after Georgia voting restrictions
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: U.S. President Joe Biden said on Wednesday that he would support moving MLB's July All-Star Game from Atlanta as a protest against Georgia's new voting restrictions.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"WASHINGTON U.S. President Joe Biden said on Wednesday that he would support moving MLB’s July All-Star Game from Atlanta as a protest against Georgia’s new voting restrictions."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“I would strongly support them doing that,” Biden told ESPN. “It’s just not right. This is Jim Crow on steroids what they’re doing in Georgia.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The state last week strengthened identification requirements for absentee ballots, shortened early voting periods for runoffs and made it a crime to offer food and water to voters waiting in line."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Georgia’s Republican Governor Brian Kemp says the law is “another step to making our elections fair and secure.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"But it faces legal challenges from civil rights groups that contend the law is aimed at suppressing voting among Black people and other racial minorities."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Biden said that athletes were behaving responsibly in lending their voices to a protest against the law."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"White House press secretary Jen Psaki on Monday declined to call for a boycott of Georgia businesses as a result of the new law."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Atlanta-based Coca-Cola Co and Delta Air Lines on Wednesday joined a bid by U.S. companies to challenge the restrictions."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Biden also told ESPN that it is a mistake for the Texas Rangers baseball team to reopen its 40,000-seat stadium at full capacity."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Well, that’s a decision they made,” Biden said. “It’s a mistake.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Biden has been pushing back on moves by state governors to reopen in the middle of the COVID-19 pandemic, warning that hospitalizations are rising from the disease that has already killed 550,000 people in the United States."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Major League Baseball season starts on Thursday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Many teams are opening to reduced crowds but the Rangers plan to welcome a full crowd for their first home game, against the Toronto Blue Jays, on Monday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“It’s not responsible,” Biden said."}]

This is Jim Crow on steroids what they’re doing in Georgia.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The state last week strengthened identification requirements for absentee ballots, shortened early voting periods for runoffs and made it a crime to offer food and water to voters waiting in line."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Georgia’s Republican Governor Brian Kemp says the law is “another step to making our elections fair and secure.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"But it faces legal challenges from civil rights groups that contend the law is aimed at suppressing voting among Black people and other racial minorities."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Biden said that athletes were behaving responsibly in lending their voices to a protest against the law."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"White House press secretary Jen Psaki on Monday declined to call for a boycott of Georgia businesses as a result of the new law."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Atlanta-based Coca-Cola Co and Delta Air Lines on Wednesday joined a bid by U.S. companies to challenge the restrictions."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Biden also told ESPN that it is a mistake for the Texas Rangers baseball team to reopen its 40,000-seat stadium at full capacity."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Well, that’s a decision they made,” Biden said. “It’s a mistake.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Biden has been pushing back on moves by state governors to reopen in the middle of the COVID-19 pandemic, warning that hospitalizations are rising from the disease that has already killed 550,000 people in the United States."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Major League Baseball season starts on Thursday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Many teams are opening to reduced crowds but the Rangers plan to welcome a full crowd for their first home game, against the Toronto Blue Jays, on Monday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“It’s not responsible,” Biden said."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Australia, NZ dollars lean on support as US$ barges ahead
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: The Australian and New Zealand dollars were perilously close to major chart bulwarks on Thursday as the U.S. dollar continued its broad advance, though both currencies fared better against the low-yielding euro and yen.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"SYDNEY, April 1 The Australian and New Zealand dollars were perilously close to major chart bulwarks on Thursday as the U.S. dollar continued its broad advance, though both currencies fared better against the low-yielding euro and yen."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Aussie eased to $0.7584, after failing to clear resistance at $0.7664. The focus was on the recent low of $0.7564 where a break would risk a retreat to $0.7500, if not the 200-day moving average at $0.7385."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The kiwi faded to $0.6975 and away from resistance at $0.7033. Again, that was uncomfortably near a recent four-month trough of $0.6944 and a breach would open the way to the 200-day moving average at $0.6880."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Australian data was a mixed bag with retail sales falling a smaller-than-expected 0.8% in February, while the trade surplus missed forecasts at A$7.5 billion ($5.69 billion) because of a surprisingly sharp rise in imports."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Much more emphatic were figures showing home prices rose at the fastest pace in three decades in March, delivering a windfall to consumer wealth and confidence."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Yet the surge has done little to shake the Reserve Bank of Australia’s (RBA) commitment to super-loose policy, which is focused on driving unemployment down to levels that will lift wage growth and inflation."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“With this in mind, we expect the RBA to remain dovish, despite rapidly rising housing prices and growth in new housing finance,” said Paul Bloxham, Australia chief economist at HSBC."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“We expect the RBA to keep its cash rate and 3-year yield targets at 0.10% in 2021 and 2022, and to extend its QE programme beyond October.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"While three-year yields are pinned near 0.1%, longer-term yields have been carried higher by the global reflation trade leaving the yield curve at its steepest in decades."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Yields on 10-year bonds were up at 1.819% on Thursday, a rise of 15 basis points for the week."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"With yields in Japan and the EU held back by central bank action, the Aussie has gained on the yen and euro. The euro was at A$1.5461, against $1.6000 at the start of the year."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“AUD’s 10-year yield pickup on the euro has trended sharply higher since November 2020,” said Westpac FX strategist Sean Callow."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Once the global recovery becomes more synchronised in the second half of the year, AUD’s leverage to industrial growth should underpin gains on crosses. Our base case is A$1.51 mid-year, A$1.49 year-end.” ($1 = 1.3175 Australian dollars) (Editing by Muralikumar Anantharaman)"}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Olympics: Sky's the limit for British skateboard prodigy Brown
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Twelve-year-old skateboarding prodigy Sky Brown said she has fully recovered from her life-threatening fall last May and plans to broaden her horizons by adding surfing to her Olympic schedule.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"LOS ANGELES Twelve-year-old skateboarding prodigy Sky Brown said she has fully recovered from her life-threatening fall last May and plans to broaden her horizons by adding surfing to her Olympic schedule."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Brown, who will be the only female member of Team GB when skateboarding makes its highly-anticipated debut in July, suffered skull fractures and a broken wrist and hand after she fell from a half-pipe in Southern California."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"She was taken by helicopter to the hospital where she underwent surgery and her father Stewart later said she was lucky to be alive."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Brown said the experience has only added fuel to her considerable fire."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“What doesn’t kill you makes you stronger,” a beaming Brown told Reuters in an interview from her home in Oceanside, California."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“It just made me feel like I want to push harder, go stronger and show that even if you fall, you’ve got to get back up.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Brown has excelled on both boards from an early age and would be a formidable dual-threat Olympian."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“I love surfing as much as I love skating,” said Brown, who won bronze at the 2019 World Skateboarding Championship in the sport’s park discipline."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“That would be my dream.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"A spokesperson for Brown said it is still possible for her to qualify for Britain’s surfing team in Tokyo but she would first need to compete in the British Cup, and it is unclear if she will allowed to do so."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"If not, she will have to wait until the Paris Olympics come around in three years time."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Competing in both sports would greatly expand Brown’s medal-earning opportunities and make her a potentially transformational Olympic figure at a time when the Games are trying to appeal to a younger demographic."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"When the Los Angeles Games roll around in 2028, she will still be a teenager. If she can stay healthy, her potential is staggering."},{"type":"heading","content":"COPING WITH DELAY"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Like every Olympic athlete, Brown, who was born to a Japanese mother and a British father, was forced to cope with the disappointment of the one-year delay of the Tokyo Games."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"She used the time to improve on all aspects of her skating."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“I think I got better” she said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“I’m going higher now, I’ve learned some new tricks and I can’t wait. It’s going to be really cool."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“All the girls are getting better too, so now we’ll just have a better show.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Brown said staying active during the pandemic has been a key to her well-being and inspired her to partner with Plum Play, which makes backyard equipment like trampolines and climbing structures."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Through her fall and recovery, Brown has remained upbeat and focused on inspiring others, especially aspiring female athletes."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Be brave, be strong, have fun and do it because you love it,” she said. “And don’t let anybody stop you.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Tokyo Games begin on July 23."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: 'It's been a long year for New York' - Yankees fans cheer Opening Day at last
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Yankee Stadium's gates swung open for the first time in nearly 18 months on Thursday, as elated and emotional fans welcomed back their Bronx Bombers after a season played to empty stands amid the COVID-19 pandemic.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"NEW YORK Yankee Stadium’s gates swung open for the first time in nearly 18 months on Thursday, as elated and emotional fans welcomed back their Bronx Bombers after a season played to empty stands amid the COVID-19 pandemic."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Fans young and old streamed into the park as an organist played the Big Apple anthem “New York, New York”, the latest hint that life may slowly be starting to get back to normal."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“It’s surreal. I didn’t think there would be fans this year,” said Nicole Marinello, a 34-year-old middle school teacher from Brooklyn who lives and breathes Yankees baseball and watched virtually all of last year’s 60-game season on TV."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Unbothered by the chilly, 45-degree Fahrenheit weather and the drizzle speckling her navy blue satin Yankees jacket, Marinello watched her team warm up from the stands, one of some 9,000 fans allowed inside the stadium, which opened to 20% capacity in accordance with state regulations."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"\u003ca href=\"https://graphics.reuters.com/USA-ECONOMY/BASEBALL/qzjpqlzykvx\"\u003ehere\u003c/a\u003e"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Very emotional to be here. It’s been a long year for New York so it’s nice to be back to normal,” said Marinello, as her brown eyes filled with tears and voice quaked. “This is normal.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"‘THOSE CHILLS’"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"A little more than a year ago, MLB announced it was putting its 2020 campaign on hold, as the professional sports world ground to a halt amid the coronavirus pandemic. In July, it kicked off a shortened, 60-game regular season, played entirely without fans. Attendees were permitted at the National League Championship Series and World Series."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"This season will see a return to the standard 162-game format, with fans allowed to attend games for all 30 teams, a welcome dose of normalcy for MLB, which took an estimated more than $6 billion hit last year."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"There were early signs on Thursday, however, that it would be anything but business as usual, after the Washington Nationals’ home opener against the New York Mets had to be put on hold a day after the Nationals said one of their players had tested positive for COVID-19."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"With ballparks across the country mandating mask-wearing and social distancing, Yankee Stadium enforced its own rules for fans, requiring proof of either a COVID-19 vaccine or negative test to enter the stadium."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The team was one of 11 MLB clubs to open its facilities as a vaccine center during the off-season."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Brendan Condon, a 36-year-old Brooklyn-born Yankees fan who lives in Delaware, drove two and a half hours to attend his 18th consecutive Opening Day – not counting last year."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“There’s an asterisk there,” said Condon, who works at a pharmacy and has been administering coronavirus vaccinations."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“I walked up the block from the parking garage and once you see the lights and the facade, you get those chills. No matter what, I’ve been to hundreds of games, but it’s the same every year for that first one – you get those chills, that excitement.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Yankees were unable to bring home a win, however, ceding an early lead to lose 3-2 in the tenth inning to divisional rivals the Toronto Blue Jays."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Starting pitcher Gerrit Cole, who had eight strikeouts on the day including his 100th as a Yankee, left the game in frustration after giving up a game-tying homer in the sixth inning."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“I just want that slider back,” he told reporters."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Just to feel the energy of the people in the park was welcome. Family being here certainly after not being able to see me much last year means a lot,” the three-time All-Star said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Manager Aaron Boone struck an optimistic tone, batting aside concerns over his offense and calling the return of fans “awesome”."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“It felt like a bigger crowd than (20% capacity),” said Boone. “We just couldn’t push through for them today but it was not something that any of us take for granted… it’s different, it’s better, it’s the way it needs to be.”"}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: No breaks from COVID-19 as MLB returns
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Not even the excitement of Major League Baseball's Opening Day on Thursday could provide a break from COVID-19 as ballparks across the United States were left mostly empty while the curtain raiser in Washington, D.C. between the Nationals and New York Mets was postponed...
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"Not even the excitement of Major League Baseball’s Opening Day on Thursday could provide a break from COVID-19 as ballparks across the United States were left mostly empty while the curtain raiser in Washington, D.C. between the Nationals and New York Mets was postponed after positive tests."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Fans, many wearing masks, did their best to put on a happy face but the usual buzz associated with Opening Day was lacking as COVID-19 health and safety protocols were observed from New York to Seattle."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"With 14 scheduled games the mood was defiant as much as giddy as stadiums, many that had been used as vaccination centers, prepared to welcome back spectators."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“We’re reminded of how this wonderful game can lift our spirits, especially after this doozy of the past year. Not a day too soon,” tweeted legendary Los Angeles Dodgers broadcaster 93-year-old Vin Scully."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Opening Day, however, was put on hold for Nationals fans after a player tested positive for COVID-19 and four others and a staff member were in quarantine following contact tracing."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In the Bronx, for the first time in nearly 18 months Yankee Stadium opened its gates to fans with 10,850 allowed inside for the Yankees opener against the Toronto Blue Jays, but only if they had proof of a COVID-19 vaccine or negative test to go with their ticket."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Those fans sitting through the grey, cold New York afternoon didn’t have anything to celebrate on the field as they watched their Yankees fall 3-2 in extra-innings to the Jays."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Toronto fans weren’t celebrating much either as a few shuffled in the chill around the Blue Jays home the Rogers Center wondering when they might see their team again."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Blue Jays, who have taken up temporary residence in Dunedin, Florida, have not played at the Rogers Centre since 2019 and are unlikely to be back in Toronto anytime soon with Ontario announcing on Thursday a new 28-day lockdown as COVID-19 cases and hospitalizations surge."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Mother Nature was also a party pooper with rain forcing the postponement of Boston Red Sox and Baltimore Orioles season opener at Fenway Park."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In Detroit Miguel Cabrera smacked what was the season’s first home run as snow fell at Comerica Park helping the Tigers to a 3-2 win over the Cleveland Indians."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Golf: Wie West makes stirring return to major competition
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Michelle Wie West, in only her second tournament after a nearly two-year absence, showed she can still compete with the game's best as she made an encouraging start to the first major of the LPGA season on Thursday in Rancho Mirage, California.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"Michelle Wie West, in only her second tournament after a nearly two-year absence, showed she can still compete with the game’s best as she made an encouraging start to the first major of the LPGA season on Thursday in Rancho Mirage, California."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Wie West, who was out of action while on maternity leave and recovering from a wrist injury, fired a two-under-par 70 at the ANA Inspiration to sit four shots off the early first-round lead at Mission Hills Country Club."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“I am just happy to see my name on the first page of the leaderboard,” said Wie West. “That’s really special to me. Been a long time since I’ve seen that.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"For Wie West, who has been playing Mission Hills since 2003 when she was a 13-year-old amateur, it was a remarkable turnaround considering she missed the cut last week in the first event of her comeback."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Wie West made a bogey on her first hole, but got back to even par when she nearly aced the par-three 14th. She made three consecutive birdies after the turn but dropped a shot at the par-four sixth."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Especially after last week, it was really good to see those putts roll in,” said Wie West, who counts the 2014 U.S. Women’s Open among her five LPGA Tour wins."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Put myself in some interesting spots today, but really proud of how I grinded it out out there.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Wie West still has plenty of work ahead if she is to secure an improbable victory this week and make the winner’s traditional leap into Poppie’s Pond."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"But it was a remarkable first step that even Wie West likely did not think was possible 21 months ago when she broke down and walked away from reporters while discussing her playing future in what was the final event before her break."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“It was fun today making putts out here. I have a lot of great memories, my first one being 18 years ago,” said Wie West."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“This place is really special to me and I’m just glad to be here.”"}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Spieth getting short game in order right in time for Masters
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Jordan Spieth came into the Valero Texas Open mainly looking to fine-tune his short game ahead of next week's Masters and on Thursday he did just that as he grabbed the early first-round clubhouse lead.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"Jordan Spieth came into the Valero Texas Open mainly looking to fine-tune his short game ahead of next week’s Masters and on Thursday he did just that as he grabbed the early first-round clubhouse lead."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Spieth was a little loose off the tee in tough conditions at TPC San Antonio but more than offset that with a sublime short game en route to a five-under-par 67 that left him one shot clear after the morning wave."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“I didn’t quite hit it as good as I have been, but certainly the short game came through,” Spieth said. “Just kind of put a little more emphasis on that this week, so kind of a little balancing act right now trying to get enough work in on all facets of the game.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"For Spieth, who has shown signs that he could soon snap a victory drought that dates back to the 2017 British Open, the score marked his lowest in 19 career rounds at the Valero Texas Open."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Spieth finished in a share of 46th place at last November’s Masters and missed the cut in his next event. But the 2015 Masters winner has since found a new gear and recorded five top-15 finishes in his last six starts."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Augusta National will surely present much tougher challenges but a resurgent Spieth, who has four top-three finishes in seven Masters starts, appears to be gaining confidence in his game."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Wedged it better than I did the last couple of events and chipped the ball really well,” said Spieth. “I didn’t have much stress for par after missing greens.”"}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Swimming: Sun's second CAS hearing to take place in May
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Chinese swimmer Sun Yang's appeal against an eight-year ban for missing an out-of-competition doping test will take place in May with a new panel of judges, the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) said on Thursday.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"Chinese swimmer Sun Yang’s appeal against an eight-year ban for missing an out-of-competition doping test will take place in May with a new panel of judges, the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) said on Thursday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Triple Olympic champion Sun was banned by CAS last February after it accepted an appeal from the World Anti-Doping Agency against a decision by swimming governing body FINA to clear him of wrongdoing for his conduct during a 2018 test."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The swimmer appealed and the Swiss Federal Supreme Court in December upheld his challenge against the CAS panel “on the grounds of bias of one of the arbitrators of the CAS”."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"As a result, the case was sent back to CAS, which said it would hear it again with a different panel."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"\"A new hearing will take place during the week of May 24-28 2021,\" CAS said in a statement \u003ca href=\"https://www.tas-cas.org/fileadmin/user_upload/CAS_Media_Release_6148_HearingMay21.pdf\"\u003ehere\u003c/a\u003e."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“In light of the travel restrictions and sanitary measures in place due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the hearing will be held by video conference."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“At the conclusion of the hearing, the panel will commence its deliberations and prepare the arbitral award. Accordingly, the decision will not be announced when the hearing concludes, but at a later date.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The sanctions imposed on Sun were automatically lifted after the court’s December decision, CAS said in January."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"A different decision could potentially clear the way for Sun to compete at this year’s delayed Tokyo Olympics."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Sun, the reigning world and Olympic champion in 200 metres freestyle, was banned after he and members of his entourage were found to have smashed vials containing blood samples taken at an out-of-competition test in September, 2018."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Sun, 29, has questioned the credentials and identity of the testers and has proclaimed his innocence."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Paris-Roubaix race postponed until October due to COVID-19
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: The Paris-Roubaix one-day cycling race has been moved from April to October due to the COVID-19 situation, the Union Cycliste Internationale (UCI) said on Thursday.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Paris-Roubaix one-day cycling race has been moved from April to October due to the COVID-19 situation, the Union Cycliste Internationale (UCI) said on Thursday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The UCI said the new dates were approved by the stakeholders of men’s and women’s road cycling after a consultation process involving the organisers."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"\"This decision follows the decision of the competent French authorities to prohibit the holding of the 2021 edition ... on the dates scheduled in the UCI International road calendar in the context of the current health situation,\" the sport's governing body said in a statement \u003ca href=\"https://www.uci.org/inside-uci/press-releases/the-2021-edition-of-paris-roubaix-and-paris-roubaix-femmes-postponed-to-the-weekend-of-2-3-october\"\u003ehere\u003c/a\u003e."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The 2020 edition of the ‘Queen of the Classics’ race was postponed before being cancelled due to the COVID-19 outbreak."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The 2021 men’s race will be held on Oct. 3 with the inaugural women’s edition taking place a day earlier."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“For the UCI and the cycling community, it was important that both races could take place in 2021, and I’m delighted that new dates suitable for all parties have been found,” UCI President David Lappartient said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Paris-Roubaix is the third ‘Monument’ classic of the season after Milan-Sanremo, which took place last month, this Sunday’s Tour of Flanders and before Liege-Bastogne-Liege and the Giro di Lombardia."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: NHL roundup: Sabres rout Flyers, end run of futility at 18 games
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Steven Fogarty recorded his first NHL goal and added an assist and Brandon Montour scored two late short-handed goals as the Buffalo Sabres snapped their franchise-record, 18-game losing streak with a 6-1 victory over the visiting Philadelphia Flyers on Wednesday night.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"Steven Fogarty recorded his first NHL goal and added an assist and Brandon Montour scored two late short-handed goals as the Buffalo Sabres snapped their franchise-record, 18-game losing streak with a 6-1 victory over the visiting Philadelphia Flyers on Wednesday night."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"After blowing a 3-0, third-period lead Monday in a 4-3 overtime loss to the Flyers, Buffalo had no such concerns this time, building a 4-1 lead after two periods and pulling away. The Sabres ended an 0-15-3 skid that began after a 4-1 win at New Jersey on Feb. 23."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Sam Reinhart and Curtis Lazar also scored for Buffalo, which snapped an 0-9-2 home skid. Jacob Bryson, Rasmus Ristolainen and Kyle Okposo each posted two assists, and Linus Ullmark made 31 saves."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Ivan Provorov scored and Brian Elliott allowed four goals on 16 shots before being pulled for Philadelphia, which had won two straight overall and five straight against the Sabres."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Avalanche 9, Coyotes 3"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Joonas Donskoi had a hat trick in the first period and later added an assist, Gabriel Landeskog had two goals and an assist and Colorado beat Arizona in Denver to move into first place in the West Division."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Andre Burakovsky also scored two goals for the Avalanche, Mikko Rantanen had a goal and two assists, Pierre-Edouard Bellemare had a goal and an assist and Philipp Grubauer stopped 28 shots. Nathan MacKinnon and Samuel Girard added two assists each."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Michael Bunting had a goal and an assist, Oliver Ekman-Larsson and Conor Garland also scored and Ivan Prosvetov had 23 saves in his NHL debut for the Coyotes. Prosvetov came in for Adin Hill, who allowed four goals on 10 shots before being pulled 6:04 into the game."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Kings 4, Golden Knights 2"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Calvin Petersen made 40 saves and Andreas Athanasiou had a goal and an assist as Los Angeles snapped a three-game losing streak at the expense of Vegas in Las Vegas."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"It was Petersen’s second victory in 10 days over Vegas, which had a six-game home winning streak snapped. Lias Andersson, Jaret Anderson-Dolan and Alex Iafallo also scored goals for the Kings, who moved within four points of fourth-place St. Louis for the final playoff spot in the West Division."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Shea Theodore had a goal and an assist and William Karlsson also scored for Vegas, which dropped out of first place in the West. Marc-Andre Fleury finished with 26 saves for the Golden Knights, who fell a point behind the Avalanche."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Sharks 4, Wild 2"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Martin Jones made 26 saves to help San Jose complete a two-game sweep of visiting Minnesota."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Nikolai Knyzhov scored his first NHL goal in his 38th game, and Rudolfs Balcers, Ryan Donato and Evander Kane also scored for the Sharks, who pulled within four points of fourth place in the West Division."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Kirill Kaprizov and Mats Zuccarello scored and Kaapo Kahkonen made 29 saves for the Wild, who have won a franchise-record 11 straight home games but are 0-4-1 in their past five road games with one road win since Feb. 24."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Maple Leafs 3, Jets 1"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Auston Matthews scored a goal in his third consecutive game and Jack Campbell made 26 saves to fuel Toronto’s win over host Winnipeg."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Zach Hyman matched Matthews by collecting a goal and an assist and Alexander Kerfoot added a short-handed tally for the Maple Leafs, who are 4-0-1 in their past five games. Mitchell Marner contributed two assists."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Defenseman Josh Morrissey scored a power-play goal for the Jets, who saw captain Blake Wheeler sustain an undisclosed injury late in the first period and did not return. Connor Hellebuyck made 23 saves for the Jets."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"--Field Level Media"}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Utah Jazz players feared for lives during emergency landing: Conley
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Utah Jazz players feared they might be killed when their charter plane struck a flock of birds and was forced into an emergency landing on Tuesday, point guard Mike Conley said.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"Utah Jazz players feared they might be killed when their charter plane struck a flock of birds and was forced into an emergency landing on Tuesday, point guard Mike Conley said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The plane carrying the team to Memphis sustained “engine failure” following the collision shortly after takeoff, but returned safely to the Salt Lake airport."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Jazz boarded another flight a few hours later and landed in Memphis on Tuesday night."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“All of a sudden it felt like there was an explosion. That’s what it sounded like for most people on the plane,” Conley said after Wednesday’s 111-107 victory over Memphis Grizzlies."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“For 10 or 15 minutes, all of us on that flight were questioning if we were going to be here."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“The plane started to bounce and then tilted to the left, people in the back said they saw flames. The altitude started to drop, we started looking down wondering what happened."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“That’s how serious it was. I can’t speak for everybody, but I know guys were trying to text family just in case. It was that kind of situation.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"All-Star guard Donovan Mitchell, who has a fear of flying, did not accompany his team mates on the second plane and, shortly after takeoff, the Jazz said he was not with the team for “personal reasons.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Sixth man Jordan Clarkson said he “fully understood” why Mitchell chose not to travel."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“It got to that point where we were all on the plane like, ‘This might be the end,’” Clarkson said. “It was crazy.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Clarkson said an announcement from the pilots that they would be returning to Salt Lake airport helped calm the situation."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“That was comforting, but we were all looking out the window like, ‘man... just land anywhere,” he added. “Please put this plane on the ground, let us live and get past this.”"}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Bautista Agut ousts Medvedev to guarantee new ATP Masters champion
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Roberto Bautista Agut maintained his spotless record against Daniil Medvedev with a 6-4 6-2 quarter-final victory over the world number two at the Miami Open, ensuring there will be a new ATP Masters 1000 winner on Sunday.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"Roberto Bautista Agut maintained his spotless record against Daniil Medvedev with a 6-4 6-2 quarter-final victory over the world number two at the Miami Open, ensuring there will be a new ATP Masters 1000 winner on Sunday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Four of the top six on the men’s tour have skipped Miami, and with the exit of the Russian top seed on Wednesday there are no players with a Masters 1000 title left in the draw."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Medvedev, who replaced Rafa Nadal as No. 2 last month, went into the quarter-final with a 17-2 win-loss record for the season but had lost to the experienced Spaniard in their two previous career meetings."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"And there was no third time lucky for the Russian, with seventh seed Bautista Agut sealing the win in 92 minutes."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“To beat Daniil in two sets, it’s because I played great tennis,” the 32-year-old Spaniard told reporters. “I was very solid and I could play with a lot of rhythm, make him work a lot."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Physically I felt well on the court. It was a very tight first set. Well, it was a great match from my side.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"After eight tight games in the opening set, Bautista Agut nudged ahead with a service break for 5-4, leaving Medvedev to smash his racquet in frustration."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Spaniard, who will face 19-year-old Jannik Sinner for a place in Sunday’s final, did not look back from there."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“I was very focused on me, on the things I had to do on the next game,” he said. “Of course if he broke the racquet, it’s because he lost his patience."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“I think I did some great things to put him under pressure and to (make him) feel like this.”"}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: NFL: England's FA in talks with Jaguars over Wembley games
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: English soccer's governing body said it is in talks with the National Football League's (NFL) Jacksonville Jaguars to continue staging games at London's Wembley Stadium.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"English soccer’s governing body said it is in talks with the National Football League’s (NFL) Jacksonville Jaguars to continue staging games at London’s Wembley Stadium."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Jaguars had played at Wembley every year since 2013 and were due to feature in two games at London’s iconic venue in 2020 before the COVID-19 pandemic forced the NFL to scrap all international fixtures."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The NFL has staged games at Wembley since 2007 but its deal expired at the end of 2020."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"England’s Football Association (FA) told Sky Sports they were involved in “positive discussions with the Jacksonville Jaguars about hosting future games at Wembley Stadium”."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“The FA maintains good relationships with the NFL and the Jacksonville Jaguars having enjoyed over a decade of hosting games at Wembley Stadium,” they added."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The NFL said on Tuesday its owners had approved a plan to expand the regular season to 17 games from 16 and that from 2022 all 32 teams would play internationally at least once every eight years."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The NFL also said scheduling of up to four games per year outside the United States would focus initially on Canada, Europe, Mexico, South America and the United Kingdom."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Jaguars said they hoped to continue playing at Wembley, though they did not have an agreement in place."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Our annual home games in London have strengthened our franchise ... and established the Jaguars as the team to follow in London, UK and Europe,” Sky Sports quoted the team as saying."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Tennis: Bublik convinced teenager Sinner not 'human'
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Alexander Bublik tried everything to unsettle Jannik Sinner at the Miami Open on Wednesday but with the Italian teenager keeping his composure to win 7-6(5) 6-4 the Kazakh was left convinced he had been beaten by a robot.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"Alexander Bublik tried everything to unsettle Jannik Sinner at the Miami Open on Wednesday but with the Italian teenager keeping his composure to win 7-6(5) 6-4 the Kazakh was left convinced he had been beaten by a robot."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Bublik used underarm serves, drop shots and a sneak-attack serve return against Sinner during the quarter-final of the ATP Masters 1000 event but fell to his second straight defeat to the 19-year-old following a loss in Dubai in mid-March."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“You are not a human,” Bublik told Sinner at the net after the Italian had wrapped up the match. “You are 15-years-old and you play like this. Good job.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"2019 Next Gen ATP Finals winner Sinner has made rapid progress over the last two years, reaching his maiden Grand Slam quarter-final at last year’s French Open and now sits at a career-high 31st in the world."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In February he became the youngest player since Novak Djokovic in 2006 to win two ATP titles by claiming the Great Ocean Road Open after his Sofia Open title at the end of 2020."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“He’s not (human). That’s a fact,” world No.44 Bublik later told reporters. “For me it’s very surprising that the guy at his age has this mental toughness that many, many other players don’t have."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“I called him a robot couple of times during the match, but I do it in a very sincere way because he’s really, really a great player.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Sinner had to be focused against Bublik, who has already reached two finals this season."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Rallying from a break down in each set, the Italian was not only on the receiving end of a sneak-attack return and the underarm serves but also watched on helplessly as Bublik hit a 105mph forehand return against his serve."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Kazakh was also impressed with the shot and asked the chair umpire for the speed of his rocket return, adding that it was “the best forehand I’ve ever hit in my life”."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Surfing: Mask-free! Florence resumes Olympic preparations Down Under
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Some of the world's best surfers, including twice world champion John John Florence, are enjoying the relative freedom of life in Australia as they resume their preparations for surfing's Olympic debut at a World Surf League event this week.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"SYDNEY Some of the world’s best surfers, including twice world champion John John Florence, are enjoying the relative freedom of life in Australia as they resume their preparations for surfing’s Olympic debut at a World Surf League event this week."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The surfers underwent two weeks of quarantine after arriving Down Under and finally got back to competition in the Newcastle Cup on Thursday -- the first of four tour events being held in Australia over the next two months."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Australia has been more successful than most countries in containing the new coronavirus and Florence was very much enjoying the lack of restrictions in the port city northeast of Sydney."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“It’s pretty weird walking to a restaurant and like, ‘oh no I forgot my mask’ and then you realise you like just don’t need it here, so it’s cool,” the American said on the eve of competition on Wednesday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Seeing everyone out and about and exercising and surfing and beach days and everything, it just feels normal and so it definitely feels good to be back into that.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"As well as competing for a third world crown this year, Florence will have the chance in Tokyo to become the first Olympic champion in a sport which originated in his home state of Hawaii."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Pretty much all my Olympic preparations are just being here and competing on the tour, ... I feel like that’s pretty good preparation,” he added."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“You’re competing against the best surfers in the world and some of the most challenging conditions too. So a lot of my focus is just doing well in this and hopefully it will translate over the Olympics.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The 28-year-old made light of the three-month wait since his last competition at the Pipeline Masters by sweeping through his heat with the top score on Thursday morning."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Florence’s fellow Hawaiian and Tokyo hopeful Carissa Moore, the reigning women’s world champion, was also enjoying the freedoms of life in Australia ahead of the start of her competition later on Thursday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“It’s different to be here in Australia where there really isn’t COVID and to not have to wear a mask everyday,” she said on Wednesday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Being able to hug people especially, that’s something I really missed.”"}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Boxing: 'I need those big guys', Australian Tszyu looks to go global
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Australian super welterweight Tim Tszyu has once again voiced his desire to take on the best in the world after extending his record to 18-0 with a fifth round TKO of Dennis Hogan in Newcastle on Wednesday.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"SYDNEY Australian super welterweight Tim Tszyu has once again voiced his desire to take on the best in the world after extending his record to 18-0 with a fifth round TKO of Dennis Hogan in Newcastle on Wednesday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Tszyu registered his 14th career knockout when Hogan’s corner threw in the towel as the Irishman wilted under a barrage of powerful left-hand blows in front of a noisy crowd in the port city."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The son of former Russian-born undisputed light-welterweight world champion Kostya, Tszyu retained his World Boxing Organization (WBO) “Global” title but has long made it clear that he has his eyes on bigger prizes."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“I’m not satisfied,” Tszyu said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“I want to be a global boxing star. That’s my goal. It’s always been my goal and I need those big guys."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“We’re at that stage where I do believe I can compete with the big boys. I want an international fight. I want to be recognised globally.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Tszyu may have a wait on his hands as travel restrictions caused by the COVID-19 pandemic have added further complications to the already convoluted process of negotiating professional boxing bouts."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"American Jermell Charlo holds the World Boxing Council, World Boxing Association and International Boxing Federation titles in the division -- also known as junior or light middleweight -- and Argentine Brian Castano the WBO title."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Charlo is keen on a unification fight with Castano and Tszyu’s manager told Sydney’s Daily Telegraph before Wednesday’s fight that the Australian may not get his shot at a world title until next year."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“We don’t know,” Glen Jennings told the paper. “But we’ll be ready. And it doesn’t bother Tim. He’ll be patient.”"}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Massachusetts man pleads guilty to stealing Warhol paintings, selling fakes
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: A Massachusetts man pleaded guilty on Thursday to charges that he stole Andy Warhol paintings from a former college classmate living in South Korea and used them to produce forgeries that he sold.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"BOSTON A Massachusetts man pleaded guilty on Thursday to charges that he stole Andy Warhol paintings from a former college classmate living in South Korea and used them to produce forgeries that he sold."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Brian Walshe, 46, pleaded guilty in federal court in Boston to three counts, including a wire fraud charge, related to Warhol forgeries he sold to a Los Angeles gallery’s owner in 2016."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"He faces sentencing on Aug. 2. Under a plea deal, prosecutors agreed to recommend a prison term at the low end of the 30 to 37 months he faces under federal sentencing guidelines."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Walshe also agreed to forfeit the original Warhol paintings, which Assistant U.S. Attorney Timothy Moran said are now in the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s possession. He also agreed to pay $195,000 in restitution to two victims."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Prosecutors said that in 2011, Walshe visited a former Carnegie Mellon University classmate and his family in South Korea and offered to sell some of their art, including two Warhol paintings from his “Shadow” series."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The art also included a Warhol “Dollar Sign” painting, two prints by artist Keith Haring and a Chinese statuette."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Prosecutors said Walshe sold the “Dollar Sign” painting for $40,000 through the Christie’s auction house but never passed along the money. He then paid someone to make copies of the “Shadows” paintings, prosecutors said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"They said Walshe sold forged “Shadow” paintings to a Parisian art consultant for $145,000 and a likely fake “Dollar Sign” to his own dentist for $23,000."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Walshe also sold fake “Shadow” paintings to the California gallery owner for $80,000 after listing them on eBay with the claim that he “overpaid terribly” when he bought them in 2007 for $240,000, authorities said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"After the gallery owner realized they were forged, Walshe refunded him $30,000 but no more, prosecutors said."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Fewer people in the U.S. drank coffee during the pandemic: survey
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Fewer people drank coffee in the United States during the pandemic compared to levels seen before it, although the drink remained by far the most popular in the country, according to results of a national survey released on Thursday.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"NEW YORK Fewer people drank coffee in the United States during the pandemic compared to levels seen before it, although the drink remained by far the most popular in the country, according to results of a national survey released on Thursday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The survey commissioned by the National Coffee Association (NCA) found that 58% of people in the U.S. had at least one coffee the day before responding to the survey in January, versus 62% a year earlier."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The results, however, do not necessarily indicate a reduction in coffee volumes consumed in the U.S., the world’s largest market for the product, since many people while working from home drank more coffee than they normally would in offices."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Major coffee retailers in the U.S. posted increases in overall volumes sold during the pandemic."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"It is unclear if those increases offset the fall in out-of-home consumption."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The fact coffee shops are still operating with limitations might be one of the reasons for the coffee drinking fall."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The survey says people are drinking as much coffee in the morning as always, but drinking in the afternoon - a habit often linked to coffee shops visits - fell 4 percentage points."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Coffee continues to be America’s undisputed favorite beverage, even with the entire country in various stages of lockdown and footfall in coffee shops down massively this year,” said NCA President and CEO Bill Murray."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"He expects consumption to increase in coming months as the country recovers from the coronavirus."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"According to the survey, people continued to be divided about when they would feel comfortable to go out for coffee, with 33% saying they feel comfortable now and another 31% saying they will not be comfortable until the pandemic is over."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: COLUMN-U.S. oil production to start rising in second quarter: Kemp
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: U.S. crude oil production has stabilised and is set to start rising again, after the massive shock last year caused by the coronavirus epidemic and a volume war in the oil market between Saudi Arabia and Russia.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"(John Kemp is a Reuters market analyst. The views expressed are his own)"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"* Chartbook: \u003ca href=\"https://tmsnrt.rs/3whfxzO\"\u003etmsnrt.rs/3whfxzO\u003c/a\u003e"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"LONDON, April 1 U.S. crude oil production has stabilised and is set to start rising again, after the massive shock last year caused by the coronavirus epidemic and a volume war in the oil market between Saudi Arabia and Russia."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"U.S. production was 11.1 million barrels per day (bpd) in January, essentially unchanged from December, according to data published by the U.S. Energy Information Administration on Wednesday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Output was still down 1.7 million bpd compared with the same month a year earlier, and 1.8 million bpd from the cyclical peak in November 2019 (“Petroleum supply monthly”, EIA, March 31)."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"But production is no longer declining month on month as the industry has adapted and prices have rebounded after the crisis, creating a floor from which output is likely to start increasing by the middle of this year."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In the short term, output is likely to have declined again sharply in February because of the extreme cold that disrupted the Texas oilfields, and the interruption probably bled into the first part of March."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"But these are short-term interruptions driven by adverse weather rather than prices and market conditions so they should reverse rapidly."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"By April and certainly by May, U.S. production should start rising, slowly at first, then accelerating into the second half of the year (\u003ca href=\"https://tmsnrt.rs/3whfxzO\"\u003etmsnrt.rs/3whfxzO\u003c/a\u003e)."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Experience shows there is a lag of around four or five months between changes in the price of WTI futures and drilling rates, and then another lag of up to six months between changes in drilling and changes in output."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Front-month WTI futures prices hit a low of less than $20 per barrel in April 2020, and the number of rigs drilling for oil hit a cyclical low four months later in August."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Based on previous experience, output should hit a cyclical low roughly six months later, putting the trough sometime in the first quarter of 2021."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Since April 2020, front-month futures prices have roughly tripled to $60 per barrel, while the number of active rigs has nearly doubled since August."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The drilling recovery is broadly following the same trajectory as after the two previous slumps ending in May 2016 and May 2009."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Once the weather-related production problems in February and March are out of the way, the earlier increase in prices and drilling should filter through to higher production in the second quarter."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"U.S. production is likely to remain below its previous peak of almost 13 million bpd throughout 2021 and 2022, but as output starts to turn upward, the extra barrels will start competing for market share with OPEC+."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Related columns:"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"- Oil prices hit critical threshold for OPEC+ (Reuters, Feb. 12)"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"- Escalating oil prices signal need for more output (Reuters, Feb. 4)"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"- U.S. oil drilling set to start rising after cycle turns (Reuters, Sept. 2) (Editing by David Evans)"}]

test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Asia's cash differentials for 10 ppm gasoil weakened on Thursday, weighed down by ample supplies available in the region amid a sluggish demand recovery. Cash discounts for 10 ppm gasoil <GO10-SIN-DIF> widened to 31 cents per barrel to Singapore quotes, compared with a 29...
test_endpoint.articlesDescription:
[{"type":"p_table","content":"
    SINGAPORE, April 1 Asia's cash differentials for 10 ppm gasoil weakened on
Thursday, weighed down by ample supplies available in the region amid a sluggish demand
recovery.
    Cash discounts for 10 ppm gasoil GO10-SIN-DIF widened to 31 cents per barrel to Singapore
quotes, compared with a 29 cent discount a day earlier.
    Higher exports from China and India in recent weeks, alongside limited scopes of arbitrage
opportunities to Europe, is keeping the regional gasoil market grappling with supplies, traders
said.
    The exchange of futures for swaps (EFS), which determines the gasoil price spread between
Singapore and Northwest Europe, traded around minus $11 a tonne on Thursday – a
level that typically makes it unworkable for arbitrage shipments.
    Gasoil arbitrage to the west is usually profitable when the EFS trades at about minus $15 a
tonne or below, although it also depends on factors such as freight rates, according to trade
sources. 
    Traders and refiners, however, have been using some new-build supertankers to take diesel
from Asia to the West on their maiden voyages, partly buoyed by expectations that demand for the
industrial fuel would pick up pace following COVID-19 vaccinations.
    Refining margins, or cracks, for 10 ppm gasoil were at $5.27 per barrel over
Dubai crude during Asian trading hours, up from $4.76 per barrel on Wednesday.
    
    SINOCHEM-CHEMCHINA MERGER
    - China's State Council, the country's cabinet, has approved a long proposed merger of
Sinochem Group and China National Chemical Corp, or ChemChina, the Chinese state assets
regulator said on Wednesday.
    - The complex merger, which has been under discussion since at least 2017, would create the
world's biggest industrial chemicals firm.
    
    SINGAPORE CASH DEALS
    - No gasoil deals, no jet fuel trades
    
    OTHER NEWS
    - The oil market is likely to be in balance in the second half of 2021, even though European
coronavirus lockdowns and U.S. winter storms caused disruptions in March, crude and petroleum
products market price structures showed.
    - Crude oil prices rose on Thursday, recouping some of the previous session's losses on
expectations that a meeting of OPEC and its allies later on Thursday would yield output
constraint in the face of resurgent COVID-19 infections in some regions.

test_endpoint.articlesName: U.S. rolls out first update to flood insurance pricing in 50 years
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Hundreds of thousands of Americans will pay significantly more to insure their homes in coastal areas and flood zones under new rules released on Thursday by the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), the first major update to its pricing system in half a century.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"NEW YORK Hundreds of thousands of Americans will pay significantly more to insure their homes in coastal areas and flood zones under new rules released on Thursday by the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), the first major update to its pricing system in half a century."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The agency said that, over the coming year, it will phase in a price-setting method that marks an epochal shift in the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP), which was set up in 1968 to cover property in flood-prone areas."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"New premiums will be based on a property’s value, risk of flooding and other factors, rather than simply on a property’s elevation in a flood zone. They will take effect on Oct. 1, 2021, for new policies and April 1, 2022, for the rest, FEMA said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The NFIP currently provides $1.3 trillion in coverage through more than 5 million policies in the U.S., but has been losing money for years and is currently $20.5 billion in debt."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The new rules will mean hefty increases for expensive properties in wealthy coastal enclaves, said Jeremy Porter, head of research and development at First Street Foundation, a Brooklyn-New York based nonprofit that studies flood risk."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Current flood zone-based pricing was “basically a subsidy to people,” Porter said. Under FEMA’s new system, “pricing is based on your insurance risk.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"FEMA said it expects 4%, or more than 200,000 policies, will see significant premium increases, while about 1.15 million will see decreases, noting the change makes prices “more equitable.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In a study released in February of flood-prone properties rather than policies, First Street determined that more than 4 million would face increases and the average premium in flood zones would be $7,895 a year."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The numbers in First Street’s study are higher than FEMA’s because only about 30% of flood-prone properties carry NFIP coverage, Porter noted."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The changes mark the first update to FEMA’s pricing methods in 50 years, and are based on updated technology and FEMA’s evolving knowledge of flood risk, the agency said."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Canada govt's bid to create national securities regulator stalls
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: A decades-old bid by successive Canadian governments to create a national securities regulator officially stalled on Thursday, leaving the country reliant on a fragmented system long derided as inefficient and cumbersome.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"OTTAWA, April 1 A decades-old bid by successive Canadian governments to create a national securities regulator officially stalled on Thursday, leaving the country reliant on a fragmented system long derided as inefficient and cumbersome."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Canada is the only developed nation without an overarching regulatory body to oversees capital markets. Instead, a patchwork system of regulators in the 10 provinces and three northern territories requires companies to file documents in each jurisdiction separately."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In 2016, the Liberal government decided to create a regulatory system that provinces and territories could join voluntarily."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"But on Thursday, the organization charged with building that system paused operations, citing the need for provinces to reform their securities legislation."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“We are disappointed,” said Katherine Cuplinskas, a spokeswoman for Finance Minister Chrystia Freeland. Ottawa remained committed to establishing a national securities regulator, she added."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Some provinces stress that constitutionally, securities regulation falls under their jurisdiction. In 2011, the Supreme Court ruled that Ottawa could not unilaterally impose a new system on the provinces."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Quebec and Alberta, two powerful provinces, made clear they had no interest in Ottawa’s proposal for a voluntary regulatory system. Manitoba and two of the three territories also refused to sign on. (Reporting by David Ljunggren Editing by Marguerita Choy)"}]
