test_endpoint.articlesName: TD branch network unlikely to shrink despite growing technology push, CEO says
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Toronto-Dominion Bank is unlikely to close a large number of branches in Canada even as it accelerates investments in technology, as demand for in-person services has stayed strong during the coronavirus pandemic, its chief executive said on Thursday.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"TORONTO, April 1 Toronto-Dominion Bank is unlikely to close a large number of branches in Canada even as it accelerates investments in technology, as demand for in-person services has stayed strong during the coronavirus pandemic, its chief executive said on Thursday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“There was a view emerging generally that physical locations aren’t going to be attractive because of the pandemic,” Bharat Masrani, CEO of Canada’s second-biggest lender told Reuters."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“And we’re seeing to the contrary,” he added. “Sometimes we went to open more locations because there was so much demand that we couldn’t handle the traffic with all the health protocols.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"TD had 1,087 branches across Canada as of Jan. 31, just one fewer than a year earlier. It had 1,223 branches in the United States, three more than a year ago, although the bank said in February that it will close 82 branches that it deems redundant."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Even as it does so, it remains open to growing its U.S. business through acquisitions, Masrani said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"While TD expects its office employees to combine remote work with a few days in workplaces when they return to work, Masrani said it is still early to gauge the impact it will have on its office space needs. (Reporting By Nichola Saminather; Editing by David Gregorio)"}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: COLUMN-China's aluminium imports underpin physical premium surge: Andy Home
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Japanese aluminium buyers have agreed to pay the highest premium in six years to get their metal in the second quarter.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"(The opinions expressed here are those of the author, a columnist for Reuters)"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"* CME aluminium premiums: \u003ca href=\"https://tmsnrt.rs/3mci9u1\"\u003etmsnrt.rs/3mci9u1\u003c/a\u003e"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"* China's aluminium imports: \u003ca href=\"https://tmsnrt.rs/2OaC7J9\"\u003etmsnrt.rs/2OaC7J9\u003c/a\u003e"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"LONDON, April 1 Japanese aluminium buyers have agreed to pay the highest premium in six years to get their metal in the second quarter."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Japanese premium [PREM-ALU-JP\u0026gt;, which serves as a benchmark for the wider Asian market, has risen for three straight quarters to $148-149 per tonne over London Metal Exchange (LME) cash prices."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Rising physical premiums are a global phenomenon amid consumer restocking as the demand recovery gains momentum and turmoil in the shipping sector, which was restricting supply to consuming regions even before this week’s blockage of the Suez Canal."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"U.S. premiums are back above $400 per tonne for the first time in two years, while European premiums have leapt to three-year highs."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Even the world’s largest producer - China - seems to be running short of aluminium. Its continued purchases of metal from the international market are underpinning the global premium surge."},{"type":"heading","content":"CHINA’S IMPORTS STILL STRONG"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"China started importing primary aluminium in the second quarter of 2020. It was the first time the country had tapped international markets since the Global Financial Crisis."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Both aluminium demand and prices bounced back earlier and stronger than anywhere else last year thanks to China’s early exit from COVID-19 lockdown. That opened up an arbitrage window through which aluminium has been flowing ever since."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Imports remained strong in the first two months of this year, the country sucking in another 245,000 tonnes of primary aluminium and 141,000 tonnes of alloy."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The cumulative net draw on primary metal from the rest of the world now stands at 1.3 million tonnes, compared with 1.5 million tonnes during the 2008-2010 period."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"China turned net importer of alloy only briefly back then but this time around the shift to net importer status looks more structural with the cumulative tally standing at 1.1 million tonnes since the start of 2020."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"This new alloy trade is dominated by Malaysia, which has emerged as a processor of lower-grade scrap now banned by the Chinese authorities. A similar phenomenon is taking place in the copper scrap sector."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Chinese alloy imports, in other words, may be here to stay."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Primary imports may prove more volatile as the London-Shanghai arbitrage gyrates in and out of import-friendly territory."},{"type":"heading","content":"LOCATION, LOCATION, LOCATION"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"China’s pull on aluminium from the rest of the world is reducing the surplus built up during last year’s manufacturing collapse and therefore the amount of metal now available for restocking."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"It is also having an indirect influence on availability for European and U.S. manufacturers."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"After China’s import gates started opening last year, ever more aluminium has gravitated to the Asian region to capitalise on the potential for future buying."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Over 90% of the registered stocks in the LME warehouse system are now located at Asian locations, particularly Malaysia’s Port Klang, which holds 1.13 million tonnes."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"European locations hold a total 136,000 tonnes and those in the United States just 44,000 tonnes."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The same geographic distribution is evident in LME shadow stocks. The exchange’s most recent off-warrant stocks report showed 1.63 million tonnes of shadow stocks at the end of January, of which 1.38 million tonnes were sitting at Asian good-delivery locations."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"It’s worth remembering that this is very different from how things played out in 2009-2010, when global surplus accumulated at LME locations first in the United States (Detroit) and then in Europe (Vlissingen)."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Today most of the readily-accessible inventory is located within easy shipping distance of China."},{"type":"heading","content":"BUYERS EXPOSED"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"This mass relocation of aluminium eastwards has left buyers elsewhere short of inventory cover, leaving them exposed to the trials and tribulations of the shipping sector, which was facing severe disruption from COVID-19 backlogs even before the Ever Given blocked one of the world’s busiest traffic arteries."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"U.S. buyers have been further hampered by a quota on Canadian imports, which was the condition set by the administration of President Donald Trump for exempting Canada from the 10% aluminium import tariff."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Unfortunately for U.S. manufacturers, the quota applies specifically to the commodity-grade ingot which the country now appears to be running short of, which is why the U.S. Midwest premium has risen particularly sharply since the start of the year."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"With the physical supply chain struggling to supply units in the right place at the right time and little sign of any easing in the stressed shipping sector, premiums look set for further rises in the short term."},{"type":"heading","content":"COMPETITION FOR METAL"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Physical aluminium buyers, not for the first time, find themselves competing for units with stocks financiers, who have tied up large amounts of metal in profitable deals using the LME forward curve, which spent a large part of last year in finance-friendly contango."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Rising premiums are a sign of this increased competition for metal. High premiums are an upfront cost for financiers and instill a level of risk into financing stocks, given the potential for premiums to drop over the course of a deal."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Physical demand can also be expected to tighten the LME curve, reducing the ability of stocks financiers to lock in higher futures prices."},{"type":"inline_items","wrapper_element":"p","items":[{"type":"text","content":"The benchmark LME cash-to-three-months time-spread "},{"type":"ric","symbol":"CMAL0-3","ric_type":"stock"},{"type":"text","content":" closed Wednesday valued at a contango of $24.50 per tonne. Two weeks ago it was $35.50."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":"There is no contango at all on the Shanghai Futures Exchange (ShFE) aluminium contract. The futures curve is backwardated through October."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"There is evidently still considerable supply stress for commodity-grade metal in the Chinese domestic market."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Inner Mongolian power restrictions have fuelled the market heat. Suggestions that the State Reserves Bureau might offload some of its stockpiled aluminium bear all the hallmarks of the authorities trying to damp the speculative flames."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Chinese domestic aluminium market is as disjointed as it’s been in many years and there’s a lot of metal sitting in Asia on the premise the country’s going to need more primary metal."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"That’s bad news for aluminium consumers everywhere else."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: UK's Next says landlords must be pragmatic to keep shops open
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: British fashion retailer Next said it will retain stores as long as landlords continue to be pragmatic on the rents they charge.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"LONDON, April 1 British fashion retailer Next said it will retain stores as long as landlords continue to be pragmatic on the rents they charge."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“As they have been so far, if landlords continue to be as pragmatic in determining rents going forward then that will allow shops to stay open,” CEO Simon Wolfson told reporters on Thursday after Next reported annual results."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In Next’s 2020-21 year 80 of its store leases expired, it closed 18 branches and renegotiated rents in 62 stores, achieving an average reduction in rent of 58%."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Wolfson said Britain also needed a new settlement on business rates that brings them down to a level commensurate with the value of shops today."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“At the end of the day if consumers don’t want to shop in shops they won’t continue to,” he added."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: COLUMN-U.S. lawmakers' generosity on pensions is just a starting point for bolstering retirement security
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: The U.S. Congress recently rescued the retirements of more than 1 million workers who faced the prospect that the pensions they earned and had been promised might evaporate.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"(The opinions expressed here are those of the author, a columnist for Reuters.)"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"CHICAGO, April 1 The U.S. Congress recently rescued the retirements of more than 1 million workers who faced the prospect that the pensions they earned and had been promised might evaporate."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The American Rescue Act signed into law last month by Democratic President Joe Biden allocated $86 billion for grants to struggling multiemployer pension funds that would allow them to continue paying full benefits. The law authorizes the Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation (PBGC) to make the grants, which do not need to be repaid."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The generosity of the move came as a surprise. Previously, Democrats had been pushing a package of low-interest loans to aid the multiemployer funds, while Republicans wanted to boost insurance premiums paid by employers, add new premiums paid by plan participants, and force more conservative accounting assumptions."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"But the Democratic majority is looking at things a bit differently this year. “They felt that since we’ve bailed out the banks and airlines over the years, why aren’t we doing that here? We’ve got the votes,” said Gene Kalwarski, CEO of Cheiron Inc, an actuarial consulting firm that advises multiemployer plans."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The bailout makes sense. Multiemployer plans are created under collective bargaining agreements and jointly funded by groups of employers in industries like construction, trucking, mining and food retailing. The funds declined following stock market crashes in 2001 and 2008-09, and due to industrial decline that led to consolidation and sliding employment. Moreover, the pension plans’ financial problems threatened the health of the PBGC as well (\u003ca href=\"https://reut.rs/3st48KT\"\u003ereut.rs/3st48KT\u003c/a\u003e)."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"But so long as Congress is casting a benign eye on the well-being of these pensioners, I have a short list of other “must-do” retirement items for the consideration of lawmakers. And these are reforms that will impact a much larger - and more demographically diverse - group of retirees now and in the years ahead than the multiemployer plan fix."},{"type":"heading","content":"EXPAND SOCIAL SECURITY"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The economic devastation wrought by the pandemic makes expansion of our only universal retirement income program a critical item. As a presidential candidate, Biden proposed a series of moderate expansions that should be passed into law. One would award Social Security benefit credits to caregivers for time spent out of the workforce - a change that would especially benefit women, who already face a substantial retirement gender gap."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The president also proposed expanding benefits for widows and seniors who had collected payments for 20 years. He also favors shifting to a more generous yardstick for determining Social Security’s annual cost-of-living adjustment."},{"type":"heading","content":"REDUCE THE MEDICARE AGE"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Short of Medicare for All, making Medicare available to younger workers is the smartest way to expand the program (\u003ca href=\"https://reut.rs/39j8uga\"\u003ereut.rs/39j8uga\u003c/a\u003e). And with millions of Americans retiring earlier than expected due to the pandemic, expansion would help them control their healthcare costs."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Senator Bernie Sanders is pushing to reduce the age of Medicare eligibility from 65 to 60 or lower as part of the big infrastructure spending bill now taking shape. His proposal also would add dental, vision and hearing care to Original Medicare. That change would plug a coverage gap that makes absolutely no sense, considering that these services are a critical part of overall good preventive healthcare (\u003ca href=\"https://reut.rs/3waEtc3\"\u003ereut.rs/3waEtc3\u003c/a\u003e)."},{"type":"heading","content":"REDUCE LONG-TERM CARE RISK"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Medicare also should be expanded to include coverage of long-term care. This remains one of the largest gaps in our retirement security insurance net: the commercial insurance market continues to shrink, and Medicaid remains the largest payor - and the one of last resort."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The smart solution would add a baseline of coverage to Medicare, with all workers contributing through the course of their working lives. This could be coupled with streamlined, less expensive private policies that could be sold as add-ons to basic Medicare."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"This approach was proposed by several bipartisan research groups in 2016, and it is an idea worth revisiting (\u003ca href=\"https://reut.rs/3u5430w\"\u003ereut.rs/3u5430w\u003c/a\u003e). And the Medicare for All Act of 2021 recently introduced in the House of Representatives proposes comprehensive long-term care coverage for older adults and people with disabilities."},{"type":"heading","content":"FUND AFFORDABLE SENIOR HOUSING"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The share of households headed by someone over age 65 will jump from 26% in 2018 to 34% in 2034, according to the Joint Center for Housing Studies at Harvard University - and the share of households age 80 and over will grow even more rapidly."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The nation’s housing stock is nowhere near ready to accommodate this age wave. A tiny percentage of housing units has the age-appropriate modifications such as single-floor living, no-step entry, and extra-wide halls and doors for wheelchair access."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"And affordability is a critical issue. Nearly 10 million retirement-age households face cost burdens related to housing, meaning that housing consumes more than 30% of their income, according to Harvard. Homelessness among older adults is rising (\u003ca href=\"https://reut.rs/3cuDCLJ\"\u003ereut.rs/3cuDCLJ\u003c/a\u003e)."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Expanded funding for Section 8 rental subsidies would help, along with increased funding for the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit program and increasing funding for Section 202 (Supportive Housing for the Elderly Program), which has historically funded new construction as well as operating costs for housing for older adults, said Jennifer Molinsky, senior research associate at the Harvard center."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“We need both more rental assistance as well as more funding to expand the supply of affordable housing,” she said."}]

test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: The U.S. Congress recently rescued the retirements of more than 1 million workers who faced the prospect that the pensions they earned and had been promised might evaporate.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"(The opinions expressed here are those of the author, a columnist for Reuters.)"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"CHICAGO, April 1 The U.S. Congress recently rescued the retirements of more than 1 million workers who faced the prospect that the pensions they earned and had been promised might evaporate."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The American Rescue Act signed into law last month by Democratic President Joe Biden allocated $86 billion for grants to struggling multiemployer pension funds that would allow them to continue paying full benefits. The law authorizes the Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation (PBGC) to make the grants, which do not need to be repaid."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The generosity of the move came as a surprise. Previously, Democrats had been pushing a package of low-interest loans to aid the multiemployer funds, while Republicans wanted to boost insurance premiums paid by employers, add new premiums paid by plan participants, and force more conservative accounting assumptions."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"But the Democratic majority is looking at things a bit differently this year. “They felt that since we’ve bailed out the banks and airlines over the years, why aren’t we doing that here? We’ve got the votes,” said Gene Kalwarski, CEO of Cheiron Inc, an actuarial consulting firm that advises multiemployer plans."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The bailout makes sense. Multiemployer plans are created under collective bargaining agreements and jointly funded by groups of employers in industries like construction, trucking, mining and food retailing. The funds declined following stock market crashes in 2001 and 2008-09, and due to industrial decline that led to consolidation and sliding employment. Moreover, the pension plans’ financial problems threatened the health of the PBGC as well (\u003ca href=\"https://reut.rs/3st48KT\"\u003ereut.rs/3st48KT\u003c/a\u003e)."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"But so long as Congress is casting a benign eye on the well-being of these pensioners, I have a short list of other “must-do” retirement items for the consideration of lawmakers. And these are reforms that will impact a much larger - and more demographically diverse - group of retirees now and in the years ahead than the multiemployer plan fix."},{"type":"heading","content":"EXPAND SOCIAL SECURITY"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The economic devastation wrought by the pandemic makes expansion of our only universal retirement income program a critical item. As a presidential candidate, Biden proposed a series of moderate expansions that should be passed into law. One would award Social Security benefit credits to caregivers for time spent out of the workforce - a change that would especially benefit women, who already face a substantial retirement gender gap."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The president also proposed expanding benefits for widows and seniors who had collected payments for 20 years. He also favors shifting to a more generous yardstick for determining Social Security’s annual cost-of-living adjustment."},{"type":"heading","content":"REDUCE THE MEDICARE AGE"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Short of Medicare for All, making Medicare available to younger workers is the smartest way to expand the program (\u003ca href=\"https://reut.rs/39j8uga\"\u003ereut.rs/39j8uga\u003c/a\u003e). And with millions of Americans retiring earlier than expected due to the pandemic, expansion would help them control their healthcare costs."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Senator Bernie Sanders is pushing to reduce the age of Medicare eligibility from 65 to 60 or lower as part of the big infrastructure spending bill now taking shape. His proposal also would add dental, vision and hearing care to Original Medicare. That change would plug a coverage gap that makes absolutely no sense, considering that these services are a critical part of overall good preventive healthcare (\u003ca href=\"https://reut.rs/3waEtc3\"\u003ereut.rs/3waEtc3\u003c/a\u003e)."},{"type":"heading","content":"REDUCE LONG-TERM CARE RISK"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Medicare also should be expanded to include coverage of long-term care. This remains one of the largest gaps in our retirement security insurance net: the commercial insurance market continues to shrink, and Medicaid remains the largest payor - and the one of last resort."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The smart solution would add a baseline of coverage to Medicare, with all workers contributing through the course of their working lives. This could be coupled with streamlined, less expensive private policies that could be sold as add-ons to basic Medicare."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"This approach was proposed by several bipartisan research groups in 2016, and it is an idea worth revisiting (\u003ca href=\"https://reut.rs/3u5430w\"\u003ereut.rs/3u5430w\u003c/a\u003e). And the Medicare for All Act of 2021 recently introduced in the House of Representatives proposes comprehensive long-term care coverage for older adults and people with disabilities."},{"type":"heading","content":"FUND AFFORDABLE SENIOR HOUSING"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The share of households headed by someone over age 65 will jump from 26% in 2018 to 34% in 2034, according to the Joint Center for Housing Studies at Harvard University - and the share of households age 80 and over will grow even more rapidly."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The nation’s housing stock is nowhere near ready to accommodate this age wave. A tiny percentage of housing units has the age-appropriate modifications such as single-floor living, no-step entry, and extra-wide halls and doors for wheelchair access."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"And affordability is a critical issue. Nearly 10 million retirement-age households face cost burdens related to housing, meaning that housing consumes more than 30% of their income, according to Harvard. Homelessness among older adults is rising (\u003ca href=\"https://reut.rs/3cuDCLJ\"\u003ereut.rs/3cuDCLJ\u003c/a\u003e)."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Expanded funding for Section 8 rental subsidies would help, along with increased funding for the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit program and increasing funding for Section 202 (Supportive Housing for the Elderly Program), which has historically funded new construction as well as operating costs for housing for older adults, said Jennifer Molinsky, senior research associate at the Harvard center."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“We need both more rental assistance as well as more funding to expand the supply of affordable housing,” she said."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: ECB's growth forecast at risk amid infections surge, Weidmann says
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: The European Central Bank's three-week-old forecast for a 4.0% economic rebound in the euro zone this year is already in jeopardy as a surge in COVID-19 infections forces governments to delay the reopening of businesses, ECB policymaker Jens Weidmann said in remarks published...
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"FRANKFURT, April 1 The European Central Bank’s three-week-old forecast for a 4.0% economic rebound in the euro zone this year is already in jeopardy as a surge in COVID-19 infections forces governments to delay the reopening of businesses, ECB policymaker Jens Weidmann said in remarks published on Thursday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The euro zone is lagging far behind an economic rebound in the United States as it struggles to control a third wave of the coronavirus pandemic and its vaccination campaign has been marred by delays."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Weidmann, president of Germany’s Bundesbank, warned the ECB’s GDP forecast for this year, which was revised up as recently as March 11, might not be met if pandemic-fighting curbs are extended."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Due to the currently strong increase in the number of infections, it could take longer for the protective measures to be relaxed than assumed in the March forecast,” Weidmann told journalists late on Wednesday for publication the following day."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“In this case, the forecast of the GDP growth rate for the euro area in 2021 might no longer be sustainable.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"He cautioned that a successful vaccination campaign could still allow the currency bloc to make up for the lost ground in the remainder of the year."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Weidmann backed the central bank’s decision in March to accelerate its bond purchases -- a form of monetary stimulus -- despite a temporary bounce in inflation, as subdued economic activity was likely to keep a lid on prices."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"He added the recent back-up in German bond yields mainly reflected better economic prospects in the United States and warned that this might still filter through to higher borrowing costs for euro zone households and companies. (Reporting by Francesco Canepa; Editing by Catherine Evans)"}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Lockdown home-working thwarts Germany's burglars
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: The number of break-ins in Germany fell to an all-time low last year because so many people were working from home, the insurance industry association GDV said on Thursday.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"BERLIN, April 1 The number of break-ins in Germany fell to an all-time low last year because so many people were working from home, the insurance industry association GDV said on Thursday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Insurance claims for break-ins fell to 85,000 in 2020, 10,000 fewer than the year before and the lowest level since records began in 1998."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“The fall in break-ins is largely due to people spending so much time at home thanks to the coronavirus pandemic,” GDV head Joerg Asmussen said. “Burglars often had no opportunity to carry out the deed.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"As a result, damages fell to 230 million euros ($269.68 million), 70 million euros less than the year before, while the average size of an individual claim fell by 10% to 2,750 euros, the association said. ($1 = 0.8529 euros) (Reporting by Klaus Lauer; Writing by Thomas Escritt; Editing by Alison Williams)"}]

test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: * Biden's EV plan boosts lithium, copper-exposed stocks (Updates to close)
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"* AMP jumps nearly 5% after naming new CEO"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"* Tech stocks mark best day since March 16, up about 2.5%"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"* Biden’s EV plan boosts lithium, copper-exposed stocks (Updates to close)"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"April 1 Australian shares settled higher on Thursday, wrapping up the holiday-shortened week on a firm note as investor cheered an end to Brisbane lockdown ahead of the long Easter weekend."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The S\u0026amp;P/ASX 200 index closed up 0.6% at 6,828.70, with gold and technology stocks leading the gains. Both Australian and New Zealand markets are closed on Friday and Monday for Easter holidays."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Market participants cheered after Australia ended a lockdown of its third-biggest city Brisbane, just in time for Easter holidays, as only one new locally transmitted COVID-19 case in Queensland state eased fears of a widespread outbreak."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“We haven’t been told anything today that we’re going to continue on into Easter, which is really good news,” said Brad Smoling, managing director of Smoling Stockbroking, of the three-day lockdown in Brisbane."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Technology stocks closed about 2.5% higher in their best session since March 16, following a tech-led rally on Wall Street."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The S\u0026amp;P 500 and Nasdaq rose on Wednesday, boosted by gains in technology shares, and the three major Wall Street indexes registered their fourth straight quarterly rise as investors positioned themselves for U.S. President Joe Biden’s massive infrastructure plan."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Megaport gained 5.7%, while Afterpay added about 4%."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Gold stocks ended 2.9% higher, notching their best session in two weeks, as bullion prices rebounded."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"West African Resources advanced 7.8%, while De Grey Mining climbed 8.6%."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Miners added 1.6%, lifted by higher iron ore prices. BHP Group rose 0.8%, while Rio Tinto gained 1.1%."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Lithium and copper-exposed stocks advanced as Biden’s $2.25 trillion infrastructure plan pushed for investments and subsidies on electric vehicles."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The heavyweight financial sector climbed 0.4%, bolstered by a near 5% gain in AMP Ltd after the embattled wealth manager named its new chief executive officer."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"New Zealand’s benchmark S\u0026amp;P/NZX 50 index closed 0.6% lower at 12,488.31. Vista Group and Stride Property were the top losers. (Reporting by Nikhil Subba in Bengaluru; Editing by Subhranshu Sahu)"}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: China's home prices extend gains in March, defy renewed curbs - survey
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: China's monthly new home prices maintained steady growth in March, while the resale housing market also saw an uptick, despite a renewed crackdown on property speculation, a private-sector survey showed on Thursday.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"BEIJING, April 1 China’s monthly new home prices maintained steady growth in March, while the resale housing market also saw an uptick, despite a renewed crackdown on property speculation, a private-sector survey showed on Thursday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"New home prices in 100 cities rose 0.2% in March from a month earlier, unchanged from February’s pace, according to data from China Index Academy, one of the country’s largest independent real estate research firms."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"More cities reported monthly gains, with the number up to 76 from 66 in February, while 23 cities posted lower home prices compared with 27 in the preceding month."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In another sign of strong demand, growth in second-hand home prices quickened to 0.44% in March from previous month, compared with 0.28% in February."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“We saw a jump in supply of new housing projects in major cities, as developers sped up sales in March, which is a traditionally a peak season,” said China Index Academy Research Director Cao Jingjing."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Cao also noted Guangzhou and Chongqing saw strong residential property markets, while demand in the northern cities of Taiyuan and Tianjin waned."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Authorities have maintained a tight grip on the sector, with measures ranging from stepped-up scrutiny on illegal flows of funds to fixed price references for secondary market financing in some cities."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The government has also vowed to boost residential land supply to contain fast-rising home prices."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In a whack-a-mole clampdown, the southern capital city of Nanchang was last week ordered to revoke its easing policies one day after their release, as policymakers remained vigilant to any bubbles."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"China’s land sales by volume rose 11% in the first quarter from a year earlier, CIA data showed. (Reporting by Lusha Zhang and Tony Munroe; Editing by Sam Holmes)"}]

test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: * AMP tops ASX200 gainers with 5.5% rise, co appoints group CEO
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"* AMP tops ASX200 gainers with 5.5% rise, co appoints group CEO"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"* Financials dip as regulators take action on Macquarie Bank, CBA"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"* Australia, New Zealand markets closed on Friday"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"April 1 Australian shares rose on Thursday, tracking an overnight Wall Street rally that was driven by tech stocks and as U.S. President Joe Biden’s multi-trillion-dollar infrastructure investment plan lifted investor sentiment globally."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The S\u0026amp;P/ASX 200 index climbed 0.2% to 6,804.90 by 0027 GMT, also helped by data showing Australian home prices rose at the fastest pace in three decades in March and February retail sales fell less than expected."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"However, the index was down 0.2% so far in the week. Australia and New Zealand markets are closed on Friday for the Good Friday holiday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"On Wednesday, Biden called for a sweeping use of government power to reshape the world’s largest economy and counter China’s rise in a $2 trillion-plus proposal."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Sentiment from U.S. markets and strong mining gains lifted the Australian benchmark index, but market moves are likely to be quieter given the long weekend ahead, said James Tao, a market analyst at CommSec."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In Australia, miners rose 1.3% as Chinese iron ore futures climbed in early trade. BHP Group and Rio Tinto added 0.6% and 1.4%, respectively."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Financials was largely weaker amid regulatory pressure."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Macquarie Group traded about 1.5% lower after the prudential regulator ordered the company’s banking unit to increase its cash reserves following material breaches of prudential standards that it said raised serious concerns about the lender’s risk controls."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Commonwealth Bank of Australia slipped about 0.5%. test_endpoint.articlesName: Breakingviews-Capital Calls-Chinese loans attach unexpected strings
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: FINE PRINT. China is sabotaging some international credit cooperation, but not in the way typically feared. An analysis of 100 of the country’s loans to poor countries over the last two decades by U.S. research outfit AidData undermines arguments that Beijing ensnares them...
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"HONG KONG (Reuters Breakingviews) - FINE PRINT. China is sabotaging some international credit cooperation, but not in the way typically feared. An analysis of 100 of the country’s loans to poor countries over the last two decades by U.S. research outfit AidData undermines arguments that Beijing ensnares them in so-called debt traps: It neither charged predatory rates nor demanded strategic assets like ports as collateral. And although the sample used reflects less than 5% of an estimated $900 billion of credit China has extended to developing countries, the contractual fine print reinforces fears about China."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In addition to overly broad confidentiality clauses, 75% of loans scrutinised were excluded from restructuring deals with the Paris Club group of developed-economy lenders. China Development Bank often demands that if borrowers take action deemed adverse to any Chinese entity, it triggers a default. For wealthy nations seeking to arrange debt relief, the AidData findings ultimately raise as many trust issues as they resolve. (By Pete Sweeney)"}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Breakingviews - Chinese AI dragon confronts fiery new realities
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Megvii Technology’s political problems have turned into financial ones. The Chinese developer of artificial-intelligence hardware and software is angling to go public again, this time in Shanghai after a U.S. trade ban factored into its abandonment of a Hong Kong listing...
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"HONG KONG (Reuters Breakingviews) - Megvii Technology’s political problems have turned into financial ones. The Chinese developer of artificial-intelligence hardware and software is angling to go public again, this time in Shanghai after a U.S. trade ban factored into its abandonment of a Hong Kong listing attempt a year ago. The mainland venue makes more sense, but the numbers are far from compelling."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Best known for its facial recognition system, Megvii generates 64% of its revenue from selling technology mainly to Chinese government clients so they can identify and track residents for security and social order. Its market share is second only to Sensetime in consultancy IDC’s rankings of the country’s four so-called AI dragons, which include Yitu and CloudWalk. In October 2019, Washington blocked Megvii and others from buying U.S. components without government approval because of their alleged involvement in human rights violations related to repression of China’s Muslim minority populations."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In its prospectus seeking to raise some 6 billion yuan ($924 million) from selling China Depositary Receipts on Shanghai’s STAR board, Megvii denied any significant impact from the U.S. ban. Even if true, its results are troubling."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Despite Covid-19 contact-tracing initiatives that lifted Chinese demand for surveillance capabilities, Megvii’s revenue growth had been slowing, and for the first nine months of 2020 tallied about $109 million compared to nearly $200 million for all of 2019. With heavy research and development spending, the roughly $150 million net loss attributable to shareholders through September, excluding one-off items, was wider again after it more than doubled the previous year."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The company, valued at $4 billion in a fundraising last May, warns about “continuously” worsening negative cash flows. Moreover, its 2018 revenue and gross profit were significantly smaller than what was disclosed in the Hong Kong IPO documents, a discrepancy Megvii did not explain."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"It has run into more awkward timing too. Last month, Yitu requested, without any stated reason, that its $1.1 billion Shanghai listing application be suspended. Alibaba and its financial technology affiliate Ant, which own a combined 29% of Megvii, have been targeted in Beijing’s expanding tech crackdown. Megvii is trying to grow its small supply-chain management segment, but so much dependence on government contracts adds more policy risk. This artificial intelligence provider presents some real concerns."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Europe should match U.S.'s economic stimulus ambition: France
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Europe should match the ambition shown by the United States with its huge new economic stimulus, French Finance Minister Bruno Le Maire said on Thursday.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"GENEVA Europe should match the ambition shown by the United States with its huge new economic stimulus, French Finance Minister Bruno Le Maire said on Thursday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The new administration of U.S. President Joe Biden is already making payments to households under a new $1.9 trillion COVID-19 relief package and plans to plough $2.3 trillion into infrastructure investments to fire up the world’s biggest economy."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Whatever we may think about it, the American stimulus plan shows ambition, and the return of U.S. ambition is a good thing,” Le Maire said in a speech at the Geneva Graduate Institute."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“The best response to U.S. ambition isn’t to fight it. It is to match it. Europe needs to challenge itself like America does,” he added."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"While European countries’ support for their economies last year was on par with that seen in the United States, the new U.S. stimulus dwarves the European Union’s 750 billion euro ($881 billion) economic recovery plan."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Though the 27-nation bloc agreed the landmark stimulus fund last summer, EU governments are still submitting detailed plans on how they aim to spend money from the fund, which many still need to ratify."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Meanwhile, the European Commission and the governments also have yet to agree on structural reforms that are supposed to accompany the stimulus, while domestic politics in some countries and a legal challenge before the German constitutional court has fuelled concerns about possible delays."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"As some European countries tighten their coronavirus restrictions in the face of a sluggish vaccine roll-out, calls are emerging not only for Europe to speed up its recovery plans but to increase its size."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Le Maire said that Europe needed to focus on returning as quickly as possible to pre-crisis levels of economic activity and not restoring public finances."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“We shouldn’t get bogged down in complicated calculations about whether we should revert to fiscal discipline in January or September 2022,” he said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"($1 = 0.8511 euros)"}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: India power demand falls for first time in 35 years
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: India's annual electricity demand fell for the first time in at least 35 years in the fiscal year to March, government data reviewed by Reuters showed, mainly due to strict coronavirus-induced lockdowns across the country.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"CHENNAI India’s annual electricity demand fell for the first time in at least 35 years in the fiscal year to March, government data reviewed by Reuters showed, mainly due to strict coronavirus-induced lockdowns across the country."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Power demand fell 1% during the year ended March 2021, the data showed, mainly due to the imposition of lockdowns that resulted in a decline in electricity consumption for six straight months ending in August."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Graphic: India's annual electricity demand growth"},{"type":"infographics","media_type":"static","content":"https://graphics.reuters.com/INDIA-ELECTRICITY/DEMAND/yzdvxezgmpx/chart_eikon.jpg"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Demand for electricity has picked up since, and generation grew 23.3% in March from a year earlier, a Reuters analysis of daily load despatch data from federal grid operator POSOCO showed, making it the seventh consecutive monthly increase and the fastest since March 2010."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Power generation fell 0.2% during the year 2020/21, compared with the previous year, the POSOCO data showed."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Power generation in March grew much faster than the average increase of 6% in the last six months, mainly because India had imposed an intense nationwide lockdown in the last week of March 2020, resulting in a dramatic fall in power usage."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Graphic: India's monthly power generation over last two years"},{"type":"infographics","media_type":"static","content":"https://graphics.reuters.com/INDIA-ELECTRICITY/DEMAND/yzdpxezwbvx/chart_eikon.jpg"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Electricity demand has been steadily increasing this year due to a pickup in economic activity and amid higher temperatures being recorded in March in North India, which could have led to higher use of air conditioning."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Exclusive: India's March gold imports surge 471% to a record 160 T – government source
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: India's gold imports in March surged 471% from a year earlier to a record 160 tonnes, a government source told Reuters on Thursday, as a reduction in import taxes and a correction in prices from record highs drew retail buyers and jewellers.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"MUMBAI India’s gold imports in March surged 471% from a year earlier to a record 160 tonnes, a government source told Reuters on Thursday, as a reduction in import taxes and a correction in prices from record highs drew retail buyers and jewellers."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Higher imports by the world’s second-biggest bullion consumer could support benchmark gold prices, which have corrected nearly 17% from an all-time high of $2,072 in August 2020."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The surge in imports could increase India’s trade deficit and pressure the rupee."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"India imported a record 321 tonnes in the March quarter, up from 124 tonnes a year ago, the source said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The source asked to remain anonymous since he is not authorised to speak to the media."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In value terms, March imports surged to $8.4 billion from $1.23 billion a year ago, he said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In February, India slashed import duties on gold to 10.75% tax from 12.5% to boost retail demand and curtail smuggling into the South Asian country."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Many consumers had postponed buying due to higher prices. They rushed to buy after prices corrected sharply,” said Harshad Ajmera, the proprietor of JJ Gold House, a wholesaler in the city of Kolkata."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In March, local gold futures hit a one-year low of 43,320 rupees per 10 grams."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Jewellers were building inventories after seeing robust retail demand, said a Mumbai-based bullion dealer with a gold importing bank."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Throughout the month gold was trading at premium because of jewellery demand,” the dealer said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Last month dealers charged premiums of up to $6 an ounce over official domestic prices, inclusive of 10.75% import and 3% sales levies."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"India’s gold imports in April could fall below 100 tonnes as jewellers fear government could impose lockdown to arrest rising coronavirus infections, the dealer said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"India reported 72,330 new COVID-19 infections overnight, data from the health ministry showed on Thursday, the highest since Oct. 11."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: India moves to deport Rohingya girl to Myanmar, draws criticism
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: A 14-year-old Rohingya Muslim girl has been taken to a border town in northeastern India for deportation to Myanmar, police officials said on Thursday, as the U.N. refugee agency and rights groups pressed New Delhi to halt the process.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"NEW DELHI A 14-year-old Rohingya Muslim girl has been taken to a border town in northeastern India for deportation to Myanmar, police officials said on Thursday, as the U.N. refugee agency and rights groups pressed New Delhi to halt the process."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Tens of thousands of Rohingya, who are denied citizenship in their home country Myanmar, have lived in India for years but Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government regards them as a security threat and has started detaining them."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Police have taken the girl to a border crossing in Manipur state, where paperwork was being finalised to send her back to coup-hit Myanmar. She had been sheltered for more than a year in the neighbouring Indian state of Assam, while her family lived as refugees in Bangladesh’s Cox’s Bazar."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“It is under process,” Assam police official B.L. Meena told Reuters, referring to her deportation. “This was previously scheduled.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Diba Roy, founder of non-profit Nivedita Nari Sangshta in Assam’s Silchar town that had cared for the girl, said local authorities had been informed that she did not have family in Myanmar."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“But she was sent to Myanmar,” Roy said, adding that she had received instructions from federal authorities to hand over the girl to local police this week. “We have only obeyed the order.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"India’s foreign and home ministries did not immediately respond to requests for comment."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The U.N. refugee agency, UNHCR, opposed the deportation."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“The situation in Myanmar is not yet conducive for voluntary return in a safe, secure, and sustainable manner, and returning the child to Myanmar may place her at immediate risk of serious harm,” a UNHCR spokesperson said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Police in India’s northern region of Jammu and Kashmir last month detained more than 150 Rohingya refugees and started a process to deport them back to Myanmar."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"India is not a signatory to the U.N. Refugee Convention and rejects a U.N. position that deporting the Rohingya violates the principle of refoulement – sending refugees back to a place where they face danger."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Indian growth outlook brightens but COVID-19 casting a shadow: Reuters poll
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: India's economy will grow at a faster pace this fiscal year than previously thought, according to a Reuters poll of economists who warned a surge in coronavirus cases was the biggest risk to growth.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"BENGALURU India’s economy will grow at a faster pace this fiscal year than previously thought, according to a Reuters poll of economists who warned a surge in coronavirus cases was the biggest risk to growth."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Downside risks remain high as daily reported coronavirus cases touched a peak not seen since Oct. 11 on Thursday and a few states have renewed restrictions, although the continuing vaccination drive could avoid a complete lockdown."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The March 26-April 1 poll showed economists now expect the economy to grow a record 27.0% this quarter after expanding only 1.5% in the January-March period compared to 21.1% and 1.0% predicted previously."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"It would then grow 10.0% next quarter and 5.9% and 6.0% in the following two quarters. Those predictions were an uptick from 9.1%, 5.9% and 5.5% respectively."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"But nearly 70% of economists, or 31 of 45, who responded to an additional question said the biggest risk to the economy this fiscal year was a rise in coronavirus cases. Ten picked said inflation."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“It is reasonably clear that the pandemic would worsen before it gets better, as it has been in other countries. The economic damage may be far less given strict lockdowns are unlikely,” said Abhishek Upadhyay, senior economist at ICICI Securities."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“The biggest risk to economic recovery would be in case there is greater evidence of reinfections from the new strains of the virus that also turn out to be less deterred by the existing vaccines.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"With the third highest number of reported COVID-19 cases - over 12 million infections - lagging only the United States and Brazil, India has so far injected 64 million vaccine doses."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Still, the poll of over 45 economists showed Asia’s third largest economy would expand 11.0% in the fiscal year 2021-22 and 6.5% next, from 9.5% and 6.0% predicted in January. It likely contracted 7.5% in 2020-2021 compared to -8.0% predicted previously."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“India’s economy has been (one of) the worst-affected by COVID-19 but has also been (one of) the fastest to recover from the slump,” said Prakash Sakpal, senior Asia economist at ING."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“However, the second wave of the pandemic paves the way for a bumpy ride again this year, while structural bottlenecks will continue to hold back India’s economic potential for years to come.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The risk the pandemic hurts economic growth significantly this year was high, said 29 of 45 economists including one who said it was very high."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“We acknowledge the downside risks to our FY22 GDP growth forecast should movement restrictions be tightened across the country,” noted Anubhuti Sahay, head of South Asia economic research at Standard Chartered."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“However, it is too early to build in the impact. The ‘shock and awe’ of FY21 is unlikely to be repeated this year.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"India on Thursday reversed its decision to lower interest rates by up to 1.1% on its state-backed small savings programme. Small savings are the lifeblood of low- and middle-income groups, and cutting rates would have dealt a severe blow to millions."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The RBI was predicted to hike rates by 25 basis points in the first quarter of next fiscal year to 4.25%, compared to no change until at least 2023 expected previously."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Although we do not expect the imposition of another nationwide lockdown, the RBI may want to keep its powder dry to ward off the potentially debilitating impact of the resurging pandemic,” said Kunal Kundu, India economist at Societe Generale."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Inflation was expected at 4.9% and 4.5% in the current and next fiscal year, within the central bank’s target band of 2-6%, but 39 of 44 economists in response to an additional question said their price forecasts were skewed more to the upside."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"(For other stories from the Reuters global long-term economic outlook polls package:)"}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Indian shares end higher, state-run lenders climb on capital infusion
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Gains in metal and auto stocks helped Indian shares rise more than 1% on Thursday, while capital infusion by the government in some state-run lenders lifted public-sector banks.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"BENGALURU Gains in metal and auto stocks helped Indian shares rise more than 1% on Thursday, while capital infusion by the government in some state-run lenders lifted public-sector banks."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The blue-chip NSE Nifty 50 index closed 1.2% higher at 14,867.35, while the benchmark S\u0026amp;P BSE Sensex gained 1.1% to 50,029.83."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Commodity prices have gone up, so metals are doing well, said Samrat Dasgupta, chief executive of Esquire Capital Investment Advisors in Mumbai."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"He added that the market was also seeing short-covering ahead of the weekly expiry of derivatives contracts and a long weekend."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Indian markets will be closed for a holiday on Friday. They booked a weekly gain of 2%, after declining 1.6% last week."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Leading the charge on Thursday, the Nifty metals index and the Nifty auto index advanced 5.33% and 1.6%, respectively."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Ashok Leyland, Tata Motors and Mahindra and Mahindra gained between 1.5% and 3.8% after posting strong March sales numbers."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Indian government on Wednesday infused a total of 145 billion rupees ($1.98 billion) in state-run lenders Indian Overseas Bank, Bank of India, Central Bank of India and UCO Bank."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Shares of Indian Overseas Bank jumped 6%, Central Bank rose 5%, while Bank of India and UCO Bank gained 3% and 4.1%, respectively."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Meanwhile, India rolled back its decision to lower interest rates on the small savings scheme, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"World stocks also ran higher as U.S. President Joe Biden’s sweeping $2.3 trillion plan to rebuild America’s crumbling infrastructure lifted sentiment."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"($1 = 73.4150 rupees)"}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Future Retail to offer quick online deliveries in bet on e-commerce
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: India's Future Retail will deliver groceries and clothes from its main retail stores within two hours, it said on Thursday, as the company expands in an e-commerce sector dominated by the likes of Amazon.com Inc.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"NEW DELHI India’s Future Retail will deliver groceries and clothes from its main retail stores within two hours, it said on Thursday, as the company expands in an e-commerce sector dominated by the likes of Amazon.com Inc."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Future will allow customers to order goods from its popular hypermarket “Big Bazaar” stores in Mumbai, Bengaluru and New Delhi and later expand the service to 150 cities, the company said in a statement. There are 285 Big Bazaar outlets in India."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Future, the country’s second-largest brick-and-mortar retailer, has only had small e-commerce presence so far, but plans to use faster deliveries to expand in India’s fast-growing e-commerce market, which is seen growing by 30% a year to $200 billion by 2026."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Popular online grocery service BigBasket, in which India’s Tata Group is seeking to acquire a majority stake, and Amazon both offer quick online deliveries in India."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Asked about the competitive landscape, Future Group executive Kamaldeep Singh said during a media briefing the company would have an edge over other players as it aims to deliver a wider array of goods from its stores - including food, fashion and kitchen utilities - within two hours."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Retail companies as well as consumer goods makers in India are focusing on bolstering their e-commerce prowess as shoppers increasingly move online to order everything from clothes to groceries."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Future’s plans come as its businesses struggled in recent months due to the COVID-19 pandemic, forcing it to sell its retail assets to Reliance Industries for $3.4 billion. The transaction is currently being reviewed by India’s Supreme Court after Amazon accused Future of breaching some contracts."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Reliance is also fast expanding into e-commerce operations with its JioMart online platform."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: India's daily new infections highest in more than five months
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: India reported 72,330 new COVID-19 infections overnight, data from the health ministry showed on Thursday, the highest since Oct. 11.

test_endpoint.articlesName: India rolls back decision to cut interest rates on small savings
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: India has reversed its decision to lower interest rates by up to 1.1% on its state-backed small savings programme, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Thursday, adding that orders to cut rates to a near five-decade low were issued because of an oversight.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"CHENNAI India has reversed its decision to lower interest rates by up to 1.1% on its state-backed small savings programme, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Thursday, adding that orders to cut rates to a near five-decade low were issued because of an oversight."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Small savings are the lifeblood of India’s low- and middle-income groups, and cutting interest rates would have dealt a severe blow to hundreds of millions of Indians at a time when many have lost jobs and faced pay cuts amid the pandemic."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“India shall continue to be at the rates which existed in the last quarter of 2020-2021, i.e., rates that prevailed as of March 2021,” Sitharaman said in a tweet on Thursday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Orders issued by oversight shall be withdrawn,” she said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Opposition leaders said the rollback was due to a potential backlash from voters in state assembly elections. Two eastern states have begun voting, and two southern states will vote next week."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“‘Oversight’ in issuing the order to decrease interest rates on Government of India schemes or election driven ‘hindsight’ in withdrawing it?” Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, a member of the opposition Congress party, said in a tweet to Sitharaman."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"A day earlier, on the last day of the 2020/21 financial year, India had cut interest rates on small savings by up to 1.1% for the June quarter. The government reviews interest rates on government-backed schemes every quarter."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s federal government has attempted to link state-backed small savings rates with yields on government bonds every 3 months."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"However, interest rates have largely been kept above market rates, which experts say is due to fear of a backlash from middle class voters."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Dollar, U.S. Treasuries edge higher on strong U.S. labor report
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: The dollar and the yield on the benchmark Treasury note edged higher in light trading on Friday after data showing a surge in the hiring of Americans in March pointed to a U.S. economic recovery that is poised to be the strongest in decades.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"NEW YORK(Reuters) -The dollar and the yield on the benchmark Treasury note edged higher in light trading on Friday after data showing a surge in the hiring of Americans in March pointed to a U.S. economic recovery that is poised to be the strongest in decades."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Equity markets were closed in observance of Good Friday in the Americas, Europe and elsewhere but it is not a U.S. government holiday and the Labor Department released the closely watch non-farm payrolls report."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The U.S. economy added 916,000 jobs in March, more than economists’ forecast of 647,000, and the unemployment rate fell to 6.0% from the previous month’s 6.2%. Jobs numbers for February were revised upwards according to the jobs report."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Futures for the S\u0026amp;P 500 stock index extended gains to 0.43% after the report."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Despite the strong numbers the data will not alter the Federal Reserve’s stance on monetary policy, said Steven Ricchiuto, U.S. chief economist at Mizuho Securities USA in New York."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“The economy’s bouncing back, but it’s not producing the things that are going to change the direction of monetary policy,” Ricchiuto said. “We’re going to test the 1.77% level (in the 10-year Treasury note), but I’m not sure it’s going to break (through) on this number.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The 10-year U.S. Treasury note rose 3.9 basis points to yield 1.7179%, but this was still below a 14-month high of 1.776 hit on Tuesday. [US/]"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Treasury yields have spiked on the economic outlook spurred by U.S. President Joe Biden’s plans for $2.3 trillion in infrastructure spending and the accelerating rollout of COVID-19 vaccines."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The March labor market report is the first of what are likely to be several very strong jobs reports over the next few months, said Russell Price, chief economist at Ameriprise Financial Services Inc in Troy, Michigan."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“The outlook looks very good,” Price said. But “in my mind the biggest constraint could be the ability of the supply side of the economy to fulfill consumer wishes.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Asian markets overnight rose as optimism over a global economic recovery lifted equity markets in Japan, China and South Korea."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Nikkei in Tokyo hit a two-week high, with semiconductor- related shares leading the market as the industry looks to boost manufacturing amid a global shortage of chips."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Biden’s spending plan includes $50 billion for chip manufacturing and other technology research, said Fumio Matsumoto, chief strategist at Okasan Securities."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"China stocks posted a second weekly gain as recent data pointed to a solid recovery in the world’s second-largest economy. Both the CSI300 index and the Shanghai Composite Index closed at an almost four-week highs."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Chinese steel rebar and hot-rolled coil prices closed at record highs after China on Thursday announced a nationwide investigation into steel capacity cuts launched in 2016 as part of efforts to ensure output falls this year."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"South Korean shares closed higher to clock their biggest weekly gain in nearly two months as optimism about a stimulus-fueled economic recovery lifted equities."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Stocks rose on Wall Street on Thursday, with the S\u0026amp;P 500 index hitting a fresh peak as it scaled the 4,000 mark, and the benchmark Deutsche Boerse DAX index in Germany as setting a new high. Equities rose on reports of the strongest manufacturing data in decades around the world."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The dollar index rose 0.127%, with the euro down 0.14% to $1.1759. The Japanese yen weakened 0.07% versus the greenback at 110.67 per dollar."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Spot gold prices fell 0.08% to $1,728.84 an ounce."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Exclusive-Germany to propose Beirut port reconstruction with 'strings attached' - sources
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Germany will next week present a multi-billion-dollar proposal to Lebanese authorities to rebuild the Port of Beirut as part of efforts to entice the country's politicians to form a government capable of warding off financial collapse, two sources said.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"PARIS/BERLIN/BEIRUT Germany will next week present a multi-billion-dollar proposal to Lebanese authorities to rebuild the Port of Beirut as part of efforts to entice the country’s politicians to form a government capable of warding off financial collapse, two sources said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"A chemical explosion at the port last August killed 200 people, injured thousands and destroyed entire neighbourhoods in the Lebanese capital, plunging the country deeper into its worst political and economic crisis since the 1975-1990 civil war."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"According to two diplomatic sources with knowledge of the plans, Germany and France are vying to lead reconstruction efforts. Berlin will on April 7 outline its proposal, which the diplomats said would in principle include support from the European Investment Bank (EIB), to help fund the clearing of the area and reconstruction facilities."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"An EIB spokesman said it was aware of the proposal put forward by the port of Hamburg and its consultancy team for the reconstruction of the port of Beirut and surrounding areas."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“However, there currently is no financing offer by the EIB. Any EIB financing would be subject to due diligence and have to follow the Bank’s usual processes for such operations,” he said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"It would also need to comply with the EIB’s procurement guidelines, environmental and social standards, he said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“The Bank stands ready to support the Lebanese people and reconstruction efforts as part of Team Europe and alongside its partners, the international community and all stakeholders.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"One of the sources estimated EIB funding could be in the range of 2 billion to 3 billion euros."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Germany’s ambassador to Lebanon, Andreas Kindl, confirmed a proposal would be made next week to redevelop Beirut port and nearby areas. The plan had been drawn up by several private companies who would hold talks in Beirut to present it, he said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Consultancy firm Roland Berger, which Kindl and the diplomatic sources said had been involved in putting the plan together, did not respond to requests for comment."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The two diplomatic sources said Lebanon’s political elite first need to agree on the make-up of a new government to fix public finances and root out corruption, a condition which donors, including the International Monetary Fund, are also insisting on before they will unlock billions of dollars in aid."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“This plan is not going to come without strings attached,” said one of the sources. “Germany and France want first to see a government in place committed to implementing reforms. There is no other way around it and this is good for Lebanon.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Germany’s ambassador Kindl said Lebanon could only attract support from investors by enacting meaningful reforms."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Eight months after the port disaster, many Lebanese who lost family, homes and businesses are still waiting for the results of an investigation into the causes of the blast. Lebanon is on the verge of collapse, with shoppers brawling over goods, protesters blocking roads, and businesses shuttered."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Foreign donors have said the new government must have a firm mandate to implement economic reforms, including a central bank audit and an overhaul of the wasteful power sector."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Prime Minister-designate Saad al-Hariri and President Michel Aoun have been unable to agree on a ministerial line-up, however. The outgoing cabinet, which quit after the explosion, has stayed on in a caretaker capacity."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The IMF has said there have been no programme discussions with Lebanese officials, only technical assistance with the Ministry of Finance and some state-owned enterprises."},{"type":"heading","content":"GERMANY’S PROPOSAL"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In addition to the port itself, Germany’s proposal would look to redevelop more than 100 hectares in the surrounding area in a project that the two diplomatic sources said would be along the lines of the post-war reconstruction of central Beirut."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"As in that redevelopment, the plan would involve the creation of a publicly-listed company similar to Solidere, which was set up by former Prime Minister Rafik Hariri in the 1990s and remains on the Lebanon stock exchange."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The sources put the project cost at anywhere between $5 billion to $15 billion, and said it could create as many as 50,000 jobs."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Lebanese official said France and French ports and container shipping group CMA CGM were also interested in the reconstruction project."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"One of the diplomatic sources said that France had sent several missions, including one in March that included CMA CGM, that showed an interest in playing a role in the reconstruction. That mission focused on specific clear-up operations rather than a broader redevelopment, however, the source said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The French foreign ministry and CMA CGM declined to comment."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Lebanese official put the onus for getting the project underway on the Europeans agreeing who would be the lead."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“This is a European decision at the end of the day, because they have to decide on it among themselves. Then when it comes to it, the Lebanese government can go ahead,” the official said."}]
