test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"PARIS/BERLIN/BEIRUT Germany will next week present a multi-billion-dollar proposal to Lebanese authorities to rebuild the Port of Beirut as part of efforts to entice the country’s politicians to form a government capable of warding off financial collapse, two sources said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"A chemical explosion at the port last August killed 200 people, injured thousands and destroyed entire neighbourhoods in the Lebanese capital, plunging the country deeper into its worst political and economic crisis since the 1975-1990 civil war."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"According to two diplomatic sources with knowledge of the plans, Germany and France are vying to lead reconstruction efforts. Berlin will on April 7 outline its proposal, which the diplomats said would in principle include support from the European Investment Bank (EIB), to help fund the clearing of the area and reconstruction facilities."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"An EIB spokesman said it was aware of the proposal put forward by the port of Hamburg and its consultancy team for the reconstruction of the port of Beirut and surrounding areas."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“However, there currently is no financing offer by the EIB. Any EIB financing would be subject to due diligence and have to follow the Bank’s usual processes for such operations,” he said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"It would also need to comply with the EIB’s procurement guidelines, environmental and social standards, he said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“The Bank stands ready to support the Lebanese people and reconstruction efforts as part of Team Europe and alongside its partners, the international community and all stakeholders.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"One of the sources estimated EIB funding could be in the range of 2 billion to 3 billion euros."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Germany’s ambassador to Lebanon, Andreas Kindl, confirmed a proposal would be made next week to redevelop Beirut port and nearby areas. The plan had been drawn up by several private companies who would hold talks in Beirut to present it, he said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Consultancy firm Roland Berger, which Kindl and the diplomatic sources said had been involved in putting the plan together, did not respond to requests for comment."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The two diplomatic sources said Lebanon’s political elite first need to agree on the make-up of a new government to fix public finances and root out corruption, a condition which donors, including the International Monetary Fund, are also insisting on before they will unlock billions of dollars in aid."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“This plan is not going to come without strings attached,” said one of the sources. “Germany and France want first to see a government in place committed to implementing reforms. There is no other way around it and this is good for Lebanon.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Germany’s ambassador Kindl said Lebanon could only attract support from investors by enacting meaningful reforms."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Eight months after the port disaster, many Lebanese who lost family, homes and businesses are still waiting for the results of an investigation into the causes of the blast. Lebanon is on the verge of collapse, with shoppers brawling over goods, protesters blocking roads, and businesses shuttered."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Foreign donors have said the new government must have a firm mandate to implement economic reforms, including a central bank audit and an overhaul of the wasteful power sector."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Prime Minister-designate Saad al-Hariri and President Michel Aoun have been unable to agree on a ministerial line-up, however. The outgoing cabinet, which quit after the explosion, has stayed on in a caretaker capacity."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The IMF has said there have been no programme discussions with Lebanese officials, only technical assistance with the Ministry of Finance and some state-owned enterprises."},{"type":"heading","content":"GERMANY’S PROPOSAL"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In addition to the port itself, Germany’s proposal would look to redevelop more than 100 hectares in the surrounding area in a project that the two diplomatic sources said would be along the lines of the post-war reconstruction of central Beirut."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"As in that redevelopment, the plan would involve the creation of a publicly-listed company similar to Solidere, which was set up by former Prime Minister Rafik Hariri in the 1990s and remains on the Lebanon stock exchange."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The sources put the project cost at anywhere between $5 billion to $15 billion, and said it could create as many as 50,000 jobs."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Lebanese official said France and French ports and container shipping group CMA CGM were also interested in the reconstruction project."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"One of the diplomatic sources said that France had sent several missions, including one in March that included CMA CGM, that showed an interest in playing a role in the reconstruction. That mission focused on specific clear-up operations rather than a broader redevelopment, however, the source said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The French foreign ministry and CMA CGM declined to comment."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Lebanese official put the onus for getting the project underway on the Europeans agreeing who would be the lead."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“This is a European decision at the end of the day, because they have to decide on it among themselves. Then when it comes to it, the Lebanese government can go ahead,” the official said."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Boat carries 1,200 survivors from Mozambique militant attack to safety
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: A boat carrying 1,200 survivors of a deadly attack by Islamic State-linked insurgents in northern Mozambique reached safety in the port of Pemba on Thursday, some of them crying on arrival after spending days hiding in the bush.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"PEMBA, Mozambique A boat carrying 1,200 survivors of a deadly attack by Islamic State-linked insurgents in northern Mozambique reached safety in the port of Pemba on Thursday, some of them crying on arrival after spending days hiding in the bush."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Aid workers were at the crowded port to give food to those disembarking from the green and white ferry, while police and soldiers kept control of crowds of people excited to see relatives rescued during the attack that began last week in Palma, a Reuters reporter at the port said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Many people were believed to have scattered into dense forest or to have attempted to escape by boat, aid workers said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"An emotional Mariamo Tagir, who arrived on the ferry, told Reuters TV that she had spent seven days in the bush, crying every day."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“I don’t know where my son is. It’s very painful,” said Tagir. “The situation is really bad, many dead.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Islamist insurgents have been increasingly active in the surrounding province of Cabo Delgado since 2017, although it is unclear whether they have a unified aim or what specifically they are fighting for."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The district where Palma is located is adjacent to natural gas projects worth $60 billion. It is home to around 110,000 people according to United Nations estimates, of whom more than 40,000 sought shelter there after fleeing attacks elsewhere."},{"type":"heading","content":"THOUSANDS DISPLACED"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Mozambique’s government has confirmed dozens of deaths in Palma, including at least seven killed when militants ambushed vehicles trying to escape the Amarula Hotel. One South African is confirmed to have died as a result."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"British national Philip Mawer, who has been missing since the attack, was likely also killed in the incident, his employer RA International said in a statement on behalf of his family, adding a body matching his description had been recovered but not formally identified."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“The family is devastated by the loss,” the statement said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Military operations were ongoing on Wednesday, according to footage shot by local news station TVM, which showed soldiers carrying rocket-propelled grenades and guns in the area, as well as reinforcements arriving by helicopter."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“I can’t right now say we have the whole village under control,” army spokesman Chongo Vidigal said in the footage, adding however security forces did have a presence in the port area."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Portugal, meanwhile, was reportedly ready to send 60 soldiers to help train armed forces in Cabo Delgado."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Reuters has not been able to independently verify the accounts from the town. Most means of communication were cut off after the attack began on March 24. Phone calls to Mozambique’s government and security officials went unanswered on Thursday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Aid groups believe the attack has displaced tens of thousands of people. Hundreds, including many foreign workers, have been evacuated by air."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"As of Wednesday afternoon, a U.N. migration agency tracker showed more than 8,100 people had been displaced, almost half of them children. Roughly 20% had arrived in Pemba, with others turning up in the districts of Mueda, Montepuez and Nangade in Cabo Delgado."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"However, the full scale of the casualties and displacement remains unclear."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The ferry - organised by French energy major Total in coordination with the Mozambican government and the United Nations - docked at around 8 a.m. local time (0600 GMT) in Pemba, the provincial capital of Cabo Delgado."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Total, which has a gas project on the Afungi Peninsula near Palma, said in a statement that there were almost 1,200 passengers on board, mainly women and children."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"A humanitarian official said the government was screening those arriving at Pemba to prevent infiltration by armed groups."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Saudi-led coalition thwarted two explosives-laden drones fired at Saudi city - state TV
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: The Saudi-led coalition said on Thursday it intercepted and destroyed two explosives-laden drones launched by Yemen's Houthis towards the southern Saudi city of Khamis Mushait, state TV reported.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"CAIRO The Saudi-led coalition said on Thursday it intercepted and destroyed two explosives-laden drones launched by Yemen’s Houthis towards the southern Saudi city of Khamis Mushait, state TV reported."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Houthi military spokesman Yahya Sarea acknowledged the attack, saying in a Twitter post that the group had fired two drones at the King Khalid air base in Khamis Mushait."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The coalition, which intervened in Yemen in March 2015, has often retaliated to cross-border attacks on Saudi Arabia with air strikes in Yemen."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Houthis ousted the internationally recognised government from power in Sanaa in late 2014 and now control most of northern Yemen."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: OPEC+ to ease oil curbs from May after U.S. calls Saudi
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: OPEC+ agreed on Thursday to gradually ease its oil output cuts from May, after the new U.S. administration called on Saudi Arabia to keep energy affordable, mirroring Donald Trump's practice of calling OPEC's leader over oil policy.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"LONDON/DUBAI/MOSCOW OPEC+ agreed on Thursday to gradually ease its oil output cuts from May, after the new U.S. administration called on Saudi Arabia to keep energy affordable, mirroring Donald Trump’s practice of calling OPEC’s leader over oil policy."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The group, which has implemented deep cuts since a pandemic-induced oil price collapse in 2020, agreed to ease production curbs by 350,000 barrels per day (bpd) in May, another 350,000 bpd in June and further 400,000 bpd or so in July."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Iran’s oil minister, Bijan Zanganeh, confirmed the group would have boosted output by a total of 1.1 million bpd by July."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Under Thursday’s deal, cuts implemented by the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries, Russia and their allies, a group known as OPEC+, would be just above 6.5 million bpd from May, compared with slightly below 7 million bpd in April."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“What we did today is, I think, a very conservative measure,” Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz Bin Salman told a news conference after the OPEC+ meeting, adding that output levels could still be adjusted at the next meeting on April 28."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"He said Thursday’s decision had not been influenced by any talks with U.S. officials or any other consuming nations."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Saudi minister also said the kingdom would gradually phase out its additional voluntary cut that have been running at 1 million bpd, by adding 250,000 bpd to production in May, another 350,000 bpd in June and then 400,000 bpd in July."},{"type":"heading","content":"CHANGING MOOD"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Brent crude was trading around $64 a barrel, more than 20% up on the start of the year and not far from this year’s high of around $71."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“We reaffirmed the importance of international cooperation to ensure affordable and reliable sources of energy for consumers,” Jennifer Granholm, the new energy secretary appointed by U.S. President Joe Biden, said on Twitter after her call with the Saudi energy minister."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"News of the call coincided with signs of a changing mood in informal discussions between OPEC+ members. A few days before Thursday’s talks, delegates had said the group would likely keep most existing cuts in place, given uncertainty about the demand outlook amid a new wave of coronavirus lockdowns."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"But in the 24 hours before the meeting started, sources said discussions had shifted to the possibility of output increases."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In the past, Trump had used his influence to force Saudi Arabia to adjust policy. When prices spiked, he insisted OPEC raise production. When oil prices collapsed last year, hurting U.S. shale producers, he called on the group to cut output."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Until this week, Biden’s administration had refrained from such an approach, keep a distance from Riyadh and imposing sanctions on some Saudi citizens over the 2018 murder of Jamal Khashoggi."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Even when OPEC+ decided on March 4 to keep steady output, triggering a price rise, the White House had made no direct comment."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Turkey fines firms over short selling irregularities - regulator
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Turkey fined 10 securities firms for up to 7.8 million lira ($1 million) in relation to irregularities in short-selling transactions, the country's Capital Markets Board said in its weekly bulletin on Thursday.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"ISTANBUL Turkey fined 10 securities firms for up to 7.8 million lira ($1 million) in relation to irregularities in short-selling transactions, the country’s Capital Markets Board said in its weekly bulletin on Thursday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Fines of various amounts were imposed on firms including Merrill Lynch International, JP Morgan Securities, Goldman Sachs International, Credit Suisse Securities Europe and Barclays Capital Securities, the statement said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Last July, Turkey’s Borsa Istanbul applied a temporary short selling ban on various foreign institutions because they failed to notify authorities about short-selling transactions."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Islamist turned Israeli kingmaker offers olive branch to rightist Jews
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: A key Israeli Arab politician offered the country's majority Jews an olive branch on Thursday, in what appeared to be a bid to offset ultranationalist misgivings at accommodating him as part of a new coalition under Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"NAZARETH, Israel A key Israeli Arab politician offered the country’s majority Jews an olive branch on Thursday, in what appeared to be a bid to offset ultranationalist misgivings at accommodating him as part of a new coalition under Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Mansour Abbas’ United Arab List (UAL) took four of parliament’s 120 seats in last week’s inconclusive Israeli election, making its support potentially crucial for the conservative Netanyahu to secure a stable governing majority."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Jewish right-wing and religious parties with allegiance to Netanyahu have given the prime minister 52 seats, while a kindred six-seat party opposed to his leadership has spurned him and another, with seven seats, so far has been non-comittal."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"There has been recoil across the rightist spectrum at the idea of working with the UAL, an Islamist party with pro-Palestinian leanings - even if it were to remain outside government but abstain from opposition no-confidence motions."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“I extend a hand to create an opportunity for life together in this land that is holy and blessed for the children of the three faiths and two peoples,” Mansour said in speech delivered mostly in Hebrew and aired live on Israel’s prime-time TV news."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“I have not ruled anything out,” Abbas said, signalling openness to recommending either Netanyahu or the premier’s centrist rival, Yair Lapid, for top office when coalition consultations begin next week. Lapid could now wield as many as 57 seats."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Reiterating UAL demands to improve conditions for Israel’s 21% Arab minority, Abbas said: “We do not have to agree on everything, and of course we will disagree on quite a few issues ... My approach is what merits ‘yes’ and less what ‘no’.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Netanyahu has not commented publicly on any prospective outreach to the UAL. On Wednesday, he called on his two rival rightist parties to “come back home” and join him."}]

test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"NAZARETH, Israel A key Israeli Arab politician offered the country’s majority Jews an olive branch on Thursday, in what appeared to be a bid to offset ultranationalist misgivings at accommodating him as part of a new coalition under Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Mansour Abbas’ United Arab List (UAL) took four of parliament’s 120 seats in last week’s inconclusive Israeli election, making its support potentially crucial for the conservative Netanyahu to secure a stable governing majority."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Jewish right-wing and religious parties with allegiance to Netanyahu have given the prime minister 52 seats, while a kindred six-seat party opposed to his leadership has spurned him and another, with seven seats, so far has been non-comittal."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"There has been recoil across the rightist spectrum at the idea of working with the UAL, an Islamist party with pro-Palestinian leanings - even if it were to remain outside government but abstain from opposition no-confidence motions."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“I extend a hand to create an opportunity for life together in this land that is holy and blessed for the children of the three faiths and two peoples,” Mansour said in speech delivered mostly in Hebrew and aired live on Israel’s prime-time TV news."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“I have not ruled anything out,” Abbas said, signalling openness to recommending either Netanyahu or the premier’s centrist rival, Yair Lapid, for top office when coalition consultations begin next week. Lapid could now wield as many as 57 seats."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Reiterating UAL demands to improve conditions for Israel’s 21% Arab minority, Abbas said: “We do not have to agree on everything, and of course we will disagree on quite a few issues ... My approach is what merits ‘yes’ and less what ‘no’.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Netanyahu has not commented publicly on any prospective outreach to the UAL. On Wednesday, he called on his two rival rightist parties to “come back home” and join him."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Motorcycling: Some riders don't care about rivals, says Rossi
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Seven-times MotoGP world champion Valentino Rossi believes there are riders on the grid who do not care enough about their rivals.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"Seven-times MotoGP world champion Valentino Rossi believes there are riders on the grid who do not care enough about their rivals."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Italian Rossi was involved in a clash with Brad Binder in the season-opening Qatar Grand Prix on Sunday before finishing 12th in his debut race for Petronas Yamaha."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Binder maintained there was no contact with Rossi and no sanctions were handed out by the race stewards."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Ahead of this weekend’s second race in Doha, Rossi was asked whether there is a difference in intensity when fighting for positions in the mid-pack."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“It doesn’t depend very much on the position but it depends very much on the different riders,” Rossi, 42, was quoted as saying by Autosport."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“You have a lot of riders who are more clean and ride with a lot of respect for the opponents."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“You have some other riders like Binder, who ride a lot harder and don’t care about the rival."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“So, if you try to close the line he releases the brake, and if you don’t move he hits you out of the track. But it’s like this, now it’s like this.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"After struggling for grip on his rear tyre, Rossi finished 10.7 seconds behind former factory Yamaha team mate and race winner Maverick Vinales last weekend."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Looks like Maverick has something different in the setting of the bike and in the electronic system,” Rossi said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“It’s very difficult to put exactly the same settings because every rider has some small differences, but during this weekend we can try to follow another way.”"}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Saudi man arrested as juvenile could face execution despite reforms: Human Rights Watch
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Human Rights Watch says a Saudi man who was convicted following a "grossly unfair trial" for crimes committed when he was a minor risks being executed although the Saudi authorities have said they have scrapped the death penalty for juveniles.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"DUBAI Human Rights Watch says a Saudi man who was convicted following a “grossly unfair trial” for crimes committed when he was a minor risks being executed although the Saudi authorities have said they have scrapped the death penalty for juveniles."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Abdullah al-Huwaiti was convicted by a criminal court in October 2019 when he was 17, on murder and armed robbery charges along with five other defendants, HRW said in a statement on Wednesday. He was arrested when he was 14, the rights group said, for crimes allegedly committed in 2017."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Saudi government media office did not respond to a request for comment on the case."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"HRW said Huwaiti was sentenced to death and ordered to pay 1,315,000 SAR($350,000) in restitution to the victims. His case is due to be transferred to Riyadh’s Supreme Court for a final ruling."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"HRW said all six defendants told the court at trial that the interrogators coerced their confessions through torture or the threat of it."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Al-Huwaiti’s court proceedings flouted almost every internationally recognizable fair trial guarantee,” said Michael Page, deputy Middle East director at Human Rights Watch."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Saudi authorities said last year that they would stop sentencing to death people who committed crimes while minors and would apply this retroactively."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"However, the March 2020 royal decree announcing this was not reported by state media or published in the official gazette as would be normal practice. Human rights groups and western lawmakers had raised concerns about its implementation."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Asked whether the decree applied to all types of crimes, the state-backed Human Rights Commission told Reuters in February that the ban only applied to a lesser category of offense under Islamic law known as “ta’zeer.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"This would mean judges can therefore still sentence child offenders to death under the other two categories, according to Saudi Arabia’s interpretation of sharia: “houdoud”, or serious crimes that carry a prescribed punishment, including terrorism, and “qisas”, or retribution, usually for murder."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Huwaiti was convicted on a “houdoud” charge."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"($1 = 3.7501 riyals)"}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Kuwait extends curfew, Qatar suspends in-person learning
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Kuwait said on Thursday it would extend a month-long partial curfew that had been due to end next week until April 22 as part of efforts to curb the spread of COVID-19.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"DUBAI Kuwait said on Thursday it would extend a month-long partial curfew that had been due to end next week until April 22 as part of efforts to curb the spread of COVID-19."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The cabinet said in a statement on Twitter that the curfew would be from 7 p.m. to 5 a.m. as of April 8."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Gulf Arab state recorded 1,282 new infections on Thursday. It had seen daily cases fall below 300 in December from close to 1,100 last May."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The cabinet said deliveries from restaurants, cafes and food stores would be permitted during the fasting month of Ramadan, which begins in mid-April this year, between 7 p.m. and 3 a.m."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Ramadan fast is a time when Muslims are required to abstain from food and drink during daylight hours."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Other Gulf Arab states have also seen a rise in coronavirus cases. test_endpoint.articlesName: South Africa's rand firms after positive data, stocks end higher
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: South Africa's rand extended gains against the U.S. dollar on Thursday, as positive manufacturing activity and new vehicle sales data pointed to a recovery in the economy.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"JOHANNESBURG South Africa’s rand extended gains against the U.S. dollar on Thursday, as positive manufacturing activity and new vehicle sales data pointed to a recovery in the economy."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"At 1515 GMT the rand was 0.76% firmer at 14.6525 per dollar, making advances from the previous session that were spurred by a bigger-than-expected trade surplus."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"On Thursday, a survey showed manufacturing activity expanded for a third month in a row in March. Separately, data showed new vehicles sales were up by nearly 32% in March."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Previous data releases of private sector credit extension as well as vehicle and retail sales pointed towards sluggish consumer demand over the past few months,” Pieter du Preez at NKC African Economics said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Yet, the latest vehicle sales data is the first release suggesting that consumers are willing to start spending again.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"South Africa’s economy contracted by 7% in 2020, its worst annual decline in a century, after the COVID-19 pandemic disrupted economic activity."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Shares on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) rallied on Thursday, ending the week on a higher note as financial markets in South Africa closed for a four-day long weekend."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The markets were buoyed on the back of stabilising U.S. treasury yields and a massive multi-trillion-dollar infrastructure package by President Joe Biden to boost local growth."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The benchmark all-share index went up 1.13% to end the day at 67,236 points while the bluechip top 40 companies index closed up 1.16% to 61,590 points."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Everything in the last month or so has been driven by fears of what the U.S. long bond interest rate is doing..., because ultimately the share market is supported by low interest rates,” said Wayne McCurrie, portfolio manager at local bank FNB."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"He said that whenever the markets turn sanguine about rates being stable, there is a bounce in share prices globally."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Bonds weakened, with the yield on the benchmark 2020 paper up 8 basis to 9.565%."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Turkey's new central bank head promises tight policy, sources say
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Turkey's new central bank governor, Sahap Kavcioglu, said on Thursday in his first calls with investors that tight monetary policy would remain in place because of high inflation, according to several people, helping boost the lira.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"ISTANBUL Turkey’s new central bank governor, Sahap Kavcioglu, said on Thursday in his first calls with investors that tight monetary policy would remain in place because of high inflation, according to several people, helping boost the lira."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"President Tayyip Erdogan installed Kavcioglu on March 20 in a move that sent the lira down 13% as investors predicted a quick pivot to loose policy, given Kavcioglu’s past criticism of the bank’s tight stance."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Asked in a call with local investors about a February newspaper column in which he said high rates boosted inflation, Kavcioglu downplayed his previous views and said as governor he would act in line with his “institutional task”."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"A similar question put to the new governor in a separate call with international investors, was the only one the governor answered directly, sources attending the call said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“He said basically judge me after the April MPC which I would take as a very strong signal that we will certainly not see more rate cuts in April,” said one asset manager."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Two sources told Reuters that a senior bank official said on the first call there would be no premature interest rate cuts, and that inflation - at 15.6% in February - was now close to the upper bound of its forecasts."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The official added that the recent lira sell-off would push inflation higher in the short term, the sources said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“They are saying all the right things” and will probably “hold tight” for now, one investor said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The lira was some 1.57% stronger at 8.1350 against the dollar at 1304 GMT."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The former central bank governor, Naci Agbal, had raised the policy rate to 19% from 10.25% in four months on the job, to address inflation that has remained in double digits for most of the past four years."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The bank expected a maximum of 17% inflation in March and a bit more in April, according to its February forecast. Analysts predict it will rise through April, when Goldman Sachs expects it to peak at 18%."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Omer Emec, chief economist at Albaraka Turk, who attended the first meeting, said the messages on the call helped reassure markets, but investors would want to see action."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"One of the people who spoke to Reuters said that while investors were convinced there would be no rate cut this month, the bank would struggle to shed the market perception that policy would be eased soon."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Asked on the domestic investor call whether rates would be raised further if needed, Kavcioglu did not clearly answer “yes”. He said the bank will monitor data before the next policy meeting and do what needs to be done, said two of the sources."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“It was played with a straight bat - if you are going to follow the policy of your predecessor why change the governor?” said another international fund manager attending the second call."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Data released on Thursday showing hard-currency holdings among Turks fell sharply after Agbal’s ouster, to $223.67 billion as of March 26, from $232.50 billion a week earlier."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"March inflation data will be released on April 5."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Lebanon's top Christian cleric criticizes Hezbollah in leaked video
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Lebanon's top Christian cleric has made unusually direct comments criticizing the Shi'ite Hezbollah movement, accusing it of harming the country by dragging it into regional conflicts.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"BEIRUT (Reuters) -Lebanon’s top Christian cleric has made unusually direct comments criticizing the Shi’ite Hezbollah movement, accusing it of harming the country by dragging it into regional conflicts."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“I want to tell them...You want us to stay in a state of war that you decide? Are you asking us before you go to war?” Maronite Patriarch Bechara Boutros Al-Rai said in a leaked video circulated by local media on Thursday, in which he mentioned the conflicts in Syria, Iraq and Yemen."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“You’re not looking out for (our) interests, nor the interests of your people,” he said, apparently addressing Hezbollah, a heavily-armed movement allied to its backer Tehran in regional wars."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Rai said he had received visits from Hezbollah supporters who were privately critical of the group as they felt the force of Lebanon’s financial collapse."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“We get people from Hezbollah. They come to us to tell us: ‘this arsenal is against us, we can no longer endure’. Because they are also hungry like us,” he said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The video marked his strongest criticism yet of Hezbollah, which along with its political allies holds sway in Lebanon’s parliament."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The patriarch wields influence in Lebanon as head of the Maronite church, from which the president must be drawn under a sectarian power-sharing system."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Rai has called for Lebanon to remain neutral in regional conflicts, referring to Hezbollah’s deployment of fighters to neighbouring Syria to support President Bashar al-Assad alongside Shi’ite militias, as well as its alliance with Iran in a power struggle with Saudi Arabia."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Hezbollah’s opponents say its relationship with Tehran has kept away Gulf Arab states that once funnelled money into Lebanon, closing off an important source of aid."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Lebanon’s financial meltdown has crashed the currency, fueling poverty and hunger, its worst crisis since the 1975-1990 civil war that fractured the country along sectarian lines."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Citi forecasts Turkey inflation peaking at 17% in April
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Turkey's consumer price inflation for March is likely to rise to 16.2% year-on-year, up from 15.6% in February, Citi said on Thursday.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"LONDON Turkey’s consumer price inflation for March is likely to rise to 16.2% year-on-year, up from 15.6% in February, Citi said on Thursday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The rise would be due to a relatively broad-based increase, led by transportation, the bank said, adding that the core inflation measure for the month would likely rise to about 17%."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Inflation would probably peak in April at around 17% year-on-year, before falling back to about 12% by the end of the year, with risks tilted to the upside, Citi said."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: South Sudan's central bank orders banks to use one foreign exchange rate
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: South Sudan's central bank ordered banks on Thursday to start using one foreign exchange rate in order to reduce market distortions, seeking to stabilise an economy reeling from years of war and the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"JUBA South Sudan’s central bank ordered banks on Thursday to start using one foreign exchange rate in order to reduce market distortions, seeking to stabilise an economy reeling from years of war and the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"While the central bank’s indicative exchange rate stands at 186 South Sudanese pounds per dollar, importers have been paying 610 pounds per dollar in the parallel market, officials and currency traders said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The central bank said lenders must in future use a daily market rate that it will publish based on daily foreign exchange returns from the institutions."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Banks and exchange bureaus will be expected to trade at the market exchange rate in all of their FX transactions,” the bank said in a statement."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The central bank also said commercial banks will be allowed to participate in its weekly foreign exchange auctions where they will be apportioned $3 million, adding that it also plans to introduce reserve money targeting."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The auctions have been running with the participation of just exchange bureaus so far, who have been bidding for a pot of $2 million every week, the central bank said."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: France faces rising calls to investigate Mali air strike
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: France faced mounting calls from rights groups on Thursday to open an investigation into an air strike by its forces in Mali that a United Nations probe said killed 19 civilians at a wedding party.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"BAMAKO France faced mounting calls from rights groups on Thursday to open an investigation into an air strike by its forces in Mali that a United Nations probe said killed 19 civilians at a wedding party."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"U.N. investigators published a report on Tuesday about the Jan. 3 strike, concluding that it killed 19 civilians and three armed men near the central Mali village of Bounti."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"France, which has more than 5,000 troops in Mali and neighbouring West African countries to battle militants linked to al Qaeda and Islamic State, rejected the conclusions, saying it hit Islamist militants only."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Domestic and international advocacy groups, including the Malian Association for Human Rights (AMDH), Amnesty International and Oxfam France, demanded that France and Mali conduct their own independent investigations."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“We ask the Malian and French authorities to place the quest for justice at the centre of their action, notably through an independent and in-depth investigation,” AMDH president Moctar Mariko said in a statement."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"French Defence Minister Florence Parly, who arrived in Mali late on Wednesday to visit French and other European troops, did not commit to an investigation when asked by reporters."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“What we want is for this (U.N.) investigation, which was conducted in a unilateral manner, to take into account the arguments that we already wanted to emphasise the first time,” she said on Thursday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The French government has criticised the report’s heavy use of witness accounts, which it said could be false testimonies by the militants’ sympathisers or people under their influence. It has said its aerial surveillance allowed it to identify the targets as militants. It did not share that surveillance with U.N. investigators."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Parly said France would not be willing to publish those surveillance images, as it did after killing a senior al Qaeda leader last year."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“No army in the world has the habit of providing to its enemy the elements that would allow it to understand what we know about it,” she said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Mali’s government, which in January backed the French account of the strike, has not yet commented on the U.N. report."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Namibia gets first-ever funds from IMF to help fight COVID-19
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Namibia will for the first time receive $271 million from the International Monetary Fund to address the country’s deteriorating fiscal position which has been worsened by the COVID-19 pandemic, its finance ministry said on Thursday.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"WINDHOEK Namibia will for the first time receive $271 million from the International Monetary Fund to address the country’s deteriorating fiscal position which has been worsened by the COVID-19 pandemic, its finance ministry said on Thursday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Namibia had previously avoided loans from the IMF since becoming a member in 1990, but the pandemic has hurt the country’s economy. Eighty-five nations have sought assistance from the lender under its Rapid Financing Instrument in the last 12 months."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The finance ministry said the funds will assist in the response to the COVID-19 health emergency, including the purchase and deployment of vaccines."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“The COVID-19 pandemic and its fallout have created a situation where Namibia’s fiscal deficit is widening substantially,” the finance ministry said in a statement."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Although Namibia has had just over 44,000 confirmed cases and 528 deaths compared to neighbouring South Africa which has had over 1.5 million infections, its economy has been severely battered."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The southwest African country’s debt is set to rise to 76.2% of GDP with a budget deficit of 8.6% of GDP in 2021/22."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Namibia’s statistics office said GDP had contracted by a record 8% in 2020, worse than the 7.3% estimate by the Bank of Namibia."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Only around 1,500 people have been vaccinated in Namibia so far, despite the country receiving 100,000 doses of the Chinese-donated Sinopharm vaccine and 30,000 doses of the Covishield vaccine donated by India."}]

Eighty-five nations have sought assistance from the lender under its Rapid Financing Instrument in the last 12 months."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The finance ministry said the funds will assist in the response to the COVID-19 health emergency, including the purchase and deployment of vaccines."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“The COVID-19 pandemic and its fallout have created a situation where Namibia’s fiscal deficit is widening substantially,” the finance ministry said in a statement."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Although Namibia has had just over 44,000 confirmed cases and 528 deaths compared to neighbouring South Africa which has had over 1.5 million infections, its economy has been severely battered."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The southwest African country’s debt is set to rise to 76.2% of GDP with a budget deficit of 8.6% of GDP in 2021/22."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Namibia’s statistics office said GDP had contracted by a record 8% in 2020, worse than the 7.3% estimate by the Bank of Namibia."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Only around 1,500 people have been vaccinated in Namibia so far, despite the country receiving 100,000 doses of the Chinese-donated Sinopharm vaccine and 30,000 doses of the Covishield vaccine donated by India."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: ABinBEV opens $180 million brewery plant in Mozambique
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Anheuser-Busch InBev (ABinBEV), the world’s largest beer producer, has opened a new $180 million brewery in Mozambique, the firm said on Thursday.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"MAPUTO Anheuser-Busch InBev (ABinBEV), the world’s largest beer producer, has opened a new $180 million brewery in Mozambique, the firm said on Thursday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The new site has a capacity of 2.4 million hectolitres per year, with potential to expand that to 6.7 million."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Located in Marracuene, 30 km north of the capital Maputo, it represents the biggest investment in the sector in Mozambique."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Heineken group began producing beer in Mozambique in 2019 at a $100 million factory, also in Marracuene, with a production capacity of 800,000 hectolitres per year."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The new ABinBev facility was built from scratch. It employed more than two thousand Mozambicans during the construction phase, and currently employs over 200 people on a permanent basis."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"It will be operated by its subsidiary, the Mozambican brewery Cervejas de Mocambique (CDM)."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Tomaz Salomao, President of CDM, called it “the biggest and (most) modern factory in the country and in Africa”, adding that it aimed to supply markets throughout the region."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The new facility will produce 80,000 bottles per hour, Salomao said. He also announced that the ABinBEV subsidiary would donate $1 million for the country to buy COVID-19 vaccines."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"ABinBev paid around $100 billion in 2016 to acquire rival group SABMiller. It now produces two of the most popular beer brands in Mozambique – 2M and Laurentina."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: South Africa collects $85 billion in taxes in 2020/21  - revenue service
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: South Africa collected 1.25 trillion rand ($85 billion) in tax revenue in the financial year ended March 2021, around 12% less than the government's original target of 1.425 trillion rand, the revenue service said on Thursday.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"JOHANNESBURG South Africa collected 1.25 trillion rand ($85 billion) in tax revenue in the financial year ended March 2021, around 12% less than the government’s original target of 1.425 trillion rand, the revenue service said on Thursday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The economy, in recession even before the coronavirus struck, shrank by 7% in 2020, while unemployment also soared, leading to a record budget deficit as the government was starved of revenue while forced to spend more to fight the virus."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The initial 2020/21 target of 1.425 trillion rand was set by the National Treasury before the coronavirus pandemic struck in March last year."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Treasury revised the estimate down to 1.112 trillion rand in October, but then upped it to 1.212 trillion in the February 2021 budget."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The South African Revenue Service (Sars) said improved economic activity, higher collections company tax, especially mining firms, and greater tax compliance, had led to better collection than the February target."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Sars Commissioner Edward Kieswatter said the agency would focus on stricter compliance, especially by high net-worth individuals, to close the gap."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Sars is aware of increasing number of south Africans who have financial assets offshore ... they have more than 400 billion rand in offshore accounts. We’ve identified around 10% of that, but we believe there’s still a lot to be explained,” Kieswatter told a news conference."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Kieswatter said the bans on the sale of alcohol and tobacco during the strictest period of the coronavirus lockdown cost the country around 14 billion rand in lost excise taxes."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"($1 = 14.6551 rand)"}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Pfizer COVID-19 shot 91% effective in updated data, protective against South African variant
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Pfizer Inc and BioNTech said on Thursday their COVID-19 vaccine is around 91% effective at preventing the disease, citing updated trial data that included participants inoculated for up to six months.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"Pfizer Inc and BioNTech said on Thursday their COVID-19 vaccine is around 91% effective at preventing the disease, citing updated trial data that included participants inoculated for up to six months."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The shot was also 100% effective in preventing illness among trial participants in South Africa, where a new variant called B1351 is dominant, although that rate was derived from a relatively small number of nine infections observed there, which were all in the placebo group, Pfizer said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"While the new overall efficacy rate of 91.3% is lower than the 95% originally reported in November for its 44,000-person trial, a number of variants have become more prevalent around the world since then."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Pfizer’s Chief Executive Officer Albert Bourla said the updated result, which includes data on more than 12,000 people fully inoculated for at least six months, positions the drugmakers to submit for full U.S. regulatory approval."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The vaccine is currently authorized on an emergency basis by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The trial data “provide the first clinical results that a vaccine can effectively protect against currently circulating variants, a critical factor to reach herd immunity and end this pandemic for the global population,” Ugur Sahin, chief executive officer at BioNTech, said in a statement."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Experts fear new variants of COVID-19 from South Africa and Brazil may be resistant to existing vaccines and treatment. More than 300 cases of the South African variant have been detected in more than 25 U.S. states and jurisdictions, according to federal data."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Lab tests have previously indicated that BioNTech’s vaccine was less potent but still offered a robust defense against the B1351 variant that first emerged in South Africa."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Still, BioNTech reiterated this week there would likely be a future need for booster shots that specifically address new variants and that the group was preparing to upgrade its vaccine when needed."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"BioNTech has said that it started testing a modified vaccine version against the South African mutant in March for early indications on safety and efficacy but a product for later market launch would require yet another redesign and more tests."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The updated trial data would not prompt the company to change that development strategy, a BioNTech spokeswoman said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The vaccine was 100% effective in preventing severe disease as defined by the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and 95.3% effective in preventing severe disease as defined by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"There were also no serious safety concerns observed in trial participants up to six months after the second dose, the companies said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"They added that it was generally equally effective irrespective of age, race, gender or ethnicity, and among participants with a variety of existing medical conditions."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The trial reviewed more than 900 confirmed cases of COVID-19, most of which were among participants who received a placebo."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The release of updated results comes on the heels of separate data that showed the vaccine is safe and effective in 12- to 15-year olds, paving the way for the drugmakers to seek U.S. and European approval to use the shot in this age group within weeks."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Iran adds advanced machines enriching underground at Natanz -IAEA report
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Iran has started enriching uranium with a fourth cascade, or cluster, of advanced IR-2m machines at its underground Natanz plant, a report by the U.N. atomic watchdog obtained by Reuters on Thursday showed, in a further breach of Iran's nuclear deal.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"VIENNA Iran has started enriching uranium with a fourth cascade, or cluster, of advanced IR-2m machines at its underground Natanz plant, a report by the U.N. atomic watchdog obtained by Reuters on Thursday showed, in a further breach of Iran’s nuclear deal."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“On 31 March 2021, the Agency verified at FEP that: Iran had begun feeding natural UF6 into a fourth cascade of 174 IR-2m centrifuges,” the International Atomic Energy Agency said in the report dated Wednesday, referring to the underground Fuel Enrichment Plant and to uranium hexafluoride, the form in which uranium is fed into centrifuges for enrichment."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Turkish exporters re-route goods to dodge unofficial Saudi trade blockade, traders say
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Some Turkish exporters are re-routing food, clothing and other goods to circumvent a months-long unofficial blockade by Saudi Arabia that has reduced trade between the regional rivals to record lows, according to exporters and traders.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"DUBAI/ISTANBUL (Reuters) -Some Turkish exporters are re-routing food, clothing and other goods to circumvent a months-long unofficial blockade by Saudi Arabia that has reduced trade between the regional rivals to record lows, according to exporters and traders."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Production in nearby countries allows exporters to obtain customs documents and ditch “Made in Turkey” product tags, allowing goods to enter Saudi Arabia, exporters, traders and a diplomat told Reuters."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Riyadh has never publicly acknowledged the boycott against Turkey, but last year top Saudi businessmen endorsed it as a response to what they called hostility coming from Ankara, particularly since the 2018 murder of Saudi journalist Jamal Khashoggi inside the Saudi consulate in Istanbul."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Turkey raised the boycott issue this week at a World Trade Organisation Goods Council meeting in Geneva, at which Saudi Arabia’s “restrictive policies and practices concerning Turkey” was discussed and Riyadh responded, the WTO’s website said. Ankara’s move could help bring about a settlement."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"A review of official trade data shows that in the first quarter of the year Turkish exports to the kingdom plunged 93% on an annual basis to $56 million. [nS8N2K800R]"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Exports of food, electronics, garments, jewellery and automotive goods were all down more than 90% from a year earlier, according to the Turkish Exports Assembly."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“A black market is now emerging where brokers take the Turkish goods to other ports and forge the documents so they appear to be coming from China or Europe for fees,” said one importer of building materials to Saudi Arabia, who requested anonymity."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Trade data also shows unusual parallel jumps of 200% to 400% in Turkish garments, textiles, chemicals and jewellery arriving in Oman and Lebanon."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Some companies who rely on Saudi Arabia as a main client re-routed their production lines in order to continue to be able to sell,” another trade company official told Reuters."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Seref Fayat, head of Turkey’s TOBB clothing and garment council, said manufacturers were considering sending fabrics the other way, to Bulgaria or Serbia, for “finishing touches” on Saudi-bound goods."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In so doing, Turkish companies could honour contracts with retail brands which commit them to global deliveries, including to the kingdom, he said. “Exporters are trying to overcome the blockade, but this means additional costs out of their pocket.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The data published on Thursday showed Turkish exports to Bulgaria and Serbia were up 58% and 44% respectively in March, compared to a 38% rise to all test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"DUBAI (Reuters) -Yemen’s Houthi forces said they attacked important targets in the Saudi Arabian capital Riyadh using four drones on Thursday, though there was no confirmation from the Saudi authorities or independent reports of any such strikes."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said it had destroyed a missile before it took off in Yemen, according to a report on Saudi state TV. test_endpoint.articlesName: Tunisia to offer oil licences, denies Shell plans exit
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Tunisia's Energy Ministry said on Thursday it would offer four exploration licences this year and denied that Royal Dutch Shell aimed to leave the country.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"TUNIS Tunisia’s Energy Ministry said on Thursday it would offer four exploration licences this year and denied that Royal Dutch Shell aimed to leave the country."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Senior ministry official Rania Marzouki said the new licences would bring $80 million of investment and bolster production, which she put at 3.4 million tonnes of oil equivalent last year, half what it was in 2010."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Industry sources last week told Reuters that Shell had hired investment bank Rothschild \u0026amp; Co. to sell its Tunisian assets, while Italy’s Eni had hired Lazard to run its own sale and Austria’s OMV also planned to sell up."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Shell informed us that it has no intention to leave the country and to sell its assets,” the ministry’s energy director Rached Ben Dali said at a news conference alongside Marzouki."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"He said Eni’s sale was prompted by the company’s strategy of leaving countries with low production, not by any frustration at Tunisia’s regulatory or political environment."}]

test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"TUNIS Tunisia’s Energy Ministry said on Thursday it would offer four exploration licences this year and denied that Royal Dutch Shell aimed to leave the country."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Senior ministry official Rania Marzouki said the new licences would bring $80 million of investment and bolster production, which she put at 3.4 million tonnes of oil equivalent last year, half what it was in 2010."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Industry sources last week told Reuters that Shell had hired investment bank Rothschild \u0026amp; Co. to sell its Tunisian assets, while Italy’s Eni had hired Lazard to run its own sale and Austria’s OMV also planned to sell up."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Shell informed us that it has no intention to leave the country and to sell its assets,” the ministry’s energy director Rached Ben Dali said at a news conference alongside Marzouki."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"He said Eni’s sale was prompted by the company’s strategy of leaving countries with low production, not by any frustration at Tunisia’s regulatory or political environment."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Qatar's economy shrinks 3.9% in fourth quarter of 2020
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Qatar's economy contracted by 3.9% in the fourth quarter of 2020, government data showed, with transportation and storage activity plummeting 32.8% and construction down nearly 5%.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"DUBAI Qatar’s economy contracted by 3.9% in the fourth quarter of 2020, government data showed, with transportation and storage activity plummeting 32.8% and construction down nearly 5%."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Gross domestic product, based on constant prices, also fell on a quarterly basis, decreasing by 0.5% in the fourth quarter, the Planning and Statistics Authority said in a statement."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"GDP shrank 4.5% in the third quarter on annual basis but grew 5.6% compared to the previous three months."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In December, the International Monetary Fund projected Qatar’s GDP contraction in 2020 at 2.5%. It projected a rebound to growth of 2.7% in 2021."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Lebanon's central bank says it will discuss forensic audit with Alvarez & Marsal on April 6
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Lebanon's central bank is ready to facilitate a forensic audit process by Alvarez & Marsal and will discuss this in a virtual meeting with the restructuring company on April 6, it said in a statement on Thursday.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"DUBAI (Reuters) -Lebanon’s central bank is ready to facilitate a forensic audit process by Alvarez \u0026amp; Marsal and will discuss this in a virtual meeting with the restructuring company on April 6, it said in a statement on Thursday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Alvarez \u0026amp; Marsal pulled out of the audit procedure in November, saying it had not received the information it required, prompting parliament in December to lift banking secrecy for one year."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The audit is on a list of reforms that foreign donors have demanded before helping Lebanon out of its grave financial crisis, rooted in decades of state waste and corruption."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Asia's factory recovery picks up but cost pressures grow
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Asia's factories stepped up production in March as a solid recovery in global demand helped manufacturers move past the setbacks of the pandemic, although rising costs are creating new challenges for businesses.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"TOKYO (Reuters) -Asia’s factories stepped up production in March as a solid recovery in global demand helped manufacturers move past the setbacks of the pandemic, although rising costs are creating new challenges for businesses."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"A series of upbeat factory surveys released on Thursday reinforce market optimism that vaccine rollouts, as well as strong growth in global powerhouses like the United States and China, will help economies emerge from their sharp downturns of 2020."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Japan and South Korea saw factory activity expand in March thanks to solid demand at home and abroad, purchasing manager indexes’ (PMI) showed, offering relief to policymakers facing pressure to speed up a patchy recovery."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“South Korean manufacturers continued to signal strong optimism as the rollout of COVID-19 vaccinations began and demand for new products accelerated,” said Usamah Bhatti, economist at IHS Markit."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"China’s factory activity in March expanded at the slowest pace in almost a year, though underlying economic conditions remained positive."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Caixin/Markit Manufacturing PMI, which focuses on smaller firms, dropped to 50.6 in March from February’s 50.9, missing market expectations."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The private-sector survey came after the official manufacturing PMI on Wednesday, which showed Chinese factories cranking up production after a brief lull during the Lunar New Year holiday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Activity in big, export-reliant economies stayed brisk."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The final au Jibun Bank Japan PMI rose to a seasonally adjusted 52.7 in March from the previous month’s 51.4 reading, marking the fastest expansion since October 2018."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"South Korea’s PMI stood at 55.3 in March, with activity expanding for a sixth straight month."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Manufacturing activity also accelerated in Taiwan, Vietnam and Indonesia, the March PMI surveys showed. Malaysian activity continued to decline but at a slower pace."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"There were some signs rising prices were straining firms, however, clouding the outlook for Asian economies."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Although supply chain disruption related to previous COVID-19 outbreaks eased, China’s Caixin survey showed factories reporting a sharp increase in input costs."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Input prices continue to outpace output prices, suggesting there may be some risk to profit margins,” said Erin Xin, China economist at HSBC."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Should there be significant compression in profit margins, this could dampen firms’ capex spending in the coming quarters.”"},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Some analysts also warned that lockdowns in Europe and supply constraints, such as chip shortages that are disrupting automobile production, could weigh on factory activity in countries like Taiwan and South Korea."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“All the uncertainty really rests with the economies they’re exporting to,” said Rob Carnell, Asia-Pacific chief economist at ING in Singapore. “There’s certainly a little bit of downside risk.”"}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: South Africa's Absa PMI expands again in March
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: South Africa's seasonally-adjusted Absa Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) expanded for third month in a row in March as new sales and exports rose with the easing of coronavirus lockdown restrictions, a survey showed on Thursday.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"JOHANNESBURG South Africa’s seasonally-adjusted Absa Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) expanded for third month in a row in March as new sales and exports rose with the easing of coronavirus lockdown restrictions, a survey showed on Thursday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The index, a gauge of manufacturing activity in Africa’s most industrialised economy, rose to 57.4 points in March from 53.0 points in February."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The survey showed a broad-based improvement, with all of five subcomponents in survey improving, with only the employment sub-index remaining below the 50-point mark that separates expansion from contraction."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The jump in new sales order was mainly driven by strong exports, the survey said, reflecting “the recent better-than-expected manufacturing PMI readings in Europe”, according to Absa."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"South Africa’s trade surplus widened to 28.96 billion rand ($1.96 billion) in February, more than double the surplus in the previous month, extending a trend that began in May last year."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Business activity recorded another sharp increase, up 8.6 points, but Absa questioned whether this would be sustained."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Purchasing managers turned slightly less optimistic about expected business conditions in six months’ time,” Absa said in the release."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The country has seen a sustained drop in the rate of new COVID-19 infections in 2021, leading to a loosening of lockdown restrictions that has supported economic activity, particularly in consumer sectors."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Restrictions have however been temporarily tightened for the upcoming Easter weekend. The slow pace of the rollout of coronavirus vaccines, with the country only expected to achieve herd immunity in 2022, has dampened business sentiment."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Turkish manufacturing activity expands in March -PMI
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Turkish factory activity grew in March as new orders began to improve, a survey showed on Thursday, while growth in output and employment continued in the manufacturing sector.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"ISTANBUL Turkish factory activity grew in March as new orders began to improve, a survey showed on Thursday, while growth in output and employment continued in the manufacturing sector."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The headline index reading rose to 52.6 in March from 51.7 a month earlier, data from the Istanbul Chamber of Industry and IHS Markit showed, staying above the 50.0 mark that denotes growth."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Higher new orders and the addition of new production lines supported an increase in output, the panel said, although raw material supply shortages prevented a stronger pace of increase."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Suppliers’ delivery times lengthened and supply shortages added to inflationary pressures as well as weakness in the Turkish lira at the end of the first quarter, the panel said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The sharp acceleration in input and output price inflation was mainly due to raw material issues and exchange rate fluctuations, it said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Firms continued to hire more staff with investment, new production lines and higher output requirements all mentioned as factors supporting job creation, it added."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“The Turkish manufacturing sector managed to secure renewed increases in new orders and expand both output and employment again in March, despite facing some substantial headwinds,” said Andrew Harker, Economics Director at IHS Markit."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Firms will be hoping that some of these headwinds start to ease in the months to come so that growth in the sector can start to build momentum.”"}]

test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"ISTANBUL Turkish factory activity grew in March as new orders began to improve, a survey showed on Thursday, while growth in output and employment continued in the manufacturing sector."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The headline index reading rose to 52.6 in March from 51.7 a month earlier, data from the Istanbul Chamber of Industry and IHS Markit showed, staying above the 50.0 mark that denotes growth."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Higher new orders and the addition of new production lines supported an increase in output, the panel said, although raw material supply shortages prevented a stronger pace of increase."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Suppliers’ delivery times lengthened and supply shortages added to inflationary pressures as well as weakness in the Turkish lira at the end of the first quarter, the panel said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The sharp acceleration in input and output price inflation was mainly due to raw material issues and exchange rate fluctuations, it said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Firms continued to hire more staff with investment, new production lines and higher output requirements all mentioned as factors supporting job creation, it added."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“The Turkish manufacturing sector managed to secure renewed increases in new orders and expand both output and employment again in March, despite facing some substantial headwinds,” said Andrew Harker, Economics Director at IHS Markit."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Firms will be hoping that some of these headwinds start to ease in the months to come so that growth in the sector can start to build momentum.”"}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: U.N. Security Council concerned over election impasse in Somalia -U.S. envoy
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: The United Nations Security Council on Wednesday expressed concern over a standoff in Somalia on holding new elections, the United States' top U.N. diplomat said.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"The United Nations Security Council on Wednesday expressed concern over a standoff in Somalia on holding new elections, the United States’ top U.N. diplomat said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"President Mohamed Abdullahi Mohamed’s four-year term ended last month without a successor and Somalia’s parliament was supposed to elect a new president on Feb. 8, but the exercise was delayed because new lawmakers have yet to be picked."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"U.S. Ambassador Linda Thomas-Greenfield said in a virtual press briefing following a closed-door session that the 15-member Security Council “noted ongoing efforts to find agreement between leaders of the federal government of Somalia and the federal member states” on implementing a revised electoral model."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“They expressed concern over the ongoing impasse and called for Somalia’s leaders to engage in a constructive dialogue at the earliest opportunity without precondition to resolve outstanding issues,” she said."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: Suspected Islamists kill 23 civilians in eastern Congo
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: Suspected Islamist militants killed at least 23 civilians in an overnight raid on a village near Beni in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, the provincial governor's office said on Wednesday.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"BENI, Democratic Republic of Congo Suspected Islamist militants killed at least 23 civilians in an overnight raid on a village near Beni in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, the provincial governor’s office said on Wednesday."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The death toll was still provisional as the search for bodies continued in Manyama-Moliso, north of the city of Beni, the North Kivu governor’s office said on Twitter."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"It blamed the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF), a Ugandan militia active in eastern Congo since the 1990s. The authorities have blamed the ADF for the deaths of hundreds of people since 2014."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The group has stepped up reprisals against civilians since Congo’s army launched a fresh offensive in late 2019."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The United States designated the ADF a foreign terrorist organisation earlier this month, accusing it of links to Islamic State. U.N. experts in Congo, however, have not found evidence of a direct relationship between the two groups."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Two of the assailants were also killed when the army responded, the governor’s office added."}]

test_endpoint.articlesName: South Africa's NUM union seeks 15% wage hike from gold miners and Eskom
test_endpoint.articlesShortDescription: South Africa's National Union of Mineworkers (NUM) said on Wednesday it planned to seek a hike of at least 15% in a three-year wage deal at upcoming negotiations with gold miners and state utility Eskom.
test_endpoint.articlesDescription: [{"type":"paragraph","content":"JOHANNESBURG South Africa’s National Union of Mineworkers (NUM) said on Wednesday it planned to seek a hike of at least 15% in a three-year wage deal at upcoming negotiations with gold miners and state utility Eskom."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"NUM said it would consolidate the wage demands from all sectors it operates in, and would seek increases of between 15% to 20%, or 15,000 rand ($1,016) minimum, alongside other demands including medical aid contributions and COVID-19 health and safety leave."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Higher gold prices, which reached a record in August last year, boosted 2020 earnings and offered mining companies a lifeline following production disruptions because of the COVID-19 pandemic."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"“Given the good dividend performances by mining companies NUM enters this season of negotiations in high spirit for a good settlement,” NUM said."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Gold producers have in the past argued that above-inflation wage hikes cannot be sustained unless prices also rise."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"They say higher wages could also add to already high costs in an industry the has the world’s deepest mines."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Unions argue wages remain too low, a legacy of the apartheid era when the Black mining labour force was ruthlessly exploited."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The demands far exceed the current inflation rate of 2.9%, raising the prospect of tough negotiations with companies, including Sibanye Stillwater, Harmony Gold, and smaller producer Village Main Reef."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"A double-digit wage increase is likely to pile further pressure on Eskom, which is choking under a mountain of debt, and regularly implements scheduled power cuts because of repeated faults at its ailing coal-fired power station fleet."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Eskom’s spokesman declined to comment on the demands."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Sibanye Stillwater’s spokesman said they would address demands during the wage talks."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Harmony Gold and Village Main Reef could not immediately be reached for comment."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Negotiations with Eskom are expected to begin on April 20, while an exact date has not yet been set for the start of talks with gold miners."},{"type":"paragraph","content":"($1 = 14.7700 rand)"}]

files.filesDescription: Miners work deep underground at Sibanye Gold's Masimthembe shaft in Westonaria, South Africa, April 3, 2017. Mike Hutchings
